subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following pairs (School of Thought – Proponent) is correctly matched?
explanation: The correct match is as follows :- School of Thought Proponent Vaisheshika - Kanada Uttara Mimansa - Badarayana Mimansa - Jaimini Nyaya - Gautama Yoga - Patanjali Sankhya - Kapila
source: UPPCS (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.1

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to the Puranas, which of the following statements is/are correct? (1) Vishnu Purana is considered more reliable for the history of Mauryans. (2) Matsya Purana is considered more reliable for the history of Andhras. Select the correct answer using the code given below-
explanation: Information about the Mauryan dynasty is found in the Vishnu Puran and the history of Andhras is found in Matsya Purana.
source: UPPSC (J) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.1

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following is NOT a Vedanga?
options: Virakta – Philosophy Ancient History 9 tory of India es of Ancient Indian History
explanation: Vedangas are six auxiliary disciplines associated with the study and understanding of the Vedas. These are Shiksha Kalpa, Vyakaran, Nirukts (hhanda, jyotisha). Hence, Virakta philosophy is not a type of Vedanga.
source: Mizoram PSC (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.1

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following Veda is partly prose work?
explanation: The Atharveda is fourth Veda, it comprises charms & magic spells. It is written in party in prose and partly in poetry.
source: Sikkim PSC (Pre) 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.1

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which statements regarding Periplus of the Erythraean Sea are true? (i) The text was written in Greek for traders involved in mercantile activities. (ii) The text survives in the form of 10th century manuscript. (iii) The manuscript has errors and omission. (iv) It is a work of multiple authors. Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
explanation: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, written in Koine Greek that describes navigation and trading opportunities. The writer of Periplus of Erythraean sea is a unknown Greek writer. The book was originally known only through a single manuscript dating from 14th and 15th century, this manuscript proved to be a corrupt and error ridden copy of a 10th century. Hence, option (c) is correct answer.
source: Assam PSC (Pre) 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.1

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements about Vedic literature : (i) Vedic literature is broadly divide into two parts : Shruti and Smriti. (ii) The language used in four Vedas is classical Sanskrit. (iii) The Ramayana and the Mahabharata are two major important components of Vedic literature.
explanation: Vedic literature is broadly devided into Shruti and Smriti. Shruti which means "to hear" it describes the secred texts comprising Vedas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas and upnishads. While Smriti literally means that which is remembered and it is entire body of post Vedic Classical Sanskrit literature. It comprises Vedanga, Shad darsana, Puranas, Itihasa, Upveda, Tantras, Agamas, Upangs. The language of 4 Vedas is classical Sanskrit or Vedic Sanskrit. The Ramayana and Mahabharta are two major important components of Vedic literature.
source: Assam PSC (Pre) 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.1

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following wrote the Aihole inscription?
explanation: The Aihole inscription is a Sanskrit inscription in Aihole Karnataka. It was composed by the Jain poet Ravikirti in honor of his patron king Pulakesin II of Badami Chalukya dynasty.
source: UPPSC APO 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.2

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Where is the word ‘Stupa’ first found?
explanation: The word ‘Stupa’ was first found in Rig- Veda. The word stupa has been derived from Sanskrit and pali language which stands for 'heap'. It is a round (hemispherical) shaped structure associated with Buddhism where the sacred remains of Buddha are kept.
source: Chhattisgarh PCS (Pre)G.S. 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.2

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Manu Smriti is basically related to:
explanation: The Manusmriti or laws of Manu is an ancient legal text among the many Dharmsastras of Hinduism. Manusmriti (laws of Manu) is considered by Some Hindus to be the law laid down for Hindus. It was one of the first Sanskrit texts to be translated into English in 1794 by Sir William Jones.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S.2007 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.2

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What is "Prajnaparamita"?
explanation: Prajnaparamita is a Sanskrit word that means “perfection of wisdom.” In the Mahayana Buddhist tradition, Prajnaparamita is a central concept as well as a body of sutras, or religious teachings presented in the form of short statements. Ancient History 1 B. Archaelogical Sources
source: GUJARAT PSC CIVIL PRE-PAPER-I (21-3-2021) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.2

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to the Indian History, Alexander Rea. A.H. Longhurst, Robert Sewell, James Burgess and Walter Elliot were associated with :
options: establishment of English Press in Colonial India
establishment of Churches in Princely States
construction of railways in Colonial India
explanation: Alexander Rea, All Longhurst, Robert Sewell, James Burgess and Walter Elliot all were associated with archaeological excavations. Alexander Rea is known for unearthing a sacrophagus from the hillocks of Pallavarnam in Tamil Nadu. A.H. Longhurst was in charge of the systematic digging of Nagarjunakonda. Robert Sewell and Water Elliot was associated with their archacological work at Buddhist Stupa at Amarvati. James Burgess was the Director General Archaeological Survey of India.
source: UPSC IAS (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.2

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements are correct? (1) The ceramics similar to the Anarta tradition was first reported from Surkotada. (2) The Anarta tradition or Anarta ware is a chalcolithic culture. (3) The Anarta ware found from Banaskantha and Sabarkantha districts of Gujarat.
explanation: The ceramics similar to the Anarta tradition was first reported from Surkotada with Classical Harappan ceramics. Hence statement 1 is true. The Anarta tradition or Anarta ware is a chalcolithic culture tentatively dated between 3950 BCE to 1900 BCE based on radio carbon dates from Loteshwar and Gola Dhoro. The sites associated with it are located in Gujarat, India. Hence statement 2 is true but statement 3 is false.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-26.12.21 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.2

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Bhimbetka was discovered by
explanation: The area of Bhimbetka is located in Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh which is famous for 760 caves and rock shelters. This place is located about 45 km. south of Bhopal. Evidence of antiquity and contemporary painting of middle stone culture have been found in most areas of Bhimbetka. These paintings are pre-historic rock paintings. This Bhimbetka cave was discovered by Dr. Vishnu Shridhar Wakankar in 1957. The shelters were designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003.
source: MPPCS (Pre.) 2020 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.2

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Where are the prehistoric rock painting found in Madhya Pradesh?
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 1993 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.3

subject: AP & Indian History
question: From which rock cave of India most paintings are found?
explanation: From Bhimbetka Rock Cave (Madhya Pradesh) most paintings are found. The paintings found at Bhimbetka Rock Cave are said to be the oldest form of human expression. Most of these are done in red and white on the cave walls. The oldest of the cave paintings in Bhimbetka is believed to be about 12,000 years ago. Out of the 760 rock shelters, 500 are adorned with paintings.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2008 Uttarakhand UDA/LDA (M) 2007 MPPSC (Pre) Spl. G.S. 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.3

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Robert Bruce Foote, who discovered the first archaeological equipment in India, was a:
explanation: Robert Bruce Foote was a Primarily a Geologist (also an archaeologist) who discovered India’s first paleolithic stone tool, hand-axe in 1863 from a place called Pallavaram near Madras (now Chennai). He is regarded as the Father of South Indian Geology, while archaeologists regard him as the Father of Indian Prehistory.
source: UP Lower (Pre) 2015 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.3

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who is considered as the father of Indian Archaeology?
explanation: Alexander Cunningham is called the “Father of Indian Archaeology”. He was the first Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. Ist 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.3

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following sites provides evidence of domestication of animals in the Mesolithic period?
explanation: The earliest evidence of domestication of animals has been found in Adamgarh of Madhya Pradesh and Bagor of Rajasthan. Some sites of earliest cultivation of plants around 7000-6000 BCE is suggested in Jaipur district of Rajasthan from study of deposit of Sambhar lake. Ancient History
source: UPPCS (Pre)-2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.3

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Arrange in correct chronological order- 1. Patpara sedimentation 2. Khetaunhi sedimentation 3. Bagor sedimentation 4. Sihawal sedimentation Codes:
explanation: The Middle Son valley, in Madhya Pradesh, preserves extensive alluvial sediments from the Quaternary period which contain a record that is both rich in archaeology and faunal remains. Four Quaternary sedimentation characterize the geological deposits of the Middle Son valley. In chronological order, these are as Sihawal, Patpara, Bagor and Khetaunahi sedimentation.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S.-Ist 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.3

subject: AP & Indian History
question: As per excavation evidences cattle breeding started in-
explanation: As per excavation evidences cattle breeding started in Mesolithic age. On the basis of archaeological discoveries, the beginning of the Mesolithic Age in Indian subcontinent is dated to around 10,000 BC to 8,000 BC.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S.-2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.3

subject: AP & Indian History
question: From where remains of trough residence, of Neolithic age, are found? 1. Burzahom 2. Gufkral 3. Kuchai 4. Mehrgarh Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
explanation: In Neolithic period the man's life changed due to some major achievements like the beginning of agriculture, the invention of wheel and making of pottery. At Burzahom and Gufkral in Kashmir pit houses have been found dug into the ground with steps leading into them. Therefore these evidence throw light on the remains of trough residence of Neolithic Age.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. Ist 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.3

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Dogs were cremated in human burials at
explanation: The example of burial in Burzahom, a Neolithic cultural site in Jammu and Kashmir , shows that the practice of burying humans as well as their domesticated dogs were prevalent. The remains of Pit dwelling have been found from the excavation of the Burzahom. The archaeological site of Burzahom was discovered in 1935 by De Terra and Paterson.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) 2009-10 UP Lower (Pre) 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.4

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The most ancient evidence of Systematic farming in India is found from which place?
explanation: The first clear evidence of agriculture was found from a site called Mehrgarh (Balochistan, Pakistan). In the context of around 7000 BCE evidences of various varieties of agricultural crops of wheat and barley have been found from here. The cultural relics from stone culture to Harappan civilization have been found from Mehrgarh.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. Ist 2010, 2007 UP Lower (Pre) 2004, 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.4

subject: AP & Indian History
question: At which of the following places in the northwestern region of the Indian sub continent in the Neolithic Age has the earliest evidence of the emergence of agriculture been found?
source: Chhattisgarh PCS (Pre) 2017-18 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.4

subject: AP & Indian History
question: From which one of the following archaeological site, the Cultural remains from Stone age culture to Harappan civilization are found?
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.4

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Name the site from where the evidence of ancient most permanent settlement of life is found?
explanation: Mehrgarh, near the Bolan pass in Baluchistan province of Pakistan, was the first place in the Indian subcontinent where the early man learnt to grow barley and wheat and domesticate sheeps and goats. Burials sites have also been found at Mehrgarh indicating a belief in the life after death. This site is the earliest evidence of human settlement that dates back to 7000 BC. The houses were made of mud and mud-bricks. Bones of animals (goat) and charred grains have also been found along with terracota figurines decorated with ornaments. Ancient History
source: UPPCS (Mains) Spl. G.S. Ist 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.4

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In reference to the Mesolithic period, the place from where the evidence of animal husbandry is found?
explanation: In Mesolithic period the livelihood of people were hunting, fishing and animal husbandry. Adamgarh in Madhya Pradesh and Bagor in Rajasthan provide the oldest proof of animal husbandry. This time was around 5000 BC. The deposits in Sambhar salt lake in Rajasthan give an indication that planting was in practice around 7000-6000 BC.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.4

subject: AP & Indian History
question: From where, the ancient most evidence of paddy cultivation in Ganga valley is found?
explanation: The most ancient evidence of paddy cultivation in Ganga valley has been found from Lahuradewa district of Sant Kabir Nagar. The evidence of rice has been found of 7000 BC to 6000 BC from here.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.4

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The ancient most evidence of paddy cultivation in Indian sub-Continent is found from:
explanation: Koldihwa (in Belan Valley) and Mahagara (South of Prayagraj) in Vindhya region are the most ancient evidence of paddy cultivation in the world. The excavation at Koldihwa has revealed evidence of three cultural phases, Neolithic, Chalcolithic and Iron age. Plentiful evidence of rice has been found from the excavations of Koldihwa and Mahagara in loose form as well as embedded in Potsherds.
source: UPUDA/LDA Spl. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.4

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The ancient most evidence of the practice of iron metal is found from the excavation of which site of India?
explanation: Atranjikhera excavation has yielded some iron tools. Scholars have dated its time to the first millennium BC. This proves that iron tools started being used in Northern India from 1000 BC, it was considered to be the oldest evidence yet. It is known that recent excavations and NCERT sources have acknowledged the use of iron in fifteen hundred BC.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1998 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.4

subject: AP & Indian History
question: From the contents of the Copenhagen Museum a triangular division of the stone, Bronze and Iron Age was done by:
explanation: Danish archaeologist Christian Jurgensen Thomsen divided the contents of the Copenhagen Museum into a triangular division of the Stone, Bronze and Iron Age.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.4

subject: AP & Indian History
question: From where the earliest evidence of human being in India is found?
explanation: The first evidence of human beings in India was found at a place called Hathnora on the banks of river Narmada in Hoshangabad district of Madhya Pradesh. Human skull fossils have been found from here. It is placed under the category of Homo erectus, preceding Homo sapiens, the modern species.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) 2006-07 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.5

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Archaeological site Sanghol is located in:
explanation: Sanghol is a historical site located in the Fatehgarh Sahib district of Punjab. It was discovered by S.S. Talwar and R.S. Bisht. Important historical evidences from post-Harappan era to post Mauryan era have been found from here. Mixed coins have been received from the Kushanas and semi-tribal people including Hind-Pahlavas, Vima Kadphises. It appears that there was also a mint in Sanghol.
source: UPPSC Asst. Forest Conservator Exam 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.5

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the followings cast light on Indus valley civilization?
explanation: The only source about Harappan civilization is archaeological remains found from the excavation. Though the 400 pictorial signs of Harappan script have been recognized but unfortunately it cannot be deciphered till now.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1993 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.5

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The main source of knowledge about Harappan civilization is:
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1996 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.5

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Findings from the recent excavations at Harappan site Sanauli:
explanation: ‘Sanauli’ is a Harappan site located in the western Uttar Pradesh. The major remains found from the excavation recently revealed the three big chariots of copper age (Pre-iron age) about 2000 BC, cremation of human body. A royal burial found from the site in which a chariot, sword and other things were kept inside.
source: UP Lower (Pre) 2004 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.5

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer from the codes given below the lists: List-I List-II A. Harappa 1. N.G. Majumdar B. Hastinapur 2. John Marshall C. Takshashila 3. Daya Ram Sahani D. Kaushambi 4. B. B. Lal Codes : A B C D A B C D
explanation: The correct match is as follows :- List-I List II Harappa – Daya Ram Sahani Hastinapur – B.B. Lal Takshashila – John Marshall Kaushambi – N.G. Majumdar
source: UPPSC RO/ARO Mains 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.5

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who of the following had first deciphered the edicts of Emperor Ashoka?
explanation: Firstly in 1838 ,James Prinsep succeeded in deciphering the state orders of Emperor Ashoka in Brahmi script. These inscriptions on the rocks and pillars depicted the reforms and policies of Ashoka. It is notable that the inscriptions of Ashoka was first discovered by T. Panthelor in 1750 and the first inscription which was discovered in Delhi-Meerut Inscription.
source: IAS (Pre) GS Ist Paper, 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.5

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who deciphered Brahmi script at first?
source: UPPCS (Main) Spl. G.S. Ist 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.5

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Ashoka inscriptions were first deciphered by:
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1993 BPSC (Pre) 2007-08 UPPCS (Main) G.S. Ist 2006 Chhattishgarh PSC (Pre) G.S., 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.5

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Paleolith 1. Match list-I with list-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists : List-I List-II (Archaeological site) (Present location) A. Nevasa 1. Rajasthan B. Isampur 2. Tamil Nadu C. Didwana 3. Maharashtra D. Gudiyam cave 4. Karnataka Code : A B C D A B C D
explanation: The correct match is as follows :- Archaeological sites Present location Nevasa – Maharashtra Isampur – Karnataka Didwana – Rajasthan Gudiyam cave – Tamil Nadu
source: UPPCS (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.6

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Correctly match the following : (I) (II) A. Paleolithic Age 1. Bhimbetka Caves B. Mesolithic Age 2. Burzahom C. Neolithic Age 3. Banas Valley D. Chalcolithic 4 Sohan/Soan River Age Valley Code : A B C D A B C D
explanation: The correct match is as follows- List-I List-II A. Paleolithic Age - Sohan/Soan River Valley B. Mesolithic Age - Bhimbetka Caves C. Neolithic Age - Burzahom D. Chalcolithic Age - Banas Valley
source: CGPSC Pre 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.6

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Match the list-I with list-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below the list : List-I List-II A. Harappa 1. Godavari B. Hastinapur 2. Ravi C. Nagarjunakonda 3. Ganga D. Paithan 4. Krishna Codes: A B C D A B C D
explanation: The correct match is as follows :- List I List II Harappa - Ravi Hastinapur - Ganga Nagarjunakonda - Krishna Paithan - Godavari A. Paleolithic Period
source: UPPCS (Mains) Spl. G.s. I Paper 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.6

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Human figurines found in Lakhudiyar near Almora depicted in red colour, are of which period? Ancient History 1 hic Culture of India
explanation: The famous rock cut cave site in Uttarakhand, Lakhudiyar is famous for its depiction of human works and animals. Lakhudiyar is located on the banks of the Suyal River in Almora. The figurines of this very place depicts the life of the early man during the time of stone age.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) 2009-10 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.6

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Given below are two statements, one is labeled as Assertion (A) and other as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The Stone Age people of the Vindhyas migrated to the Ganga Valley in terminal Pleistocene period. Reason (R): Due to climatic change, it was dry phase in this period. Choose the correct answer from the code given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: The Stone Age people of the Vindhya region migrated to the Ganga Valley in terminal Pleistocene period because there was a phase of dryness in this period of time due to climate change while the Ganga plain was full of grassland and water. Hence Assertion (A) and Reason (R) both are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). B. Mesolithic Period
source: UPPCS RO-ARO (Mains) 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.6

subject: AP & Indian History
question: One of the largest and most spectacular rock shelters is located in the Vindhya hills, full of Paleolithic and Mesolithic remains. It consists of the richest paintings of daily life events from hunting, dancing, and music to animal fighting, honey collection etc. Which of the following site is referred to above?
explanation: The Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka are in the Foothills of the Vindhya Mountains on the Southern Edge of the Central Indian Plateu. These caves are full of Paleolithic and Mesolithic remains.
source: JKPSC (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.6

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following is a large Mesolithic site in Rajasthan?
explanation: Bagor in Rajasthan in the largest Mesolithic hebitation site in India. It is on the left bank of the Kothari River, which is a tributary of Banas River. It is the only site to have been excavated horizontally.
source: Maharashtra PSC (Pre) 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.6

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Arrange the following Mesolithic sites geographically in order from west to east- 1. Paisra 2. Lekhahia 3. Birbhanpur 4. Mahadaha Select the correct answer from the code given below Codes:
explanation: Geographical order from west to east of the Mesolithic sites is Mahadaha (Pratapgarh in Uttar Pradesh), Lekhahia (Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh), Paisra (Bihar) and Birbhanpur (West Bengal).
source: UPPSC RO/ARO Mains 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.6

subject: AP & Indian History
question: From which of the following site of middle stone age bone made ornaments are found?
explanation: The Vindhyas of Uttar Pradesh and the upper and middle Ganges Valley region are extremely rich for Microlith tools. Mahdaha, Sarai Nahar Rai and Damdama are important sites. Tools and ornaments made of horn are found from Mahdaha in greater numbers than Sarai Nahar Rai in Pratapgarh U.P.
source: UPPCS (Mains) I Paper 2010 UP RO/ARO (M) 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.7

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Three human Skeletons from the same grave is found from:
explanation: The Middle Paleolithic place called Damdama is located in Pratapgarh district of Uttar Pradesh. As a result of excavation carried here from 1982 to 1987, 41 human burials have been found out of which single burials in 35 graves, two human burials in 5 graves and 3 human skeletons in one grave have been found simultaneously. A grave of 4 human skeletons buried together has been found at Sarai Nahar Rai.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G. S. 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.7

subject: AP & Indian History
question: From which rock formation of the Vindhya region most of the human skeletons are found?
explanation: Out of the middle Mesolithic sites in the Vindhyan region 17 human skeletons have been found from a rock shelter named Lekhahiya located in Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh. C. Neolithic Period
source: UPPCS (Pre) G. S. 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.7

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The cultivation of food grains started in -
explanation: The Neolithic Age, also known as New Stone Age, was the last and third part of the Stone Age. In India, it spanned from around 8,000 B.C. to 3,000 B.C. The Neolithic Age was mainly characterized by the development of settled agriculture and the use of tools and weapons made of polished stones. The major crops grown during this period were ragi, horse gram, cotton, rice, wheat, and barley. Pottery first appeared in this age.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. I , 2005 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.7

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Large stone monuments have been identified as:
options: A place for the burial of the dead
explanation: The large stone monuments have been found from south India which has been identified as the burials of the dead. These tombs were surrounded by large stone pieces. Not only the bones but also the pottery and terracotta items have been obtained from these tombs which indicate their religious beliefs.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. I , 2005 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.7

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Mound of ash is related to which Neolithic site?
explanation: A mound of ash is found from a Neolithic site called Sanganakallu located in Bellary district near Mysore in Karnataka. Scholars speculate that the dung of Ancient History 1 animals were gathered and was set on fire, making it a mound. Other Neolithic sites which show the evidence of mound of ash are Utnur, Kodekal and Kappagallu.
source: UPPCS (Mains) GS I 2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.7

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The grain used by human beings at first was :
explanation: The first grain used by the early humans was barley. Barley was also the first cereal to be domesticated by the early humans. Barley and Wheat were so called the Neolithic founder crops in the development of agriculture. D. Chalcolithic Period
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1997 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.7

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Research was done at ______ with reference to the Middle Age and Copper Age in terms of human settlement in Maharashtra.
explanation: The study of Mesolithic and Chalcolithic periods in Maharashtra has been done in terms of human settlements found at Patna Hathakhamba and Inamgaon.
source: MH PSC (Pre) 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.7

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following is also called Chalcolithic age?
explanation: The period in which human used stone and copper tools together was called copper stone period/ Chalcolithic age. The remains of the first depicted pottery were found during the Chalcolithic age. Metals such as copper and its alloy were used to make knives, axes, fishing hooks, chisels, pins and rods.
source: BPSC (Pre.) 2000-01 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.7

subject: AP & Indian History
question: How the people of Maharashtra were cremating the dead bodies under the floor, in Chalcolithic era?
explanation: In Maharashtra the dead bodies were buried under their house floor in North to South direction along with pots and copper objects, whereas in South India the direction of burial was east to west. In Eastern India fractional burial was practiced.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1997 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.7

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who excavated Navdatoli?
explanation: Navdatoli is situated on the southern bank of river Narmada in Khargone district of Madhya Pradesh. This place was excavated under the leadership of H.D. Sankalia between 1957-59 AD.
source: UP Lower (Pre) Spl. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.7

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In which state Navdatoli is located?
source: UPPCS (Mains) I G. S. 2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.7

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Garric Pottery (OCP) was named in:
explanation: Distinct pottery was obtained from Hastinapur and Ataranjikheda of Ganga-Yamuna doab called Garric pottery (ochre coloured pottery) and due to which these sites are referred to as Garric pottery culture. This culture is also associated with the Ganga Valley copper hoards.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G. S. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.7

question: Which of the following statements are correct regarding Indus Valley Civilization? (I) Mohenjodaro is on the right bank of the Indus River in Larkana District of Sind. (II) Lothal is situated on the Sabarmati River at the head of the Gulf of Cambay on the west coast of India. (III) Kalibangan lies in North-West of Delhi along the left bank of the now-dry Ghaggar. (IV) Harappa, usually identified with Hariyupiya of the Rigveda, is situated on an old bed of the Beas River.
explanation: Mohenjo-Daro is located off the right (West) bank of the lower Indus River in Larkana district of Sind, Pakistan. Lothal is famous for the discovery of several ruins of Indus Valley Civilization. Lothal is located between the Sabarmati River, at the head of the gulf of Cambay on the west coast of India and its tributary Bhogava, in the Saurasthra region. Kalibangan is one of the important Harappan cities situated on the southern bank of the river dry Ghaggar (old Sarasvati) and has a continuous history since the Hakra Phase, up to the Late Harappan. Harappa is situated on the left bank of the Ravi River. Many scholar have identified Hariyupia of Rigveda to Harappa but they don't have consensus over it.

explanation: At Kalibangan, fire alters have been discovered similar to those found at Lothal which S.R. Rao thinks could have served no other purpose than a ritualistic one. The largest number of Harappan sites in post independence India have been found in Gujarat. All three stages of Harappan culture-early, mature and late have been found. Important sites include Desalpur, Rangpur, Rojdi, Surkotada, Lothal among others. Indus civilization, also called Indus Valley Civilization or Harappan civilization, the earliest known urban culture of the Indian subcontinent. Kunal was a pre- Harappan Indus valley civilisation settlement located in Fatehabad district of Haryana. It was once a Harappan village.

question: Which of the following statements about the Indus Valley Civilization is/are correct? (I) Sites of the Indus Valley Civilization are not confined to the valley of the Indus river. (II) Typical pottery of the Indus Valley Civilization is red, as designs painted on it in black.
explanation: The Indus Valley Civilization was not only confined to Indus valley and in fact was far more expansive in India than thought before. And in India it grew along the Ghaggar-Hakra River valley which is often conjectured as courses of Ancient River Saraswati mentioned in the Rig Veda. Indus Valley pottery consists chiefly of very fine wheelmade wares, very few being hand-made. Plain pottery is more common than painted ware. Plain pottery is generally of red clay, with or without a fine red or grey slip. It includes knobbed ware, ornamented with rows of knobs. The black painted ware has a fine coating of red slip on which geometric and animal designs are executed in glossy black paint.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Indus civilization is associated with:
explanation: With the study point of view, history has been divided into three parts on the basis of period, culture and human activities – Pre Historic, Proto Historic and Historic. The period for which there is not any written evidence available and the study about this period is based on the remains found from the excavation is known as Pre Historic period. Historic age refers to the period for which the written as well as archaeological evidences are available and written evidences could be read. Whereas, proto history refers to that period during which the written evidence is available but they have not been read yet. Thus the Indus Valley Civilization belongs to proto historic age because the pictographic script has been found from Indus Valley Civilization but could not be read and its existence is noted in Mesopotamian writings.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1996 BPSC(Pre) 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.14

question: Two statements are given below: Assertion- (A) : The towns of Mohenjodaro and Harappa are extinct now. Reason-(R) : They appeared during excavation. Which of the followings is true in the above context?
options: A & R both are true and R is correct explanation of A.
A & R both are true but R is not a correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
explanation: Both the statements ‘A’ and ‘R’ are true, as the Mohenjo-daroth and Harappa had lost their entity in early 19 century BC. The excavation carried out on these two Indus sites provide information about these two places of historical importance.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.15

subject: AP & Indian History
question: A Great bath was found from which site of Indus civilization?
explanation: The remains of 'Great bath' has been found from Mohenjo-daro. It was the earliest Public Water tank in the ancient world. It measures approximately 12 meters north-south and 7 meters wide with a maximum depth of 2.44 meters. There were stairs in north and south end of the tank.

explanation: The evidence of well inside the houses has been found from Mohenjo-daro. The residential houses in Mohenjo-daro and other Indus towns were well equipped and well furnished with all the necessities of human life. People of Mohenjo-daro had about 700 wells which brought underground water to the surface.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: From which one of the following places of Indus valley civilization the famous Ox seal has been found?
explanation: The famous Ox seal has been found from ‘Mohenjo-daro’ an Indus site located at Right bank of River Indus in Larakana district of Pakistan. It is important to mention that the word ‘Mohenjodaro’ stands for Mound of the Dead. The name was given because the dead bodies were found in a large number during the excavations. Among other major remains found from Mohenjo-daro are Great Bath, Granary, the Sculpture of Pashupati Shiva and dancing figurine of a woman.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.15

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In context to Harappan civilization, the evidence of rock cut architecture has been found from :
explanation: Seven hemispherical constructions were found at Dholavira, of which two were elevated in detail, which were constructed over large rock cut chambers. Dholavira site is located in the Kutch district of Gujarat. This site was discovered by J.P. Joshi in 1967-68. The evidence of stadium and a big signboard have also been found from this site. This town was divided into three parts namely the fort, the middle and the lower town. This was the second largest site of Indus valley in India.

explanation: The largest site (in area) of Indus Valley Civilization in India is ‘Rakhigarhi’. Other towns recognized as big towns were Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Dholavira and Kalibangan. Rakhigarhi is located in Hisar district of Haryana. Other Harappan sites in Haryana are – Banawali, Mitathal, and Kunal. The excavation of Rakhigarhi was carried out by Dr. Suraj Bhan. The remains of pre Harappan age were also found from Rakhigarhi.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the followings pair is not correctly matched in context to the origin of Harappan civilization?
options: E J H Mackay– Migration of people from Sumer
Mortimer Wheeler– Immigration of the idea of civilization from West Asia
Amalananda Ghosh– Origin of Harappan civilization is a result of maturity of early Harappan civilization.
M Rafiq Mughal– Harappan civilization emerged as an effect of Mesopotamian civilization.
explanation: Many scholars have presented various views regarding the origin of Harappan civilization. E.J.H. Mackay believes that the Harappan civilization originated due to the migration of people from Sumer(Southern Mesopotamia). Historian D.H. Garden,Mortimer Wheeler believes that the Harappan civilization originated due to the migration of the idea of civilization from Western Asia. Amalananda Ghosh had the view that the emergence of Harappan civilization resulted from the immigration of the Pre-Harappan civilization. M. Rafiq Mughal believe that Harappan civilization was developed in Harappa in the Ravi river region. He has denied the old belief that the Harappan civilization drew inspiration from Western Mesopotamian civilization.
source: RAS/RTS PCS (Pre) G.S. 2015 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.16

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Excavation work in Chanhudaro was directed by :
explanation: Archaeologist E.J.H. Mackay had initiated exploration work at Chanhudaro in 1935-36. This Indus site is located at the left bank of Indus river, in a distance of 80 km from Mohenjodaro. Chanhudaro is the only Indus site from where the curved bricks have been found. It is the site from where furnaces of melting the metals and toy making factories have also been found. Ancient History

question: Who had used the word Indus Civilization at first?
explanation: Sir John Marshall was the first scholar who used the term 'Indus Civilization' for the Harappa Civilization. As the maximum expansion of the civilization is in Indus valley region that is why Sir John Marshall named it as Indus Valley Civilization.

question: Who among the followings was not associated with excavation of Harappa & Mohenjodaro?
explanation: The archaeologist associated with the excavation of Harappa and Mohenjodaro are – Daya Ram Sahni- Harappa (1921) and Rakhal Das Banerji- Mohenjo-daro (1922). The other names associated with the excavation of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro are Madho Swaroop Vats, Sir Mortimer Wheeler (1946), Ernest Mackay, K.N. Dixit, N.G. Mazoomdar. Under the direction of the then Director of Archeological department of India, John Marshall the excavation works was carried out in Harappa and Mohenjodaro. The earliest information about Harappan site was given by Charles Masson in 1826. Later in 1853 Cunningham brought attention on the historical importance of the site.

Generally 7.5×15×30 cm dimension of brick were used in construction of buildings while 6.5×13×26 cm bricks were used in construction of roads. Hence 1st statement is incorrect. subject: AP & Indian History
question: Select the correct statements about religious beliefs of the Rig Vedic Period : I. Dyus was a celestial God of the Rig Vedic Aryans similar to Jupiter of the Greeks. II. Prithvi was considered as the mother of all Gods. III. Agni was worshipped as the intermediary of taking the offerings to the deities. IV. Cow sacrifice was also the part of worship.
explanation: Dyus was the celestial God of Rig Vedic Aryans which is similar to Zeus and first syllable of the Jupiter. The Prithivi is the sanskrit name for the earth. She is complementary to Dyus Pita (Father Sky). In the Rigveda the earth and the sky are primarily addressed dually as Dyavaprithivi. She is associated with the cow. Prithu, an incarnation of Vishnu, milked her in the form of a cow. She is not considered as mother of all gods. Agni was worshipped as intermediary of taking the offerings to the dities. Cow sacrifices was also prevalent as the part of workship. Hence, option (c) is correct answer.
source: APPSC (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.21

question: Consider the following statements regarding the Rig Veda. A. It mentions the Aryans as a cultural community. B. It has many commonalities with Avesta. C. It mentions Saraswati as naditarna. D. It indicates that the dasyus kept cattle for dairy products Which of the following are correct?
explanation: The Rigveda mentioned, Aryan as a cultural community. It has many commonalities with Avesta. It also mentioned river Saraswati as Naditarna. It indicates that the Dasyus kept cattle for dairy products. Hence, all statements are true.
source: Odisha PSC (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.22

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following Vedas has two groups, Shukla and Krishna?
explanation: The Yajur Veda is about the sacrificial prayers and it is divided into two parts-Krishna Yajurveda and Shukla Yajur Veda. There are two primary versions or Samhitas of the Yajurveda: Shukla (white) and Krishna (black).
source: J & K PSC 2021 Paper-(I) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.22

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The Gayatri Mantra in Rigveda is dedicated to which of the following deities?
explanation: Savitur is also called Savitri. The popular 'Gayatri Mantra' is given in the third Mandala of the Rig Veda, which is dedicated to the god Savitur (Savitri). Gayatri Mantra has been composed by Maharishi Vishwamitra.
source: GUJARAT PSC CIVIL PRE-PAPER-I (21-3-2021) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.22

question: Which of the following statements are correct? (I) All the four types of musical instruments known today have its mention in Rigveda. (II) String instrument, membranophone, wind instruments, etc. were popular in Vedic times. (III)The discussion about Indian music is found in the most ancient book, 'Dholsagar'.
explanation: Four types of instruments have been mentioned during Vedic period. These are - stringed Instruments (Chordophones), wind instruments (aerophones), membranophones and metallic instruments. 'Samaveda' is considered to be one of the primary sources of Indian music and art. Ancient History
source: GUJARAT PSC CIVIL PRE-PAPER-I (21-3-2021) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.22

subject: AP & Indian History
question: There is similarity in Rig-Veda and Avesta. Avesta is associated with which region?
explanation: The Avesta is the primary collection of religious texts of Zoroastrianism composed in Avestan language. It is associated with Iran. Zend Avesta is the holy book of Zoroastrianism which contains the teaching of the prophet Zoroaster.
source: UP Lower (Pre) 2004 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.22

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which is the ancient most veda among the following?
explanation: The Rigveda is the ancient most veda of the four Vedas, namely Rigveda, Yajurveda, Atharva Veda, Samveda. The Rigveda is a large collections of hymns in praise of the gods. Which are chanted in various rituals.
source: UP Lower (Pre) 2009-10 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.22

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following Statements is/are correct? (I) The Rig Vedic economy was predominantly based on pastoralism. (II) The Rig Vedic farmers used ploughs in cultivation. (III)The Rig Vedic people had good trade relations with West Asia.
explanation: Rig Vedic economy was primarily pastoralist. Cattle rearing was their chief occupation. The people started the agricultural practices such were ploughing, sowing, reaping and harvesting. The Vedic people cultivated the crops of wheat, barley and other eatable nuts. The Rig Vedic people had good trade relations with West Asia.
source: GUJARAT PSC CIVIL PRE-PAPER-I (21-3-2021) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.22

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following assemblies are mentioned in the Rigveda? (I) Sabha (II) Samiti (III) Vidatha
explanation: Several tribal or the clan-based assemblies such as the Sabha, Samiti, Vidatha, Gana are mentioned in the Rigveda. They exercised deliberated, military and religious function. The vidatha seems to be a more popular assembly than either Sabha or Samiti in the Rig Vedic period.
source: GUJARAT PSC CIVIL PRE-PAPER-I (21-3-2021) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.22

subject: AP & Indian History
question: According to Atharva Veda, Sabha and Samiti are twin daughters of:
explanation: During the Vedic Period, Sabha was a body of village elders and Samiti was a general assembly in which all the members of community participated. The Atharva Veda identified Sabha and Samiti as two daughters of the high Vedic God Prajapati.
source: Arunachal PSC (GS) 26-11-2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.22

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Dadhikara is the name of a ______ mentioned in Rigveda
explanation: Dadhi-kara is the name of a divine horse or bird, personification of the morning sun, which is addressed in the Rigveda. He is invoked in the morning along with Agni, Ushas and the Asvins. Dadhikra or Dadhikara was selected for the Ashvamedha of king Trasadasyu.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-2019 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.23

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The Rig Vedic ''Pani'' belongs to which class of citizens?
explanation: In the Rig Vedic period, 'Pani' were the people who were trader (cattle). In Rig Veda, there is a mention of struggle between 'Deities' (Devatas) and 'Panis' and their massacre by deities. 'Pani' people were creditors (money lenders) and they used to charge heavy taxes and hence were called Vekanata.
source: MPPCS (Pre) 2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.23

subject: AP & Indian History
question: According to Rigveda which Aryan Chief defeated ‘Dasyus’?
explanation: According to Rigveda Trasadasyu Aryan Chief defeated ‘Dasyus’. Dasyus were considered as original native people at that time.
source: NAGALAND NCS PRELIMS, 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.23

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following is a Samhita of Shukla Yajurveda?
explanation: The Samhita of the Shukla Yajurveda is called the Vajasaneyi Samhita. The name Vajasaneyi is derived from Vajasaneya, the Patronymic of Yajnavalkya, and the founder of the Vajasaneyi branch.
source: UPPCS (Pre) 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.23

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The officer who enjoyed authority over a large pasture ground during Rigvedic period was known as?
explanation: During Rigvedic era, Vrajapati used to be an officer of the Grazing ground whose main task was to control the grazing land. Senani was used to be the chief commander. Gramini was used to be the head of the village, which assisted the king during the war. Kulap was the head of the family, also known as Grihapati. Ancient History
source: Himachal PSC (Pre) 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.23

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to difference between the culture of Rigvedic Aryans and Indus valley people, which of the following statement/ statements is/are correct? 1. Rigvedic Aryans used the coat of mail and helmet in warfare whereas the people of Indus valley civilization does not leave any evidence of using them. 2. Rigvedic Aryans knew gold, silver and copper whereas Indus valley people knew only copper and iron. 3. Rigvedic Aryans had domesticated horse whereas there is no evidence of Indus valley people having been aware of this animal. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
explanation: It is true that Aryans were using armour (safegaurd) and helmet while the Indus people were not aware about these equipments. Thus the statement ‘1’ is true. While statement ‘2’ and ‘3’ are false, as the Indus people were familiar with the metals like copper, bronze, Silver and Gold etc. Iron was not known to them. The remains of a horse are reported from Surkotda, situated in west Gujarat and relate to 2000 BC but identity is doubt full. Harappan culture wasn't horse oriented. Note- UPSC has given option (c) as correct answer.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S.1 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.23

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The basic script of Rig-Veda was :
explanation: Rigveda was not documented until late years, because the intricacies and minute details of sound and stresses of the Vedic Language could not be preserved by writing. And when, it was put down to written form, it was written in devanagari script. The oldest manuscript of Rigveda is in Pune collection which is dated to 1464 AD.
source: UPPCS (Pre) spl G.S.2004 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.23

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Collection of which of the followings is based on Rig-Veda?
explanation: The collection of Sam Veda is based on Rig Veda. There are 1549 verses in Sam Veda, Only 75 verses were added later, while the rest have been derived from Rig-Veda. The Samveda is shortest of all four vedas. The origion of Saptswara (sa, re, ga, ma etc.) is mentioned in the Samveda.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S.1997 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.23

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The early mention about Ayurveda (the science of life) is found in:
explanation: The earliest mention of Ayurveda (the science of life) is found in Atharva Veda. It provides the list of medicinal plants, diseases and their remedies. Atharva Veda was named after the name Sage Atharva.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.24

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The religion of early Vedic Aryans was:
explanation: The religion of early Vedic Aryans was based on nature worship and sacrificial act. Vedic Aryans established the relation of various deities with the natural powers. They believed that all natural happenings are stimulated by the related Deity. Among these deities Indra was assumed as the God of Rain and war. Agni was the second most powerful deities next to Indra who was the mediator between man and God, who performed its duties through sacrificial act. Varun was the God of water, Sun was the God of light, Earth was assumed as the goddess of productivity etc. There was ‘Polytheism’ in Rigvedic period. No evidence of Idol worship is found in Rig-Vedic society.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S.1st 2012 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.24

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The word Gotra occurs for the first time in:
explanation: The early mention of the term ‘Gotra’ is found in Rig-Veda while introduction of Gotra as a tradition can be traced in Atharva Veda. The term Gotra is commonly considered to be equivalent to clan. It broadly refers to people who are descendants in an unbroken male line from a common male ancestor or patrilineage. Ancient History

question: To whom the 9th Mandal of Rig-Veda is dedicated?

explanation: The 9th Mandal of Rig-Veda is devoted to Soma. Soma was considered as the 'God of vegetation'. ‘Soma’ was the juice of a plant which was found at Moojwant hills of Himalaya. The Soma was consumed on the occasion of religious celebrations. It was also considered as an Eternal drink. It is equivalent to the Iranian 'Haoma'.

The verses of this Veda were sung by the priest called Adhvaryu. There is mention of various types of sacrificial acts also, as the different type of sacrificial acts were performed at different occasions.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Sabha during Vedic period was :
options: An organization of professionals in the villages
A national assembly of all the people of the state
explanation: During Vedic period we found the existence of institutions like Sabha, Samiti and Vidath. The Sabha was related to the senior most and recognized people of Vedic society, while samiti was institution in which the people from all families of the state used to take part. Vidath was a type of general assembly in which the total people of the state could participate. Sabha was like a council of ministers which was responsible to advise the king on various issues. Sabha was playing a crucial role in appointment of the king.

explanation: The term Vedic literature means the four Vedas, their Samhita and the allied literature based on or derived from Vedas. The correct order of Vedic literature is – Vedic Samhita, Brahmana, Aranyaka, Upanishads

explanation: The word ‘Yava’ referred in Rig-Veda is applied for the barley. The people during Rig-Vedic period were producing various crops like wheat (Godhoom), Rice (Brihi), Yava (Barley), black pea (urad), red lentil (Masoor) etc. The detailed information about various crops is provided by Shatpath Brahmana. subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following was considered as valuable asset during Rigvedic period?
explanation: Cow was a sacred and valuable animal during Rigvedic period. It was the medium of exchange in Vedic society. Brahmanas used to get the charity in the form of cows. The cow was called ‘Aghanya’ in the Rigvedic period. The maximum battles fought during Vedic period was only because of cows. The term Gaveshana in Rig-Veda stands for cow search and the battle was known as ‘Gavishti’. 'Pani' community was said to be involved in cow stealing. Pani were basically the businessmen. They were said to be the enemies of Aryans.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In Vedic rituals Hota is associated with:
explanation: Hota (Hotri) was the priest associated with Rig-Veda, who used to read the hymns of Rig-Veda during sacrificial act. The priest of Yajurveda was called Adhvaryu, where as the priest of Samveda was called Udgatri and the priest of Atharva Veda was known to be Brahma.
source: UP RO/ARO (Mains) 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.28

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The term ‘Aryan’ denotes
explanation: Arya is the word of Sanskrit language, which mean ‘The great’ or ‘noble’.
source: UPPCS (Pre) GS 2007 IAS (pre) G.S. 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.28

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Meaning of the word Arya in classical Sanskrit?
options: Person having faith in others religion
explanation: Meaning of the word Arya in classical Sanskrit is ‘A noble person’ with specific qualities and reputed class and community.
source: UP Lower (Pre) 1998 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.28

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Name the tribe which does not belong to the Panchajana of Rigvedic Aryans?
explanation: Panchjanya is the common name given to five most ancient vedic tribes of Aryans. These were – Anu, Yadu, Turvasa, Druhyu, Puru. Thus the Kikkat was not among the tribal communities of the aryans.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.28

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who had composed Gayatri mantra?
explanation: Gayatri mantra was composed by Rishi Vishwamitra. This mantra is devoted to Goddess Savitri who is associated with Sun. Early mention of Gayatri mantra is found in Rig-Veda in the third mandal. Ancient History
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) G.S. 2006-07 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.28

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In the context of ancient Indian society, which one of the following terms does not belong to the category of the other three?
explanation: Kosh is different from three other options, As the Kula, Vansha and Gotra are related to the family in Hindu society, while the word ‘Kosh’ stands for treasury.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S.1996 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.28

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the followings had not participated in Dasharagya battle?
explanation: As mentioned in Rig-Veda, Puru, Yadu, Turvasha, Anu, Druhyu, Alinas, Paktha, Bhalanas,Visharin and Shiva were the kings who took part in Dasharagya battle against King Sudas of Bharat dynasty. It was Gandhari who had not participated in Dasharagya battle.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.28

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Choose the correct chronological order of four Purushartha:
explanation: The concept of four Purushartha existed during post Vedic period for the social growth of human being. These are recognized as the four objectives of a human being. The correct chronological order of Purushartha is Dharma-Artha-Kama-Moksha.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Mains) 2010-11 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.28

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which Vedic epics mentioned the word ‘Varna’ at first?
explanation: The earliest mention about class system is found in Purusha Sukta of Rig-Veda, while as per Hindu mythology the origin of Varna system is said to be from Virat purusha in the 10th Mandala of Rigveda.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) G.S.1st 2014-15 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.28

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The basis of untouchability during Vedic age was :
explanation: The Rigvedic society was divided into four varnas. These varnas were Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras. This division was done on the basis of occupation. The earliest mention about class system was found in Purusha Sukta of Rig-Veda, while as per Hindu mythology the origin of Varna system is said to be from Virat purusha.
source: UPPSC Asst. Forest Conservator Exam 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.28

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Rig-Veda is a:
explanation: Rig-Veda is a collection of hymns and verses devoted to various Vedic deities.
source: UP RO/ARO (Pre) exam 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.28

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements in reference to Vedic Deity Indra and select the correct answer from the following codes: 1. Was the God of thunderstorms 2. Punished sinners 3. Was the guardians of the moral system 4. The God of rain Codes :
explanation: Indra was supposed as the god of rain, storm and battle etc. Indra was most powerful and popular Vedic deity. 250 Suktas (Hymn) of Rig-Veda are devoted to Indra. Varun is considered as the protector of the moral law and punishes the sinners.
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. I 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.29

source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) G.S. 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.29

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Rigvedic tribal assembly associated with judicial function was:
explanation: There were three democratic institutions during Vedic period, named as Sabha, Samiti and Vidatha. These institutions were responsible for different types of tasks. Sabha was the assembly of elders and was associated with pastoral affairs and also performed judicial and administrative functions.
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) G.S.2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.29

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The utterance ‘Tamso-Ma-Jyotirgamaya’ basically belongs to:
explanation: The utterance of ‘Tamso-Ma-Jyotirgamaya’ basically belongs to Upanishads, which means ‘Take me to light from the darkness’. ‘Tamso-Ma- Jyotirgamaya’ has been derived from ‘Brihadaranyak Upanishad’. It means ‘Provide me wisdom and take me out from the darkness of superstition’.
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre)G.S. 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.29

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The word meaning of which Upanishad is white horse?
explanation: Shwetashwatar Upanishad is related to Krishna Yajurveda is an important Upanishad having 113 hymns. The literal meaning of shwetashwatar Upanishad is ‘white horse’. B. Later Vedic Period
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S. 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.29

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which officer was known as 'Bhagadugha' during Vedic administration?
options: Chief Officer of the Gambling Department
explanation: During vedic period officials responsible for revenue collection were called on Bhagadugha, (Bhag- share). Note- other officers– Govikartana → Keeper of forest & games Spasas → Spies & messengers Palagala → Messenger Akshavapa → Incharge/Superintendent of Gambling
source: UPPCS (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.29

subject: AP & Indian History

explanation: Bhagvad Gita is comprises 18 chapters in the Bhisma Parva of the epic Mahabharata.
source: UPPSC (J) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.29

question: The term : Votive inscriptions" refers to
options: Records of miseries of women such as sati, etc
Royal orders and decisions of the kings
Account on sacrifices done by kings during their consecration ceremony
explanation: The Votive inscriptions are those inscriptions that records gifts made to religious institution. Votive inscriptions are among the oldest inscriptions. They may express gratitude for victory in battle.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In the Later Vedic Period, religion had become more
explanation: The emergence of monarchical states in the later Vedic age led to a distancing of the 'Rajan' from the people and the emergence of a Varna hierarchy. The society was divided into four social groups - Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras. Also due to various rituals and emergence of deities the religion during latter Vedic period became more complex.
source: Mizoram PSC (CCE) Pre-2018 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.29

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The sage who is said to have Aryanized South India was?
explanation: Aryanization (Aryakaran) of south India was made by Rishi ‘Agastya’. This information is found in Tamil legends and literatures. Agastya Rishi was included in Saptarishi in Vedic texts, he invented an early grammar of Tamil Language.
source: Jharkhand PCS (Pre)G.S. 1st 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.30

explanation: Some important officials during post Vedic era were regarded as Ratnin. There were 18 Ratnins which are as follows - Purohita, Senani, Vrajapati, Jivagribha, Dutas/Spasas, Gramani, Kulapati, Madhyamasi, Bhagadugha, Sangrihitri, Mahishi, Suta, Govinkartana, Palagala, Kshatri, Akshavapa, Athapati, Takshan.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.30

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following epics mentioned about Krishna, the son of Devaki?
explanation: The earliest information about Krishna (The son of Devaki) is found in Chandogya Upanishad. Krishna has been recognized as the disciple of Ghora Angiras and the son of Devaki here. Krishna is credited for initiating Bhagawat sect. He was popular as Bhagawan Krishna among his followers. Later his parity was established with Vedic god Vishnu and his sect became popular as Vaishnavism. The story of Satyakam Jabali is also mentioned in Chhandogya Upanishad. Jabali was the son of Jabala. Jabala was the disciple of Maharshi Gautam and she (Jabala) was said to be an unmarried mother.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) re-exam G.S.1999-2000 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.30

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Ekalavya was the self proclaimed disciple of which mentor?
explanation: Ekalavya was the self proclaimed disciple of ‘Dronacharya’ (the mentor of Kauravas and Pandavas during Mahabharat age). Dronacharya had denied to teach Ekalavya, the art of archery. Then Ekalavya made a terracotta figurine of Dronacharya and started the practice of archery, assuming Dronacharya figurine as his mentor, and became a great archer.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 1996 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.30

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which one of the the following usages was a Post Vedic development?
explanation: ‘Ashram system’ was initiated during post Vedic period. Assuming the total age of human being 100 years, the Hindu epics divided it into four part of 25 years each. The concept of Ashram was related to duties and responsibilities of a person at different stages of the age. Brahmcharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sanyasa were the four Ashrams.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S.1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.30

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Sarga, Pratisarga, Vamsa, Manvantars and Vansanucharita are the indicators of:
explanation: Amarkosa Purana is one which describes Sarga, Pratisarga, Vamsa, Manvantars and Vansanucharita. Sarga - Speaks about the creation of the Universe. Pratisarga - It speaks about secondary creations after dissolution. Vamsa - It speaks about the great Geneology of Rishis and Devtas. Manvantara - It speaks about the reigns of Manus. Vansanucharita - It gives detailed description of dynasties of kings who ruled the world.
source: UPPCS (Pre) Re-Exam G.S. 2015 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.30

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The no. of Puranas is:
explanation: There are traditionally 18 Puranas which were composed perhaps between 350 and 750 CE. These Puranas are – Matsya Purana, Kurma Purana, Varaha purana, Vishnu Purana, Naradiya Purana, Garuna Purana, Bhagwata Purana, Linga Purana, Shiva Purana, Padma Purana, Skand Purana, Agni Purana, Brahmanda Purana, Brahmvaivarta Purana, Markandeya Purana, Bhavishya Purana, Vamana Purana and Brahma Purana.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S.2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.30

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following is considered to be the first law-giver of India ?
explanation: Manu is regarded as ancient most law giver of India. His creation Manu Smriti is Known as Manava Dharma Shastra. It was composed in Sanskrit language. Timing of its composition was between 200 BC to 300 AD. It contains the laws related to various social and spiritual life of a human being. Kulluka, Govinda raj and Medhatithi has commented on it. Manu-Smriti composed by Manu gives a description of four social classes (Varnas) and four state of life (Ashrams).
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S.1st 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.30

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Religious Movem 1. With reference to Indian history, consider the following pairs: Historical person Known as 1. Aryadeva - Jaina scholar 2. Dignaga - Buddhist scholar 3. Nathamuni - Vaishnava scholar How many pairs given above are correctly matched?
explanation: The Correct match is as follows:- Aryadeva - Buddhist scholar Dignaga - Buddhist scholar Nathamuni - Vaishnava scholar
source: UPSC IAS 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.31

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following were common to both Buddhism and Jainism ? I. Avoidance of extremities of penance and enjoyment. II. Indifference to the authority of the Vedas III. Denial of efficacy of rituals IV. Non-injury to animal life Select the correct answer using the codes given below: Codes:
explanation: Similarities and differences in thoughts of Jainism and Buddhism sects are as follows– Similarities:– Both Sects had denied the authority of Vedas. Both criticized the sacrificial acts and emphasized on Non- violence. Both believed that the law of Karma (object) is above all the living objects, whether deity or human being. They denied the theory that god is the creator of the World. Both believed in the theory of re-incarnation. Differences:– Buddhism argued the middle path for the enlightenment or to get rid of the birth and death cycle. Buddhist denied the hardness in life, while on the other hand Jains emphasized on harsh life style and austerity. In Buddhism ‘Nirvana’ stand for the highest spiritual wisdom or the self consciousness, While in Jainism the term Nirvan stands for the death. Both Jainism and Buddhism focus on the superiority of the Kshatriya Varna over all others Varnas including Brahamanas.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1996 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.31

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following is not similar in Buddha and Jain sect?
options: Rejection of customs and rituals Ancient History 3 ments of Ancient India
explanation: Both Jain and Buddhism were Nastik sects and were initiated against the supremacy of Brahminism and their sacrificial acts. The similarities and difference in their belief are as under– Similarities: (i) Both challenged the supremacy of Brahmins and the sacrificial acts and rituals followed by them. (ii) Both rejected the supernaturality of Vedas. (iii) Both emphashised on non-voilence and etiquette. (iv) Both believed in ‘theory of Karma’ and incarnation theory. (v) Both believed in ‘Moksha’. Differences: (i) Gautam Buddha emphashised on Madhya Marg (The middle path) for the Moksha while Mahavira emphashised on penance. (ii) Buddhism denied the presence of soul. It believed that every article in the world are transitory (momentary) while in Jainism it is believed that the souls are infinite and lives in all particles of the worldly articles. (iii) Buddhists believed that ‘Nirvana’ can be achieved in the life time of a person while in Jainism it is believed that Nirvana (Moksha) can be attained only after the death. (iv) Buddha favored the simple clothing for the monks while Mahavira told his followers to remain Naked. (v) Buddha was the big critic of class/ caste system while Mahavira did not reject the caste/ class system emphatically.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2000-01 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.31

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statement and select the answer from the codes given below: A. There was great religious turbulence in almost whole of the world during 6th century BC. B. Vedic religion became more complicated. Code:
options: A is true but B is false
A is false but B is true
explanation: Both the statements (A) and (B) are true. The period of 6th century B.C. is recognized as the period of religious turbulence in all part of the world. Religion had become so complicated due to its sacrificial acts and beliefs that it resulted in emergence of various infidel sects such as Jainism, Buddhism, Ajivakas etc.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which one of the following is the distinctive features between a Nastika and Astika system in India?
options: Belief in the existence of God
Belief in the doctrine of re-birth
Belief in the authenticity of the Vedas
Belief in the existence of heaven and hell
explanation: There are two types of thought in India—(1) Theist (2) Atheist. Theists are those who believe in existance of god while Atheists are against this view. The two thoughts can be differentiated on the basis of their belief in god and Vedas. The word ‘Atheist’ in Vedas has been used for those who do not believe in authenticity of Vedas. Charvaka, Jain and Buddhist are atheist in Indian philosophy while Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Sankhya, Yoga, Mimansa and Vedanta are theist philosophy. The Nyaya school holds that there are four valid means of knowledge - Pratyakasha-(perception), Anumana-(inference), Upamana (analogy) and Shabda- (hearing). Ancient History 4 A. Nastik Schools
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. Ist , 2005 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.32

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Identify the incorrect statement on the contributions of Jainism :

The early Jainns discarded Sanskrit language.
They never used Apabhramsa for the earliest important works of Jainism.
explanation: The early Jainas adopted prakrit languages of the common people to preach their doctrines and discarded Sanskrit language. The oldest surviving Jain texts are the Angas. These are written in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit language itself is apbramsa of Sanskrit. Thus only statement 4 is correct.

explanation: Devardhi Kshemasharman was a prominent Jain scholar, under whose leadership the second assembly of Jainism was organized at a place called Vallabhi in Gujarat in about 512 AD. Here 12 Angas and 12 Upangas were compiled together. In this meeting, the final compilation of Jainism texts were scripted and written.
source: Himanchal PSC (Pre) 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.35

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The followers of Vardhamana Mahavira originally were called .........
explanation: After continuous and severe Penance for twelve years, on the tenth day of Vaisakha, outside the town of Jimbhikgram, Mahavira attained perfect knowledge or “Kaivalya” at the age of 42 while meditating under a sal tree beside the river Rijjupalika. For his final deliverance from the bonds of pleasure and pain Vardhamana became known as Mahavira and Jina or the conqueror. He was also known as “Kevalin”. His followers or disciples were known as ‘Nirgranthas” (free from fetters or bonds). The doctrine preached by him was known as Jainism.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) 2004-05 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.35

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements is/are applicable to Jain doctrine? 1. The surest way of annihilating Karma is to practice penance. 2. Every object, even the smallest particle has a soul. 3. Karma is the bane of the soul and must be ended. Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
explanation: Jain epic Acharanga Sutra mentions that the only way to destroy Karma (object) is austerity. It also says that the soul exist in all object-even in the smallest molecule. Jain sect believes that the flow of Karma towards life is ‘Asrava’ while the break of Karma’s flow towards life is called ‘Samvar’ and the destruction of stored Karma is called 'Nirjara'. As per this thought the Karma is destroyer of the soul, so the karma should be destroyed at first. To obey this, pupils must follow 'Pancha Mahavrata'.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.35

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements: 1. Vardhamana Mahavira’s mother was the daughter of Lichchhavi chief Chetaka 2. Gautam Buddha’s mother was a princess from the Koshalan dynasty 3. Parashvanatha, the twenty-third Tirthankara, belonged to Banaras Ancient History 4 Which of these statements is/are not correct?
explanation: Mahavira Swami was born in 540 BC, was the son of Siddhartha and Trishala. His birth place was (Kundagrama) Vaishali. His mother Trishalard was the sister of Lichchhavi ruler Chetak. The 23 Teerthankar Parshwanath belonged to Varanasi. Gautam Buddha’s mother Mahamaya Devi was the princess of ‘Kosala’ republic. She was the daughter of king Arjun of Devadah Gana, located in modern Gorakhpur district of Uttar Pradesh. Mahavir Swami died in Pavapuri near Rajgriha in 468 BC at the age of 72 years. According to historical facts Mahavira Swami was born in 540 BCE whereas according to traditional facts he was born in 599 BCE.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.35

question: Assertion (A): The emphasis of Jainism on non-violence (ahinsa) prevented agricultura- lists from embracing Jainism. Reason (R): Cultivation involved killing of insects and pests.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
explanation: There are the five Vows (religious beliefs in Jainism – non-violence, non lying (Satya), non Stealing (Asteya), non possession (Aparigraha) and celibacy (Brahmacharya). Among all these vows the maximum emphasis was given on non-violence. The war and agriculture both were prohibited in Jainism, that's why the peasants did not join the Jain religion in large number. Jains limited themselves to trade and commercial activities only. It was notable that the fifth vow celibacy was introduced by Mahavira Jain.

explanation: The concept of Anuvrata was advocated by Jain religion. It includes non violence, non lying, non stealing, non possession and celibacy. explanation: Jain religion divided into two part in 300 BC during the first Jain council called after 200 years of the death of Swami Mahavira Jain. The council was presided by Sthulbhadra. Those who stayed in Magadh during the famine period in the leadership of Sthulbhadra were called Svetamber and the followers of Bhadrabahu who had gone to Karnataka were called Digamber. The followers of Bhadrabahu had not participated in the first council Ancient History 4 organized at Pataliputra.nd The Shwetamber Agams were composed in the 2 Jain council called at Vallabhi in 512 AD. subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to ancient India, consider the following statements: 1. The concept of Stupa is Buddhist in origin. 2. Stupa was generally a repository of relics. 3. Stupa was a votive and commemorative structure in Buddhist tradition. How many of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: The term stupa comes from the Sanskrit word stupa, which means heap or pile. Originally stupas were simple mounds of earth or stones that served as commemorative markers for important events or burial sites. The concept of stupa is not Buddhist in origin. Hence statement-1 is incorrect. One of the primary functions of stupa is serve as a repository of relics. Relics are objects associated with Buddha such as his physical remains personal belonging or items used by him. Hence statement-II is correct. Stupas are also associated with votive and commemorative purposes. Stupas are often built as acts of devotion and as offerings to the Buddha or others enlightened beings. Hence statement III is also correct. Ancient History

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to the religious history of India, consider the following statements: 1. Sautrantika and Sammitiya were the sects of Jainism. 2. Sarvastivadin held that the constituents of phenomena were not wholly momentary, but existed forever in a latent form. Ancient History 4 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Statement 1 is false as Sautantrika and Sammitiya were the Buddhist sect, not the Jain. The creator of Sautantrika sect was Kumarlabdha in 200 AD. Sautantrika sect believed that world is truth while Nirvana is false. Though Sautantrika Sect was near to Hinyana but it was also nearer to Yogachar in view of Mahayana. Basically it created a bridge between Hinyana and Mahayana Sects. Sarvastivadin was early Buddhistrd school established under the reign of Ashoka in the 3 century BC. It is a unique set of seven Abhidharma. Sarvastivadin as the name suggest (Sarva + Asti = Everything existed) believed that Dharma is not momentary but existed in past, exists in present and will exist in future.
