explanation: After the death of Mahatma Buddha (the event of Buddha's death is known as Mahaparinirvana) the four Buddhist councils were organized at different time and place under the patronage of different rulers and was considered by different Buddhist scholars to compose the preaching and teachings of Buddha in the form of epics. These councils are as follows: (i) The First-Buddhist Council was organized just after the death of Buddha in 483 B.C. at Rajgriha (Saptaparni Cave) during Haryanka ruler Ajatshatru. The council was presided by Mahakasyapa. Sutta Pitaka and Vinay Pitaka were composed during this council. (ii) The Second Buddhist Council was organized at Vaishali in 383 B.C. during the regime of Kalashok of Shishunag dynasty. This council was presided by ‘Sabbakami’. The prime objective of the council was to remove the conflict created on the matter of discipline. Here Buddhist sect was divided in two part as (1) Sthavir and (2) Mahasanghika. (iii) The Third Buddhist Council was organized in Pataliputra in 250 B.C. during Ashoka's regime. The council was chaired by Moggaliputta Tissa. The main objective was to make rules and regulation for the stability of Buddhist religion. Third Pitaka named Abhidhamma Pitaka was composed during this council. (iv) The Fourth Buddhist Council was organized in Kundalvana (Kashmir) in 72 A.D. during the regime of Kushan ruler Kanishka. explanation: Buddhist sect was dividedst into two parts during Kanishka regime in the 1 century A.D. The fourth Buddhist council was organized by Mahayanians. With the conclusion of this council the Buddhist community was divided into two parts (i) Hinyana (ii) Mahayana. The basic difference in these two sects was on the issue of idol worship of lord Buddha. It was the Mahayana sect that started idol worship of Buddha while Hinyanis were against it because they were of the view that Buddha was a great human being not the God. Mahayanians were reformist while Hinyanians were orthodox in opinion. Later Mahayana was divided in two sub sects– (i) Sunyavad (Madhyamika) and (ii) Vigyanwad (Yogachar). Likewise Hinyana was also divided in two sub-sects– Vaibhashik and Sautantrik.

explanation: Both (A) and (R) are correct but R is not the correct explanation of ‘A’. Mahatma Buddha died in 483 B.C. at Kushinagar at 80 years of age. Kushinagar (Pawapuri) was the capital of Malla republic.

subject: AP & Indian History

explanation: The image of Buddha in ‘Bhumisparsh’ form is symbolic to the incidence of Maravijaya. It shows the call of Buddha to the earth as a witness of his holiness and sanctity.th It is related to Gupta Period which dates back to 5 century CE.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. (Pre) 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.49

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During the reign of which king Buddha got the status of the God?
explanation: The earliest evidence of the idol of Lord Buddha has been found from Mathura. The idol in Mathura art were made of red sand stone. The credit to initiate idol worship in India goes to Mahayana sect of Buddhism whichst existed as a separate sect during Kanishka regime in 1 century A.D. the idol of Buddha in standing posture was made primarily during Kushan period while the ‘Bhusparsha’ posture was the creation of Gupta period.
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S. 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.49

Lhotsava Lhakhang : Zanskar Valley temple, Nako 3. Alchi temple complex : Ladakh Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
explanation: Tabo monastery and temples are situated in Lahaul spiti region of Himachal Pradesh, also known as Ajanta of Himalayan region. Alchi temple and monastery circuit is located in Alchi village of Laddakh. The Lhotsava Lhakhang temple circuit is located in trans-himalayan region in Indo-China border in ‘Nako’ village of Kinnaur district in Himachal Pradesh.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Some Buddhist rock-cut caves are called Chaityas, while the others are called Viharas. What is the difference between the two?
options: Vihara is a place of worship, while Chaitya is the dwelling place of the monks
Chaitya is a place of worship, while Vihara is the dwelling place of the monks
Chaitya is the stupa at the far end of the cave, while Vihara is the hall axial to it
There is no material difference between the two
explanation: Chaitya and Vihars have the basic importance in Buddhist sect. The place where Buddhist monks reside is known as Buddhist Vihar while the Chaitya is recognized as worshipping place of Buddhist. During ancient period the rulers of various dynasties had constructed Chaitya and Vihars for Buddhist monk. Kanheri, Karle, Nagarjunakonda, Bhaja are the examples of such Chaityas and Vihars.
source: IAS (Pre) Ist G.S. 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.50

Vihara and Chaitya both can be used for dwelling purpose

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the founder of Vikramashila Vihara?
explanation: The founder of Vikramshila Vihara was Pal ruler Dharmpal. He constructed Vikramshila and Somapuri Vihara (Paharpur) according to Taranath, he had established more than 50 religious schools in the 8th-9th century.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.50

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The stupas site not connected with any incident of Buddha's life is :
explanation: Sanchi stupa is situated in Sanchi hills in Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh. Sanchi stupard were constructed by Mauryan ruler Ashoka in the 3 century B.C. Stupa site of sanchi is not connected with any incident of Buddha's life, while other three site were the places where he gets the enlightenment, given first sermon and died. Ancient History
source: UPPCS (Pre) Spl. G.S. 2008 UPPCS (Main) Ist G.S. 2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.50

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Known as the highest Stupa in the world, where is the Stupa of world peace located?
explanation: The world's highest stupa which is known as ‘world peace Stupa’ is situated in Rajgir (Bihar).
source: BPSC (Pre) 2007-08 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.50

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which is true in reference to Stupa?
explanation: The stupas are related to the incidence of ‘Mahaparinirvana’ (death) of Buddha. Stupas were constructed on the remains of Buddha’s dead body.
source: Jharkand PSC (Pre) 2007-08 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.50

subject: AP & Indian History
question: From excavation of which Stupa, the remains of Sariputra is found?
explanation: The Buddhist stupas are hemispherical structure or commemorative monument in which some sacred or holy relics related with Buddha or other Buddhist monks are kept. In Sanchi stupa the relics related to Sariputra and Maudgalyayan (both disciples of Buddha) are kept.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.50

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following sacred place is located on the bank of river Niranjana/Phalgu?
explanation: Bodha Gaya was the place situated at the bank of Niranjana river in Bihar. It was the place where Buddha achieved enlightenment under the Peepal tree (Bodhivriksha).
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2012 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.50

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following is known as the 'Light of Asia'?
explanation: The founder of Buddhism was Gautam Buddha who is also known as 'light of Asia'. The western writer Edwin Arnold has honoured Buddha as the Light of Asia.
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. Ist Paper 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.50

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During which reign Buddha visited Kaushambi?
explanation: According to the Paramatthajyotika, Kausambi derives its name from the sage Kosamba. However, Buddhaghosa records that Kaushambi was so named because, in course of founding the city, a large number of Kusamba trees were uprooted. A modest city with a rich past with much significance to Buddhist history. It is said that Lord Buddha frequently visited Kaushambi after attaining enlightenment to deliver sermons. During that time, Kaushambi was the capital city of King Udayin of Vatsa Janpad. It was known as one of the most affluent cities of that time. It was visited by Chinese travelers like Fa-Hein and Hiuen Tsang (Yuan-Chwang).
source: UP UDA/LDA (Pre) 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.50

subject: AP & Indian History
question: To which generation the Bodhi Vriksha (peepal tree) in Bodha Gaya belongs?
explanation: ‘Bodhith Vriksha’ (Peepal tree) in Bodha gaya at present is the 5 generation of its parental tree related to Buddha. A Buddhist temple 'Mahabodhi Mandir' is also constructed in ‘Bodh gaya’ at the place where Buddha achieved enlightenment (Absolute knowledge).
source: BPSC (Pre) 2007-08 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.51

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Mahabodhi temple in Bodh Gaya was built where:
options: Gautam Buddha delivered his first sermon
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S. 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.51

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Correct description in reference to Jatak stories:
explanation: The Jatak stories are related to the previous births of Mahatma Buddha. The Jatakas describes him as being born an elephant, a king an outcast etc. but the motive is to highlight the moral values that he propogated in each of these character.
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) G.S. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.51

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Many of the Greeks, Kushanas and Shakas embraced Buddhism rather than Hinduism because

They had renounced the policy of war and violence
Caste-ridden Hinduism did not attract them
Buddhism provided easier access to Indian society

source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1998 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.51

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Upadhyaya Atisha who played a significant role in propagation of Buddhism in Tibet belonged to which monastery?
explanation: It was Acharya Atisha of Vikramshila University who led the delegation whichth went to Tibet to propagate Buddhism during the 11 century A.D.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.51

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What for Nalanda University was worldly famous?
explanation: Nalanda Universityth was established by Gupta ruler Kumar Gupta in the 5 century C.E. It was the most ancient university of the world. The students from all over the world were studying there. There were Ancient History 5 10000 students and 2000 teachers in the university at that time. The traveler Hiuen Tsang's ‘Si-u-Ki’ gives valuable information about Nalanda University. Hiuen Tsang was a Chinese traveler. He visited India during Harshavardhan regime and stayed here for 15 years (630-645 A.D.). He was a student of Nalanda University and a teacher too. Nalanda University was known for its quality education. It was a centre of Buddhist philosophy.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1997-98 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.51

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following was the last person converted by Buddha?
explanation: The last person whom Buddha has preached to join Buddhism was Subhadda. He preached him in Kushinagar before his death.
source: UP RO/ARO (Pre) Exam, 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.51

explanation: The time of the Mahaparinirvan of Buddha was about 483 BC.
source: UPPSC Ass. Forest Conservator Exam. 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.51

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What does Tri-Ratna indicate in Buddhism?
options: Vinay Pitaka, Sutta Pitaka, Abhidhamma Pitaka
explanation: Triratnas (Buddha – Dhamma and Sangha) have the basic importance in Buddhism. ‘Buddha’ was the promoter of Buddhism. Dhamma includes his teaching and Sangha is the Buddhist community which include Buddhist monks and scholars.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. Spl. 2004 UPPSC RO/ARO (Pre) 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.51

source: Chhattisgrah PCS (Pre) 2017-18 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.51

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Yamaka Buddha pitaka is associated with:
explanation: There are three pitakas in Buddhism – Sutta Pitaka, Vinay Pitaka and Abhidhamma Pitaka. Abhidhamma Pitaka compiled in Buddhist council includes 7 different books. These are – Dhammasangani, Vibhanga, Dhatukatha, Puggalapannatti, Kathavatthu, Yamaka and Patthana.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements are correct regarding Pala painting style? explanation: The Pala paintings are in the form a large number of manuscripts on palm-leaf relating to the Buddhist themes. It is a naturalistic style which resembles the ideal forms of contemporary bronze and stone sculpture and reflects some feeling of the classical art of Ajanta.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-26.12.21 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.52

subject: AP & Indian History
question: According to Buddhism, origins of rebirth lie in ........ .
explanation: Buddhists believe in the cycle of samsara , which is the cycle of birth, life, death and rebirth. This means that people will experience suffering many times over. All of the things a person goes through in life cause suffering and they cannot do anything about it. Instead, they have to accept that it is there.
source: GUJARAT PSC CIVIL PRE-PAPER-I (21-3-2021) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.52

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In Buddhist terminology, the word "Darmachakra Pravartana" indicates _____
options: The Attainment of Niravana by Buddha
explanation: Buddha, after gaining enlightment, remained under the Bodhi tree for another seven weeks, after which he travelled to Sarnath and delivered his first sermon at the Deer Park. This event is recorded in history as the 'Dharma Chakra Pravartana' or 'Turning of the wheel of Law'.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-2019 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.52

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding "Mahabhinishkramana"? (1) The renunciation of worldly life by Mahavira (2) Rejection of the authority of the Vedas (3) The renunciation of the worldly life by Buddha (4) Eightfold path of Buddha
explanation: Gautam Buddha renounced his home at the age of 29 years and this event is called "Mahabhinishkramana"
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-2019 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.52

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Taxila, the famous educational centre in ancient India is presently located in
explanation: Takshashila or Taxila, the famous educational centre in ancient India is presently located in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. Taxila was a noted centre of learning including religious teachings of Buddhism. It is an important archaeological site and the UNESCO declared it to be a world Heritage site in 1980.
source: TPPSC Group-II Pre-11.11.2016 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.52

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Bamiyan in Afghanistan was famous for:
explanation: Bamiyan (Afghanistan) is known for the great idol of Lord Buddha made in Gandhar art this was the highest idol of Buddha in the world. Taliban extremist had destroyed it as it was the symbol of idol worship according to them.
source: UPPCS (Mains) Spl. G.S. Ist Paper 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.52

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In which city Buddhist council was organized during Ashokas reign?
explanation: The third Buddhist meet was organized at Pataliputra in 250 B.C. during Ashoka's regime. The council was presided by ‘Moggaliputta Tissa’ .

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Even Being a Buddhist Ashoka did not give up his belief in Hinduism. It's evidence is:
explanation: Though Ashoka became the follower of Buddhism after Kalinga war but he continued to hold the title of ‘Devnampiya Piyadassi’ which was a term applied in Hindu religion. It shows that his belief in Hinduism did not come to an end. In maximum number of Ashoka's edicts the title of ‘Devnampiya Piyadassi has been used as his name.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre.) G.S. 1992 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.52

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Why did Buddhism start declining in India in the early medieval times? 1. Buddha was by that time considered as one of the incarnations of Vishnu and thus became a part of Vaishnavism, 2. The invading tribes from Central Asia till the time of last Gupta king adopted Hinduism and persecuted Buddhists. 3. The Kings of Gupta dynasty were strongly opposed to Buddhism. Which of the statements given above is/are correct.
explanation: Buddhism initiated by Mahatma Buddha was based on the opposition against the evils in Hinduism. Earlier Buddhism was against the sacrificial acts and idols worship of Hinduism. Later, after division in Buddhism, Mahayana sect of Buddhism started the worship of Buddha’s idols. Many other corrupt activities in Buddhist community were also responsible for the decline of Buddhism during pre-medieval period. At the same time, the acceptance of Lord Buddha as an incarnation of Lord Vishnu in Hinduism was another cause behind the decline of Buddhism.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.52

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the last abbot of the Nalanda Mahavihara?
explanation: Rahula Shribhadra was the last abbot of the Nalanda Mahavihara. He was also the head of the department of Ayurveda. In his time, Bakhtiyar Khilji burnt and destroyed Nalanda Mahavihara.
source: ACF/RFO (Mains) Ist 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.53

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following about the features of Buddhist philosophy. (1) The seed of Buddhist philosophy is traced in the teachings of Gautama Buddha itself. (2) Buddha always emphasized on leading a moral life for the emancipation of human sufferings rather than indulging into philosophical problems. Which of the statements/s given above is/are correct?
explanation: The seed of Buddhist philosophy is traced in the teachings of Gautam Buddha. Buddha always emphasized on leading a moral life for the emancipation of human sufferings rather than indulging into philosophical problems. As per Buddha cause of sorrow is lack knowledge, jealousy and it can be overcome by following eight fold path. Thus, both the statements are correct.
source: Ancient & Medieval History GS · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.53

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The founder of Ajivaka sect was:
explanation: The founder of Ajivaka sect was ‘Makkhali Goshala Maskariputra, a friend of Mahavira’. Earlier he was the disciple and follower of Swami Mahavira Jain. Due to a misunderstanding with Mahavira Jain he left the Jain sect and established a new sect named as Ajivaka. Ajivakas believed that nothing is in the hand of human being, everything is predetermined. They were Niyativadin (believed in fate). Ajivakas believed in simple life and the use of meat and liquor was prohibited. They were fully dependent on begging.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1996 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.53

subject: AP & Indian History
question: "Live well, as long as you live. Live well even by borrowings, for, once cremated, there is no "return". This rejection of after-life is an aphorism of the:
explanation: It is Charvaka Philosophy which says that enjoy the life till the date you are alive. It is an atheistic Philosophy which does not believe in god, Vedas and reincarnation theory. It denies the existence of soul and salvation. It believes that fulfillment of human desire (kama) is the ultimate goal of life, therefore all acts of human being are aimed towards happiness and comfort of life. According to Charvaka Philosophy “Yavatjiveta Sukham Jivet, Rinam Litva Ghritam Piveta”.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.53

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The sect which believed in abiding nature of destiny-
explanation: Ajivakas believed in abiding nature of destiny. The initiator of Ajivaka sect was ‘Makkhali Goshal’. Earlier he was the disciple and follower of Swami Mahavir Jain. Due to a misunderstanding with Mahavir Jain, he left the Jain sect and established a new sect named as Ajivaka. Ajivakas believed that nothing is in the hand of human being, everything is predetermined. They were Niyativadians (believed in fate). Ajivakas believed in simple life and use of meat and liquor was prohibited B. Other Religious Sects

explanation: ‘Balaram’, the elder brother of Lord Krishna, is shown with plough in the arts. Plough was the weapon of Balaram.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In which chapter (Kand) of Ramayana there is mention about first meeting of Lord Ram and Hanuman?
explanation: ‘Ramayana’ also known as ‘Chaturvinshati Sahastri Samhita’ wasth composed by the Maharshi Valmiki in about 6 century B.C. Thereth are seven chapters (Kand) in this epic. In the 4 chapter of Ramayan (named as Kishkindha Kand) there is mention about the first meeting of Ram and Hanuman.
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. I Paper 2004 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.54

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Where is the ancient most mention about Devaki's son Krishna is found?
explanation: The ancient most mention about Krishna is found in Chandogya Upanishad. He is said to be the promoter of Bhagawat religion and also known as Vasudeva (being the son of Vasudeva). In Chhandogya upanishad he has been mentioned as the son of Devaki and the disciple of Ghor Angiras. He was equated with God Vishnu during Mahabharat period. Later after some time it was known as Vaishnavism and became popular in the Indian society during Gupta period. Gupta rulers declared it as state religion. Krishna belonged to Vrishni dynasty. It was Abhiras who initiated the worship of Krishna as a god and called Bhagawat.
source: UPPCS (Pre) Opt. History 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.54

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The Types of homage (Constancy) in Bhakti sect is :
explanation: There are 9 types of constancy (Homage) as described in Nardiya Bhakti Sutra. It is called ‘Navadhabhakti’/Navaratnamalika.
source: UP UDA/LDA (Pre) 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.54

subject: AP & Indian History
question: You have authority over Karma and not on result. It is said in which of the following scriptures?
explanation: ‘Karmanyevadhikaraste Ma Faleshu Kadachan’ the verse of Geeta (the part of Bhishma Parv of Mahabharat) says that it is the ‘Karma’ (The deed) which is in the hand of human being so do your job but do not think about the result as it is in control of supreme power ‘The God’. Gita further emphasize on enlightenment ‘Karma’ and Bhakti (constancy) for the attainment of ‘Moksha’ (to get rid of birth-death cycle).

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which incarnation of Vishnu is depicted as restoring the earth from sea?
explanation: Boar incarnation of lord Vishnu has been shown as saving the earth from the sea in sculpture art. A small figurine of an women has been shown as hanging in the teeth of boar as taking earth out from the sea. The best figurine of boar incarnation of lord Vishnu has been found in Udaygiri cave temple located in Madhya Pradesh.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. (Pre) 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.55

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Whose contribution was maximum in promotion of Bhagawat sect?
explanation: During Guptas regime the popularity of Bhagawat sect reached its climax. Gupta rulers declared Bhagawat (Vaisnav) sect as their state religion. They constructed various temples in Deogarh (Jhansi), Bhitargaon (Kanpur), Tigawa (Jabalpur). In fact the art of temple was found before the Gupta period. Gupta’s period is said to be the golden period of ancient India because there was a sign of growth in all the field during this period. The International relation of Gupta rulers with south east Asian region gave way for expansion of Vaishnav religion in these countries. ‘Heliodoras’ an ambassador of Greek ruler Antialcidas accepted the Bhagawat religion and established a pillar (Garun stambha) on the bank of river Betwa (Vetravati) and declared himself as ‘Param Bhagawat’. The name of ‘Vasudev’ is mentioned on the pillar. The Besnagar (Vidisha) pillar edict is the first archeological evidence of Bhagawat sect. The pillar was devoted to god Vishnu.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.55

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The Edict, which proved the influence of Bhagawat sect in Rajasthan is?
explanation: The early evidence of Bhagawat sect in Rajasthan is found from Ghosundi edict established in Nagari village in Chittorgarh (Rajasthan). The inscription gives detailed information about presence of Bhagawat religion as the name of Vasudeva Krishna and Balaram are mentioned on it. It also gives information about Ashwamedhast sacrifice by a king. The inscription belonged to the 1 century B.C. The edict was in Sanskrit language and Brahmi script.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The main Monastery (Peetha) of Varakari sect is located at:
explanation: The main monastery of Varakari sect was established in Pandharpur. The creator of this sect was Saint Gyaneshwar. He had compiled two books named as Gyaneshwari and Amritanubhav. The Pandharpur is located near Sholapur district of South Maharashtra. It was 700 years old sect.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.55

explanation: The names of the various Mahajanapadas were found in the literatures of that time. The list produced in various texts are different. Buddhist epic ‘Anguttara Nikaya’ and Jain epic 'Bhagwati Sutra' provide the list of 16 Mahajanapads. Anguttara Nikaya includes the name of – Anga, Magadha, Kashi, Koshala, Vatsa, Matsya, Kuru, Panchala, Avanti, Asmaka, Gandhara, Kamboja, Shurasena, Chedi, Vajji, Mal, etc. Anga, Magadha, Vajji, Kashi and Koshal are included in both Anguttara Nikaya as well as Bhagwati sutra. Panini (Parini) in his Ashtadhyayi has mentioned the name of 22 Mahajanapads namely–Magadha, Ashmaka, Kamboja, Gandhara, Sursen etc. 10 Mahajanapads were located in Ganga valley.

question: Arrange the following Magadha dynasties in chronological order : 1. Nanda dynasty 2. Shunga dynasty 3. Mauryan dynasty 4. Haryanka dynasty Select your answer from the codes given below:
explanation: The correct chronological order of the given dynasties is → Haryanka → Nanda → Mauryan → Shunga. Haryanka was the first ruling dynasty of Magadha established by Bimbisar in 544 B.C. The second ruling dynasty of Magadha was established by Shishunaga in 412 B.C. The third ruling dynasty of Magadha was Nanda dynasty established by Mahapadma Nanda in 344 B.C. In 321 B.C. Chandragupta Maurya had established Mauryan dynasty as the fourth ruling dynasty of Magadha. By killing the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha (Devvarman) in 185 BC, Pushyamitra Shunga established Shunga dynasty. He was a Brahmin commander of Brihadratha. He was said to be the protector of Vedic (Brahmin) culture and religion. His ruling period is recognized for the revival of Brahmin religion. Ancient History

explanation: Taxila, the capital city of Gandhara Empire during ancient India, was known for its strategic importance and worldwide known for study centre. Taxila was also a trade centre, basically for the trading with western world. Chanakya, Jivaka and Vasubandhu were among those who had studied in Takshashila University. Chanakya was also a teacher there. Takshashila was a major centre of art and craft too. Ancient town of Taxila located between Indus and Jhelum river, which is presently identified as Rawalpindi district of Pakistan. Ancient History
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.63

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which early ruler of Magadha had murdered his father for his coronation and later assassinated by his son for the same?
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S.2007,2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.63

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The name of Ajatashatru’s dynasty was?
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S. 2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.63

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which one among the followings was not contemporary to three others?
explanation: Bimbisara ( Magadh ruler), Prasenjit (ruler of Koshal) and Gautamth Buddha were the contemporary to each other (during6 century BC), while Menandernd (Milind) was an Indo-Greek ruler during the 2 century BC. A rock edict of Menander has been found from Reha (Kaushambi). He was the disciple of noted buddhist scholar Nagsen. A buddhist epic ‘Milinda Panho’ based on Minander and Nagsen conversation gives information about him.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2005 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.63

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During which of the followings ruling period the authority of Magadh expanded in Malwa region?
explanation: Shishunaga, the founder of Shishunaga dynasty had conquered Malwa (Avanti) to expand his territory of Magadha Empire up to Malwa, making it the western boundary of Magadha.
source: UP Lower (Pre) spl. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.63

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The early capital of Magadha was:
explanation: Primarily the capital of Magadha was Girivraja. Later Bimbisar’s architect Maha Govind constructed Rajgriha as new capital of Magadha. After some time during Udayin regime the capital of Magadha was transferred to Pataliputra.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2004-05,2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.63

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which Magadha ruler was known as ‘Aparoparashuram’?
explanation: Mahapadmananda (Magadha ruler of Nanda dynasty) was also known as Aparoparashuram and Sarvakshatrantak (Re-incarnation of Parshuram). He also owned the titles of Ekarat and Ekachhatra.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. (Pre) 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.64

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which one of the followings was not the Magadha capital?
explanation: Girivraja, Pataliputra and Rajgriha were the Magadha's capitals for different span of time, whereas Kaushambi was the capital of Vatsa.
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S. 2010-11 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.64

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Depiction of which God is found on Yaudheya coins?
explanation: Yaudheya coins are found in large numbers from Rohtak which indicates that the mint of Yaudheya rulers was in Rohtak only. The figurine of Kartikeya is found on Yaudheya coins. Yaudheyand republic was located in north-west India during the 2 century AD, in the valley of Yamuna and Sutlej rivers. Panini has recognized Yaudheya as warrior community (Ayudha- jivi). Yaudheya coins have been found from Yamuna – Sutlej region, basically in Rohtak district of Haryana.
source: UPPCS (Mains) Spl. 1st G.S.2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.64

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which one of the following was initially the most powerful city of India in the 6th century B.C.?
explanation: The most powerful states in 6th century B. C. were Magadha, Kosala, Vats and Avanti but Magadha was considered as the most powerful among them.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S.1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.64

subject: AP & Indian History
question: By whom the first republic of the world ‘Vaishali; was established?
explanation: The first Republic state of the worldth was established by Licchavi at Vaishali during 6 century BC. Kautilya has recognized Licchavians as Rajshastropajivi community. Here Buddha delivered his last sermon and he informed his disciples about his impending Mahaparinivana and his desire to visit the Kushinagar (Kusavati) the capital of the Mallas.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2007-08 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.64

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Inscriptional evidences reveal that a canal was excavated on the order of Nanda King, in:
explanation: According to Hathigumpha inscription of Kharvela, Nanda ruler had ordered for the construction of (digging) a canal in Kalinga. The timing of this canal was about 344 BC. Kharvela had expanded this canal up to Ancient History 7 his capital. This inscription gives information up to 13 years of Kharvela regime. This is the only evidence about the Kharvela. Hathigumpha Inscription is found from Udayagiri Hills. Kharvela was related to Chedi dynasty.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.64

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Kalinga ruler Kharvela was associated with which dynasty?
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S.1st paper 2015 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.64

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The fable of Udayan-Vasavadutta is associated with:
explanation: The fable of Udayan-Vasavadatta is found in 'Swapnavasavadutta' a dramatic act of Mahakavi Bhas. It contains the love story of Udayan ‘King of Vatsa’ and Vasavadutta (the princess of Ujjain). She was the daughter of Chand Pradyot. Udayan was also a great veena player.
source: UP Lower (Pre) spl.2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.64

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In Mahabharata by what name were the Kuninda-kings known ?
explanation: Kuninda was an ancient kingdom located in modern state of Uttrakhand. There is mention about Kuninda state in Mahabaharata, where the kings of Kuninda were recognized as Dwij Shreshta. A Kuninda king had given a conch to Yudhisthir.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) G.S.2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.64

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the founder of the Nanda Dynasty in Magadha?
explanation: The founder of Nanda dynasty in Magadha was Mahapadmananda. He was also known as Ugrasena. The initial capital of Magadha was Girivraja or Rajgriha. It covered the modern districts of Patna, Gaya, Shahabad of Bihar. It was bordered by River Ganga from North and Son River from South.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) G.S.2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.64

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What is the rate of land revenue in theological epics?
explanation: Theth rate of land revenue in theological epics was about 1/6 of actual production.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1995 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.64

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Jeevaka, a famous physician during Gautam Buddha period was associated with whose court?
explanation: Jeevaka was a great physician (Ayurvedacharya) in the court of Bimbisara during Buddha period. When the ruler of Avanti Chand Pradyota was suffering with Jaundice, Bimbisar had sent Jeevak for the treatment. Jeevak was the son of a courtesan (Prostitute) name ‘Salavati’.
source: UP UDA/LDA (Pre) 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.64

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following is NOT one of the nine Nandas as described in Mahabodhivamsa.
explanation: The nine Nanda rulers mentioned in the Mahabodhivamsa are Mahapadma Nanda Panduka, Pandugati, Bhootpala, Rashtrapala Gobishanaka, Dashasiddhaka, Kaybarta and Dhana Nanda. Therefore, it is clear that there are no Mahanandins in the Nanda dynasty. Mahapadma Nanda ended the Shishunaga dynasty and ruled the Magadha Empire in 344 BC. In the Puranas he has been called Mahapadma and in the Mahabodhi dynasty, Ugrasen. According to the Puranas, the first king of the Nanda dynasty was Mahapadmananda.
source: UPPSC ACF Mains Paper I 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.65

subject: AP & Indian History
question: From where did the Iranians and Greek come?
explanation: Iranians and Greek came from North west.
source: Sikkim PSC (Pre) 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.65

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The correct chronological order of the following foreign invasions in India is ..........
explanation: The correct chronological order of the following foreign invasions in India is Greeks, Shakas, Parthians, Kushanas.
source: GUJARAT PSC CIVIL PRE-PAPER-I (21-3-2021) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.65

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The Indo-Greek kingdom set up in north Afghanistan in the beginning of the second century BC was:
explanation: ‘Bactria’ was an Indo-Greek statend established in North Afghanistan during early 2 century BC. After death of Alexander in 323 BCE, many Greeks came to settle on north-western borders of India, with northern part of Afghanistan, at that time which was known as Bactria. Ancient History
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.65

subject: AP & Indian History
question: From the third century AD when the Huna invasion ended the Roman Empire, the Indian merchants relied more and more on the:
explanation: During the 3rd century CE when Roman empire was on decline due to the Huna’s invasions the Indian traders relied maximum on south-east Asia for their trade activities. Hunas were nomadic people who lived in Central Asia, in the Caucasusth andth Eastern region of Europe between the 4 and the 6 Century AD.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.65

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Followings were the basic causes behind the success of Alexander in India: 1. There was no central power in India at that time 2. His army was excellent 3. He got the help from anti-national rulers 4. He was a great administrator Choose the correct answer from the codes given below :
explanation: There was political instability in north-west frontier region of India during that period. There were various small states in the region and indulged in internal disputes. There was lack of unity among them which gave chance for foreign invaders to interfere and taking advantage of situation. Alexander got help from anti-national ruler such as Ambi of Taxila Foreign invaders not only invaded India but also established their hold in the region. Thus, lack of a strong central power, help from dissident Indian rulers and better military management were basic causes behind the success of Alexander (Sikander) in India. Alexander was a great conquer but not as goods administrator.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2001 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.65

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to the invaders in ancient India, which one of the following is the correct chronological order?
explanation: Cyrus II, the founder of Hakhamani empire in Iran was saidth to be the first Persian invader of India, during the 6 century BC, but there is lack of information about his conquest in Indian territory. Therefore, the first Greek invader of India was Alexander the great in 326 BC. He was the son of Phillip II of Macedonia. After the decline of Mauryan empire there was instability in north-west frontier region of India. Taking advantage of the situation Shaka invader ‘Maus’ reign (98/50BC-60/57BC) invaded India, making it second foreign invasion on India. Gandhar became the part of his empire as capital in Taxila. Pallava and Kushans were the next to invade India. Thus the correct chronological order of foreign invasions on India is: – Greek-Shaka-Pallav-Kushan-Arab-Turkish.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.65

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which one of the following dynasties was ruling over North India at the time of Alexander's invasion?
explanation: At the time of Alexander’s invasion on India, Nanda dynasty was ruling over North India. Dhanananda was the ruler of Magadh at that time, also called as Agrammees or Xandrames by Greek writers. the year of attack was 326 BCE and Dhananad was last ruler of Nanda dynasty.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2000 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.66

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the followings king of Magadha was contemporary to Alexander?
source: BPSC (Pre) 2000-01 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.66

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following did not come to India with Alexander?
explanation: Many great scholars accompanied Alexander during his campaigns such as Nearchus, Onesicritus, Aristobulus while Deimmachus was ambassador to the court of the Mauryan ruler Bindusara.
source: UPPCS (Pre) Re-Exam G.S. 2015 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.66

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A) : After two years expedition Alexander left India. Reason (R) : He was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below: Code:
options: A & R both is true and R is correct explanation to A
A & R both are true but R is not correct explanation to A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: After two years of long operation in Indian region Alexander returned back to his kingdom in 325 BC due to refusal of his army to move ahead. While in the way to his kingdom he died in Babylon in 323 BC. Thus the statement I is true but the second statement is wrong .It is said that Chandragupta had met Alexander once but no evidence of clash is found between the two.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S 1998 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.66

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The women of which Indian tribe or kingdom had taken up arms against Alexander, after a large number of its soldiers had been killed or wounded in the battle field?
explanation: After the death of Army men in the battle with Alexander’s army, the women of Ashwak republic raised the weapons to fight against Alexander’s Greek army. The capital of Ashwak republic was ‘Massaga’. Ancient History
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. Ist Paper 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.66

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the followings addressed our country as India?
explanation: It was the Greeks who called Sindhu river as ‘Indus’. They called the people residing in the region as ‘Indus people’. Thus the region belonged to Indus people which was called India by the Greeks.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.66

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Name that brave Indian ruler who was defeated by Alexander on the Jhelum river bank?
explanation: It was ‘Porus’ the ruler of Paurav kingdom located between Jhelum (vitasta) and Chenab river in north west frontier region of India, who resisted Alexander and restricted his movement further. The battle between the two is famous as the battle of Vitasta or the battle of Hydaspes in 326 BC. It is notable that two Indian rulers Ambhi and Shashi Gupta had rendered their support to Alexander. Though Porus was defeated by Alexander but as a mark of respect for his bravery Alexander had returned his territory adding some other regions with Paurav kingdom.
source: UP RO/ARO (M) 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.66

subject: AP & Indian History
question: First Persian ruler who established his control on some part of India:
explanation: Darius I was the first Persian ruler who conquered some regions in Indian Territory. Information about it is found from the inscriptions of Darius I found from Behistun, Persipolis and Naqsh-e- Rustam. He conquered the Indus valley regions at first and later occupied Kamboj and Gandhar regions too.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 1994-95 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.66

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which Chinese general had defeated Kanishka?
explanation: Chinese ruler ‘Pan Chao’ had defeated Kanishka initially while in the next war Kanishka had defeated Chinese army and established his hold on most part of central Asian region. Kanishka was the first Indian ruler whose kingdom expanded from south Asia to central Asia and west Asia. It is notable that maximum coins of Kanishka were inscripted in Greek and Persian language and scripted in the first century AD.
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) G.S. 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.66

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following Indo-Greek ruler had circulated lead coins?
explanation: Indo-Greek ruler Strato II who ruled India during 25 BCE to 10 CE had circulated lead coins at first. The coins were Apollo/tripod types.
source: UPPCS Kanoongo Exam, 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.66

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Ma Rulers (Chandragupta Maurya, Bindusara, Ashoka A. (The Great), Heirs of Ashoka) 1. Which of the following Rock Edict of Ashoka speaks of religious synthesis?
explanation: Rock Edict – XII of Ashoka speaks of religious synthesis. It asked people to Respect other sects and not take pride in their own. 2. Consider the following pairs: Site of Ashoka's Location in the major rock edicts State of 1. Dhauli — Odisha 2. Erragudi — Andhra Pradesh 3. Jaugada — Madhya Pradesh
source: UPPCS Pre 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.67

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Kalsi — Karnataka How many pairs given above are correctly matched?
explanation: The correct match is as follows :- Site of Ashoka's Location in the major rock edicts State of Dhauli - Odisha Erragudi - Andhra Pradesh Jaugada - Odisha Kalsi - Uttarakhand
source: UPSC IAS 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.67

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Assertion (A): In Ashoka’s time, Bherighosa was replaced with Dhammaghosha Reason (R): After Ashoka acceded to the throne, Ashoka fought a major war called the Kalinga War. Choose the correct one.
options: Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: During the 8th year of Ashoka's reign, he won the Kalinga war. But due to large state devastation Ashoka felt remorse and hence he abandoned the policy of Territorial annexation and adapted the policy of cultural conquest, which is considered as replacement of Bherighosha with Dhammaghosha. Hence, Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanations of A.
source: J & K PSC Pre 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.67

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following Rock Edict of Ashoka speaks of religious synthesis?
options: Rock Edict – II Ancient History 7 aurya Dynasty Ruler
explanation: Rock Edict – XII of Ashoka speaks of religious synthesis. It asked people to respect other sects and not take pride in their own.
source: UPPSC (Pre) 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.67

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following statement/s refer/s to the Persian influence on ancient India? (I) Introduction of Brahmi script (II) Hair washing ceremony of Chandragupta Maurya. (III) Introduction of lion replica on Ashoka pillars
explanation: In accordance with Persian custom, which had much influence upon the Indian court and administration, the king ceremonially washed his hair on his birthday, which was celebrated by a splendid festival. Introduction of lion replica on Ashoka pillars are a symbol of power, courage confidence and pride mounted on a circular base.
source: GUJARAT PSC CIVIL PRE-PAPER-I (21-3-2021) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.67

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who had constructed the Sudarshan Lake?
explanation: Sudarshan Lake was constructed by Pushyagupta Vaishya, the Governor of Saurashtra under Chandragupta Maurya.
source: UK RO-ARO (Pre.) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.67

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Ashoka won the Avanti Mahajanpad and merged in the Mauryan Empire during Bindusara ruled. What text does it refer to?
explanation: The merger of Avanti Mahajanpad into Magadh Empire by Ashoka was mentioned in Samant Pasadika of Buddha Ghosh. It was a translation of Sinhala commentaries into Pali
source: MPPCS (Pre.) 2020 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.67

subject: AP & Indian History
question: How many years after his coronation did Emperor Ashoka conquered Kalinga?
explanation: Emperor Ashoka conquered Kalinga eight years after his coronation. Ashoka was an ambitious ruler whose coronation took place in 269 BC, and the war of Kalinga happened in 261 BC. The Kalinga war inspired Ashoka to dedicate his life to non-violence and religion, as a result of which he adopted the Dhamma.
source: UPPSC ACF Mains Paper I 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.68

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following sources indicate that the last Mauryan ruler Brihadrath was assassinated by Pushyamitra?
explanation: In 186 BCE, northwestern India (parts of modern-day Afghanistan and Pakistan) was occupied by the Greco-Bactrian King Demetrius (Sharmamita), followed by the overthrow of the Mauryan dynasty by the General Pushymitra Shunga. The Mauryans had diplomatic alliances with the Greeks and they may have been considered as allies by the Greco-Bactrians. Brihadratha was a weak ruler and his Senapati Pushyamitra Shunga while parading the entire Mauryan army before Brihadratha to show him the strength of the army assassinated him and this was the end of the Mauryas. Pushyamitra Shunga founded the Shunga dynasty in around 185-183 BC.
source: OPSC (OCS) Pre 2021 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.68

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following Ashokan inscriptions indicates that he did not abolish the Capital Punishment?
explanation: Ashoka built 7 Major Pillar Edicts. These are found at Topra (Delhi), Meerut, Kaushambi, Rampurva, Champaran, Mehrauli List of these 7 major pillar edicts is as follows: Pillar-I - Principles of protection of people. Pillar-II - Defines Dhamma. Pillar III - Abolishes sins of harness, anger, cruelty etc. Pillar IV - Deals with responsibilities and functions of Rajukas. Pillar-V - List of animal and birds which should not be killed. Pillar-VI - Dhamma Policy G. Pillar-VII - Work done by Ashoka for Dhamma. Note:- Pillar edict IV of Ashoka indicates that he did not abolished capital punishment.
source: OPSC Pre-2020 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.68

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which script was introduced in South India by Ashoka?
explanation: Brahmi script was found in the inscriptions of the Ashoka, the Mauryan emperor. It was introduced in South India by Ashoka.
source: Kerala (KAS) PSC-2020 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.68

subject: AP & Indian History
question: A Bilingual Inscription of Ashoka was found near :
explanation: A bilingual inscription of Ashoka was found on the mountain side of the Chil Zena outcrop on the western side of the city of Kandahar. The Kandhar Bilingual Rock Inscription is famous bilingual edict in Greek and Aramaic, proclaimed and carved in stone by the Indian Mauryan Empire ruler Ashoka around 260 BCE.
source: Nagaland NCS Prelime-2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.68

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements are correct regarding Maurya dynasty? (1) Chandra Gupta Maurya, the founder of the Mauryan dynasty, was the first emperor to unite most of India under one administration. (2) Kautilya was instrumental in helping Chandragupta Maurya overthrow the powerful Nanda dynasty at Pataliputra, in the Magadha region. (3) Bindusara, son of Chandragupta Maurya, extended the empire into central and parts of southern India. (4) The last Mauryan king was killed by his general-in-chief, Pushyamitra, who founded the Shunga dynasty.
explanation: Maurya dynasty was founded by Chandragupta Maurya around 322 BCE. Three famous rulers of the Mauryan dynasty who took the glory of the Mauryan empire to peak were Chandragupta Maurya, Bindusara and Ashoka. • The Capital city of the Mauryan Empire was Pataliputra (Present day Patna). • Chanakya convinced his disciple, Chandragupta Maurya, to conquer the kingdom of Magdha (The Nanda Empire) when he was insulted by Dhanananda. • The last Mauryan king was killed by his general-in- chief, Pushyamitra, Sunga. Later he founded his own Kingdom Shunga dynasty.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-2019 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.68

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Assertion (A) : Ashoka annexed Kalinga to the Mauryan Empire. Reason (R) : Kalinga controlled the land and sea routes to South India. Codes:
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
explanation: Kalinga Victory resulted in a large scale of bloodshed in the history of Magadha and India . This war culminated the policy of conquest and imperial expansion that Bimbisara started by conquering Anga province. Ashoka attacked Kalingath in the eighth year of his coronation in 261 BC.The 13 great inscription of Ashoka describes the Kalinga war and the destruction there. Kalinga was extremely important in Ancient India in terms of political, economic, geographical as well as strategically. For this reason, Ashoka’s Kalinga expedition was aimed at seizing the terrestrial and maritime trade route. He conquered and annexed Kalinga to his empire.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2000 UP Lower (Pre) 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.68

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The rulers of which dynasty had established diplomatic relations with the far western countries like Syria?
explanation: According to Greek sources the Mauryan king Bindusara established diplomatic relation with Greek king Antiochus. Antiochus had sent Deimachus as his ambassador to Bindusara's court.
source: UPPCS (Pre) Opt. History 2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.69

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Turamaya, contemporary to Ashoka was the ruler of :
explanation: The 13th major rock edict of Ashoka's mentions the Dhamma Victory over Greek Kings Antiochus of Syria (Antiyoko), Ptolemy of Egypt (Turamaye), Magas of Cyrene (Maka), Antigonus of Macedonia (Amtikini), Alexander of Epirus (Alika Sundar).
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2012 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.69

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In which year Chandragupta Maurya defeated Seleucus?
explanation: Chandragupta defeated Seleucus around 305- 303 BCE and Seleucus was compelled to yield Herat Arachosia (Kandhar), Gedrosia (Makran Coast) and Parapomisadai (Kabul) to Chandragupta in return of 500 elephants.
source: UP RO/ARO (M) 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.69

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Seleucus, to which Alexander had appointed as administrater of Sindha and Afghanistan, was defeated by which Indian ruler?
explanation: Seleucus, to which Alexander had appointed as administrater of Sindha and Afghanistan, was defeated by Chandragupta.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.69

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Ptolemy Philadelphus, with whom Ashoka had established diplomatic relation was the ruler of :
explanation: Pliny mentions that King Ptolemy-II Philadelphus of Egypt sent Dionysius as his ambassador to India. Ptolemy had established a library in Alexandria which aimed to protect translated Indian epics.
source: UP UDA/LDA (Pre) 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.69

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the ruler of Egypt contemporary to Ashoka?
explanation: Turamaya also known as Ptolemy II Philadelfous was the contemporary ruler of Egypt till 247 BC. He was the ruler during the period of Ashoka and had accepted the supremacy of Ionians.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) Opt. History 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.69

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following region was not the part of Ashokan Empire?
explanation: Sri Lanka was not the part of Ashoka’s empire while Afganistan, Bihar and Kalinga were the part of Magadh empire during the Ashoka regime.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1997-98 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.69

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who established the parity of Sandrocottas with Chandragupta Maurya?
explanation: It was William Jones who established the parity of Sandrocottas with Chandragupta Maurya for the first time.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2007-08 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.69

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following is the Ancient dynasty?
explanation: Among the given option the oldest ancient dynasty of India was Mauryan dynasty established by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 B.C.
source: Uttarakhand Lower (Pre) 2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.69

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The name of which ruler is mentioned in edicts as 'Piyadassi' and 'Devanampiya'?
explanation: The name of Ashoka is mentioned in edicts as Piyadassi and Devanampiya. Devanampiya means "Beloved of Gods" and Piyadassi means, who regards others with Kindness or Humane.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. Ist Paper 2015 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.69

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The ancient form of modern Devanagari script is:
explanation: The ancient form of Devanagari script was ‘Brahmi’. Brahmi script was written from left to right.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.69

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who established the monarchy in ancient Indian based on tri-principles of tolerance, liberty and compassion?

subject: AP & Indian History
question: According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, which of the following are correct? 1. A person could be a slave as a result of a judicial punishment. 2. If a female slave bore her master a son, she was legally free. 3. If a son born to a female slave was fathered by her master, the son was entitled to the legal status of the master's son. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: The Arthashastra is an Indian treatise on politics, economics, military strategy, the function of the state, and social organization attributed to Kautilya (also known as Chanakya). He was instrumental in establishing the reign of the great king Chandragupta Maurya (321-297 BCE). There were variety of protection offered to the slaves, especially to the women slaves. As per the Arthashastra, when a child is begotten on a female slave by her master, both the child and its mother shall at once be recognised as free. A person could be a slave as a result of a judicial punishment. If a son born to a female slave was fathered by her master, the son was entitled to the legal status of the master's son. So, statement 2 and statement 3 are correct.
source: UPSC (Pre)-2022, Paper -1 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.71

The farming on these lands was done by slaves, workers, tribes & prisoners, etc. The earning from Sitaland was called 'Sita Income' while revenue earned from peasants was called ‘BHAG’. (2) The last Sunga King, Devabhuti was assassinated by his Brahmana Minister Vasudeva Kanva who ascended the throne. (3) The last Ruler of Kanva dynasty was deposed by Andhras
explanation: Brihadratha was the last ruler of the Mauryan Empire. He ruled from 187 to 180 BCE, when he was killed by his general, Pushyamitra Shunga, who went on to establish the Shunga Empire. question: Which of the following Kings is credited to have issued gold coins for the first time?
explanation: Indo-Greek ruler ‘Antiochus’ was the first to circulate gold coins in India. He belonged to Demetrias dynasty, established Sialkot as his capital. Indo-Greek rulers are also credited for the circulation of inscripted coins. The timing of circulation of coins, the figurine of Greek god and goddess and the portrait of ruling monarch were inscripted on coins. The most popular ruler of this dynasty was Menander who never issued gold coins. It was Vima Kadphises of Kushan dynasty who restarted the circulation of gold coins. Afterwards the other rulers of Kushan dynasty circulated gold coins in bulk, on regular basis. Kushan rulers are also credited for the circulation of pure gold coins. It is notable that maximum gold coins in India were issued by Gupta dynasty.

explanation: Kushana ruler Vima Kadphises first issued gold coins on a large scale nearly in 100 B.C. Kushans were the migrants of central Asia also known as Yuchi and Tocharians. They came to India and resided in north west region of India and Afganistan and established a big empire extended from Khurasan (central Asia) to Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh. Their territorial expansion was from Iran to Afghanistan, total Pakistan and whole of northern India. Kushan rulers had controlled silk route connecting China (central Asia) to western region of Roman empire and established full control over the trade route (Silk route)of Afghanistan to Iran which was a major source of income for the Kushans. They were trading via Persian Bay and Red Sea. They were credited for the circulation of gold coins on regular basis at large scale in India. It is notable that gold coins in India were circulated by Indo-Greek rulers. There are no evidence of naval power of Kushan rulers. Vima Kadphises was the father of Kanishka.

question: The unique feature of whose administrative system was the development of village autonomy?
explanation: The unique feature of administrative system of the Cholas was the development of village autonomy. There was a remarkable autonomy at the village level during Cholas period. Chola officials participated in the village administration more as observers than as administrators. There were three assemblies called the Ur, Sabha or Mahasabha and Nagaram. 1. The Ur was a general assembly of the village. The Ur consisted of all the tax-paying residents of an ordinary village. The Ur was opened to all male adults but was dominated by the elder members. 2. The Sabha was apparently an exclusively Brahmin assembly of the Brahmadeya villages. The Sabha had more complex machinery, which functioned largely through its committees called the Variyams. Election to the executive body and other committees of the Ur and Sabha appears to have been conducted by drawing lots from among those who were eligible.

explanation: Chola dynasty was known for its specific local and village level administration in ancient Indian history. The villages during this period were administered through democratically formed village Govt. Thus the concept of local self govt. could be seen there during Chola regime. There were three types of villages called ‘Ur’, ‘Sabha' or 'Mahasabha’ and 'Nagaram'. The working committee of ‘Ur’ was known as ‘Alunganam’ or Ganam. Sabha or Mahasabha was related to ‘Agrahar villages’(Brahmin dwelt) and ‘Perugurri’ was the working committee of Sabha. Its members were called ‘Perumakkal’. The administration of these villages was managed by a Indian Geography 9 committee called ‘Variyams’. The members were called ‘Variyaperumakkal’. It was notable that the villages were divided in 30 wards also called Kudumbu. The members were elected for one years. The eligibility criteria to be the member was 35 years of age, owner of 1.5 acres of land, having his own home and knowledge of Vedic hymn. Followings were the main committees of village administration. The inscriptions of Ganga rulers was found from here, provide the list of commodities traded from this port.

subject: AP & Indian History

explanation: Nanadesis were the institutions in south India which belonged to Foreign Trade. They were a guild of traders who organized themselves into one of the biggest trading associations at the time of the Hoysala Empire.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The capital of Kadamba Kings was:
explanation: Banavasi (Vaijayanti) was the capital of Kadamba dynasty (345-540 CE). It was located in North Kannda district of modern Karnataka state. Founder of this dynasty was Mayursharman. He is credited for 18 Ashwamedha Yajnas.

question: Which one of the following was a corporation of merchants in ancient India?
explanation: There were various trading communities in ancient Indian period, organized on the basis of their class, nature of work, and the area of business activities. Manigramam, Nanadesi, Balenjiar, Endaamai, and Telin were the known trade communities. Manigramam were the traders organization engaged in local trade while Nanadesis were involved in outside trade. Ashtadiggaj was referred to as the group of eight Telugu poets in the court of Krishna Dev Rai, ‘the ruler of Tuluva dynasty of Vijay Nagar empire. Chaturvedi Mangalam was referred to Brahmin villages in South India.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1997 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.91

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following King is known to have sent his Ministers to suppress the cruelty against animal in Kashi region?
explanation: Kumarapala (1143-1172) was a follower of Jainism. He was a strong supporter of non-violence. Jain Acharya Hemchandra was his courtier. Kumarapala banned the killing of animals in his empire. He sent a convoy of his ministers to Kashi to stop and ban the cruelty against animals happening over there. •••• Kumarapala belongs to Chalukya dynasty of Gujarat and also known as Solankis. The dynasty of Gujarat Chalukya ended with the attack of Alauddin Khilji who conquered Gujarat and its capital was known as Anhilwara. It is also said that Kumarapala rebuilt the Somnath temple.
source: UPPCS RO-ARO (Mains) 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.93

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following had provided fund for the reconstruction of a damaged mosque in Khambhat region?
explanation: Jaisinmha Siddharaj (1094-1143 AD) the Chalukya ruler of Gujarat, had provided fund for the reconstruction of a damaged mosque in Khambhat region. He was the son of Karna. Famous Jain Acharya Hemchandra was his courtier. Kumarpala was an Indian king from Chaulukya dynasty of Gujarat. His capital was Anahilapataka (modern Patan).
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2007/1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.93

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who overthrow the Rashtrakutas in 973 AD?
explanation: In 973 CE, the Rashtrakuta dynasty was overthrown by Taila II a feudatory of Krish III. Tailapa II, also known as Taila II, was the founder of western Chalukya Dynasty in Southern India. The records of Tailapa's dynasty trace his patrilineal ancestry to the Chalukyas of Vatapi and also connect him to the Rashtrakutas of Manyakheta and the Kalachuries of Chedi through matrilineal descent. Tailapa married a Rashtrakuta princess Jakavve, the daughter of Bhammaha Ratta, possibly to strengthen his political position. B. Rashtrakuta Dynasty
source: OPSC (OCS) Pre 2021 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.93

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following laid the foundation of Rashtrakuta Empire?
explanation: Dantidurga was the founder of Rashtrakuta dynasty in 753 century AD. He made his capital in Manyakheta. Dantidurga is credited for organizing ‘Hiranyagarbha (Mahadan) yajyan’ in Ujjain.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S.2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.93

question: Who among the following was born in a military camp in the course of his father’s campaign?
explanation: Rashtrakuta ruler Amoghavarsha was born in Military camp while his father Govind III was returning from his campaign of northern India. Amoghavarsha was a great patron of scholars. Writer of, Aadi Puran- Jinsen, Ganit Sar Sangrah-Mahaviracharya and Shaktayana were in the court of Amoghavarsha. He himself had authored two epics namely, Kaviraj marg and Prashnottar Malika in Kannad language. Kumudendu, the writer of ‘Siribhuvalaya’ and a jain muni was the mentor of Amoghavarsha.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S.1 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.93

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements are correct? (1) Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna-I had constructed the famous Kailash Temple of Ellora. (2) During Rashtrakuta Rule Loksen had written 'Mahapurana'. (3) 400 dancers were in Rajrajeshwar temple of Tanjore (4) Kamban's 'Ramavataram' is considered the great epic of Tamil.
explanation: Krishna-I (756-774 CE), built the rock temple of Kailasa at Ellora (designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983). • Mahapurana or Trishashthilkshana Mahapurana is a major Jain text composed largely by Acharya Jinasena during the rule of Rashtrakuta ruler Amoghvarsha and completed by his pupil Gunabhadra in 9th century CE. • The Rajarajesvaram temple at Thanjavur, popularly called the Brihadisvara or the Big Temple had on its roll 400 accomplished dancers at the time of Raja Raja Chola called 'Talippendir to perform dances during daily rituals and in festival processions. It also employed 240 musicians. • Ramavataram popularly referred to as Kamba Ramayanam is a Tamil epic that was written by Kamban during the 12th century. Note- Gujarat PSC has given option (d) as its answer, but point no. (ii) needs correction which is Mahapurana is a major Jain text composed largely by Acharya Jinasena during the ruler of Rashtrakuta ruler Amoghavarsha and completed by his pupil Gunabhadhra. the completed and edited text was released by Lokasena, pupil of Gunabhadra. C. Pallava Dynasty
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-2019 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.93

subject: AP & Indian History
question: At which place the Kailasanatha Temple was built by the Pallavas?
explanation: The Kailasanatha temple was built by the Pallavas in Kanchi. It was Pallava king Narasimha Varman II who built the Kailasanatha temple around 700 CE.
source: Nagaland NCS Prelime-2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.94

explanation: The correct match is as follows:- (Pallavan Ruler) (Political event) Sivaskandavarman Kanchi came under the Pallavas Vishnugopa Samudragupta's Invasion Narasimhavarman-III Defeat of Pulakesin-II and destruction of Vatapi city Nandivarman-II Defeated by Vikramaditya-II and city of Kanchi was captured

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The architectural splendor Bhima Ratha was built by ______
explanation: Bhima Ratha is a monument in the Pancha Rathas complex at Mahabalipuram on the coromandel coast of the Bay of Bengal, in the Kanchipuram district of the state of Tamil Nadu, India. • It is an example of monolith Indian rock-cut architecture. Pallav king Mahendravarman and his son Narasimhavarman I (630-680 AD) build this monument.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-2019 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.94

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which inscription proved that pallavas replaced the Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri?
options: The Manchikallu inscription of pallava Simhavarman
explanation: The inscription that proved that Pallavas replaced the Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri is the Manchikallu inscription of Pallava Simhavarman. The Manchikallu inscription was found at Manchikallu, Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh. The characters in the inscription are of Southern Brahmi, the predecessor of Telugu - Kannada script, and are written in Prakrit language. The inscription belongs to Simhavarma I of the Pallava dynasty and is dated as 320 CE.
source: APPSC Group-II Screening-2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.94

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following King did send two naval expenditions to Ceylon in 642 AD?
explanation: Narasimhavarman-I (630-638), a Pallava king sent two sea Campaigns against the Simhal Island (Present Shri Lanka). He built the famous five chariot temples in Mahabalipuram. These temples are built through carving out of a single rock and named after five Pandavas. •••• He was known as Narasimha Varman Mahamalla/Mamalla. He defeated Pulkeshin-II of Vatapi and assumed the title ‘Vatapikonda’.
source: UPPCS RO-ARO (Mains) 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.94

explanation: Kanchi Ghatika was a famous educational institute during the Pallava period, situated at Kanchipuram. The Pallava rulers were famous for patronizing learning.

explanation: The Varika Vishnuvardhan Victory Tower of Bayana Fort belongs to Gupta Period. This monolithic red sand stone pillar was created by Vishnuvardhan after the completion of Pundarika Yojana.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The iron pillar established in the courtyard of Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque in the memory of-
options: Anagpal Ancient History 10 nd Vakataka Dynasty
explanation: The iron pillar established in the courtyard of Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque located within Qutub Minar complex, Delhi is said to be in the memory of Gupta ruler Chandragupta II. The pillar is famous for its non-rusted state, despite being made of 99% iron. It was originally erected during the rule of Chandra and bears his inscription in Sanskrit. This king 'Chandra' has been identified as Chandragupta II (375AD-413AD) of the Gupta dynasty. This pillar was moved to its Present location by Anangpal Tomar in 11th Century AD.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.95

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statement (s) is/are correct? (i) In the Junagarh Rock Inscription Samudragupta claims to have got the Lake Sudarshana repaired (ii) In the Mehrauli Iron Pillar inscription Chandragupta-II is said to have set up the pillar in honour of god Vishnu or Vishnupadagiri (iii) Eran Pillar inscription dated Gupta year 191 is the earliest epigraphic record of Sati pratha in India
explanation: The Junagarh inscription gives the information about the Sudarshan lake that the lake was an artificial reservoir, was built by the Mauryan emperors for checking floods. Around 150 AD, the lake was repaired by the Shaka ruler Rudradaman-I. And, it was again repaired under the Skandgupta’s reign (415 AD- 455 AD) by his governor Parnadatta. The Mehrauli Pillar inscription belongs to the period of the Guptas. The Mehrauli Iron Pillar inscription mentions Chandragupta Vikramaditya’s authority over Northwestern India. This Pillar was established by Chandragupta as Vishnupada in the honour of Lord Vishnu. The first epigraphic evidence of Sati has been found from Eran Pillar inscription of Bhanugupta, Madhya Pradesh in the Gupta period in 510 AD.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-26.12.21 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.95

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements is/are correct? (I) Bhatarka, the founder of the Maitraka dynasty of Vallabhi was appointed as commander-in-chief in Gujarat by the imperial Guptas. (II) The Eran stone pillar inscription mentions 'famous battle' between the Guptas and the Maitrakas. (III) The Vallabhi ruler Dhruvasena II was a contemporary of Budhagupta.
explanation: Maitrakath dynastyth had ruled in Gujarat and Saurashtra from 5 to 8 century CE. Its founder, Bhatarka was a General of Skandagupta taking advantage of the decay of the Gupta empire, established himself as ruler of Gujarat and Saurashtra with Vallabhi as his capital. The Eran stone pillar inscription mentions battle between Guptas and the Maitrakas. Bhanugupta is known from a stone pillar inscription in Eran, Malwa. The Vallabhi ruler Dhruvasena II was not a contemporary of Budhagupta but a contemporary of Harsha Vardhana. According to Nausari copper plate inscription, he was defeated by Harsha Vardhana.
source: GUJARAT PSC CIVIL PRE-PAPER-I (21-3-2021) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.96

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the Gupta Rulers was first to bear higher political title of Maharajadhiraja?
explanation: The first Gupta ruler to assume the title of Maharajadhiraja was Chandragupta I (319-335 CE), who had ruled in northern India. The founder of the Gupta dynasty was Srigupta. He was succeeded by Ghatotkacha. Chandragupta was also the father of Samudragupta, his next successor. Samudragupta's successor Chandragupta-II, also known as Vikramaditya, conquered the extensive territories of Malwa, Gujarat and Kathiawar. Chandragupta I, son and successor of Ghatokacha married a Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi to strengthen his position.
source: OPSC (OCS) Pre 2021 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.96

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following parts of India was NOT included in the empire of Samudra Gupta?
explanation: Samudra Gupta was the son of Chandra Gupta, and his mother name was Kumaradevi who was Lichchhavi princes. He was called the Napoleon of India. He defeated almost all the rulers of India. According to ‘Prayag Prashasti’ his territories extended from the Himalayas in the north to the river Narmada in the south and from the Brahamaputra River in the east to the Yamuna River in the west. In modern day these territories inlcude Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Bengal. Thus among the given states, Kashmir was not included in the empire of Samudra Gupta.
source: UP PSC ACF/RFO (Mains) 2020 Paper I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.96

explanation: Chandragupta II had defeated Shakas ruling in western region of India and owned the title of ‘Vikramaditya’. His other titles were Shakari, Devagupta, Devaraja, Devasri and Param Bhagawat etc. He was the first to own the title of ‘Param Bhagawat’.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The title of 'Prithivyah Prathama Vir' held by :
explanation: Samudragupta helds the title of ‘Prithivya Pratham Vir’. He was a great ruler and conqueror who fought more than 100 battles and was undefeated throughout his life. He owned the titles of Sarva-raj- ochchetta (uprooter of all kings), Ashwamedh Parakram, Likshavi Dauhitra, Parakramank, Apratiratha, Kritant parashu. His ideal was ‘Digvijaya’ and an United India. The detailed account of his victories is found in his inscription ‘Prayag Prasasti’, that's was the creation of his Prime Minister Harishena. This is why British historian Vincent Smith had recognized ‘Samudragupta’ as ‘Napoleon of India’.

question: There were various causes behind the decline of Gupta Empire. Which one of the following statement was not a cause?
options: Acceptance of Buddhism by subsequent Gupta rules
explanation: Huna’s invasion, Feudal form of administration and acceptance of Buddhism by later Gupta rulers were the basic causes behind the decline of Gupta Empire while there was no role of Arab’s attack on Gupta Empire.th The first Arab attack on India took place during the 8 century A.D.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) Ist 2014-15 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.98

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Gupta dynasty ruled during the period of:
explanation: Sri Gupta (240-280 CE) founded the Gupta dynasty. His son Ghatotkach(280-319 CE) was the next ruler. The achievements of these two early rulers are less known. It cannot be said clearly whether they were independent rulers or subordinate rulers under Kushan rulers. Chandragupta I was said to be the first independent ruler of Gupta dynasty who was coronated in 319 AD. Vishnu Gupta (543-550 CE) was the last ruler of Gupta dynasty. Thus, the glory of Gupta empire came to an end in 550 AD after a long and glorified rule of more than 200 years.
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S. 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.98

subject: AP & Indian History
question: An inscription by which of the following is found on Prayag citation of Samudragupta?
explanation: Prayag Prashasti (commendation) is the creation of Harishen,’ the prime minister of Samudragupta. It has been inscripted on Ashoka’s pillar edict found from Kaushambi which was later established by Akbar in Allahabad fort. It was next used by Mughal emperor Jahangir praising the achievements, conquests, and toth commemorate his accession to the throne during 17 century.
source: UP RO/ARO (Pre) Exam, 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.98

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The famous Allahabad Pillar Inscription was composed by:
explanation: Harishena or Harisena, was a 4th-century Sanskrit poet, panegyrist, and government minister. He was an important figure in the court of the Gupta emperor, Samudragupta. He composed the most famous Allahabad Pillar inscription which describes the bravery of Samudragupta and this inscription is engraved on the same pillar that carries the inscriptions of Ashoka.
source: Arunachal PSC (GS) 26-11-2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.98
