subject: AP & Indian History
question: The Gupta Age is called the 'Golden Age' of ancient India, but in which field, was it not so progressive?
explanation: The Gupta Age in ancient India has been called the ‘Golden Age of India’ because of the many achievements in the field of art and architecture, sculpture, paintings, science and technology, and literature except in foreign trade. Some famous architectures include Dasavatara temple (Deogarh, Jhansi), Dhammekha Stupa (Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh). Sculpture includes standing Buddha statue (Mathura), Buddha statue at Sarnath Paintings include Ajanta cave paintings (Maharashtra) and Bagh cave paintings (Madhya Pradesh). Ancient History

question: In Gupta period, the Officer associated with land-tax collection was
explanation: In Gupta period, the officer related to ‘land- tax-collection’ was called ‘Dhruvadhikaran,’ for the security of ‘land-Aalekh ,there were two other important officers called- Mahaksh Patlik and Karnic; There was one officer related to land dispute too, called as ‘Nyadhikaran’. The 'Sarthavaha' were the chief merchants represented the various trading communities.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to forced labour (Vishti) in India during the Gupta period, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: It was considered as a source of income for the State, a sort of tax paid by the people.
It was totally absent in the Madhya Pradesh and Kathiawar regions of the Gupta Empire.
The forced labourer was entitled to weekly wages.
The eldest son of the labourer was sent as the forced labourer
explanation: Bhag, Bhoga, Bali, Uparikar , Udranga and Vishti were the taxes levied on public during Gupta period. It was prerogative of the king to charge 1/6 of the real production as tax. Bhag was a land revenue levied on the peasants. Bhoga was a tax (a type of gift) paid by the people in the form of the fruits and vegetables on daily basis to the king. ‘Bali’ was a tax levied on religious activities. Udranga and Uparikar were a type of cess over land revenue. Uparikar was levied on regular farmers while Udranga was taken from irregular farmers The taxes were paid in cash (Hiranya) or kind (grains). Vishti a kind of tax which was to be given in the form of physical labour was mainly forced upon Peasants. After the Gupta Period Sudra became peasants who had to work in the field of Kings and their feudatories and for the army without any wages.
source: IAS (Pre) 2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.99

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who of the following was the first Gupta ruler to issue coins?
explanation: Chandragupta I was the first Gupta ruler who circulated his coins for the first time. He was regarded as the real founder of Gupta dynasty. He also initiated Gupta Samvat in 319 AD. It is notable that the difference between Gupta and Shaka Samvat (78 AD) is about 241 years.

question: The first Gupta ruler who circulated the Silver coins?
explanation: The silver coins were called 'Rupak'. It was believed that Chandragupta II was the first Gupta ruler who circulated silver coins for the first time. Chandragupta II initiated these silver coins to commemorate his victory over the Shakas. These silver coins were of 32-36 grains.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. (M) 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.100

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to Indian history, which of the following is/are the essential element/elements of the feudal system? 1. A very strong centralized political authority and a very weak provincial or local political authority. 2. Emergence of administrative structure based on control and possession of land. 3. Creation of lord-vassal relationship between the feudal lord and his overlord. Ancient History 10 Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation: In Feudal system of administration the powers of a king as central authority weakened while it created the way for the emergence of regional rulers. New power centers emerged at regional level based on control and ownership of land. The land provided by the kings to subordinate rulers strengthened them. The relation between kings and local rulers can be recognized as relation between owner and their loyals.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. Ist 2015 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.100

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Read the following statements carefully– 1. Gupta rulers claimed providential authority for himself 2. Their administration was completely centralized 3. They promoted the tradition of land grant Give your answer from the following codes:
explanation: The titles owned by Gupta rulers such as, Param Bhattarak, Parameshwara and Maharajadhiraja shows that they believed in their divinely origin. Though the Gupta rulers were the source of all powers but due to land grant system under Gupta rulers the Feudal lord became more and more powerful which gave way to decentralization of power. The land granted to temples and Brahmins was called ‘Agrahar’. Villages related to these kinds of land were known as Agrahar villages. The holders of these lands had complete ownership on the land.
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.100

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In ruling period of which dynasty the maximum villages donated to temples and Brahmins?
explanation: In fact, the tradition of land donation to Temples and Brahmins was initiated by Satvahana rulers. This tradition was followed by Gupta Rulers later on a large scale.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.100

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which dynasty was distracted maximum due to Hunas invasion?
explanation: Gupta Empire was destabilized due to Hunas attack, during Skandgupta regime which was successfully faced by Skandgupta, but after some time Hunas attacked in the leadership of Torman and Mihirkul during the regime of Purugupta and Budhagupta, paved the way for decline of Gupta Empire.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1993 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.100

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During Gupta period, the designations 'Mahattara' and 'Pattakila' were used for:
explanation: The terms ‘Mahattara (Mahattak) & Pattakila were used for the head of villages during ancient India. The word Pattakila was used in Maharashtra region and Mahattara was used in northern India, basically in Uttar Pradesh.
source: IAS (Pre) Ist Paper G.s. 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.100

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which one of the following ports handled the north Indian trade during the Gupta period?
explanation: Tamralipti emerged as major port for international trade of northern India during Gupta period. It is notableth that after the decline of Roman Empire in the 4 century BC due to the foreign attacks India’s trade with Roman Empire was declined. It shifted to south-east Asia and thus Tamralipti became a major port. The main articles of trade were silk and copper. Tamralipta or Tamralipti was a city in ancient Bengal, located in the Bay of Bengal in Midnapore district of modern day West Bengal.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.101

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Assertion (A) : The origin of Feudal system in ancient India can be traced to military campaigns. Reason (R) : There was considerable expansion of the feudal system during the Gupta period.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
explanation: The roots of Feudal system during ancient India can be traced in administrative system of Shakas, Kushans and Satvahans dynasties. The rulers of these dynasties used to appoint provincial governors in conquered regions. Earlier these provincial rulers expressed their loyalty towards the emperors but later when the central power became weak and redundant towards provincial administration, they behaved like an independent ruler. Feudalism during Gupta period became more frequent with the sign of drubbing in Gupta Empire.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2000 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.101

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following Nine jewels of Chandragupta was related to astrological horoscopy Falita Jyotisha?
explanation: Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) was a great patron of art and literature. He provided shelter to various scholars in his court. There were ‘9’ specific scholars of various fields in his court collectively known as nine jewels. These were Dhanavantari, Kshapanaka, Kalidasa, Ghatakarpara, Amarasimha, Varahmihira, Vararuchi, Vetal Bhatta and Shanku etc. Among these jewels Kshapanaka was related to ‘Falit Jyotish’. Kalidas was a noted Sanskrit scholar and poet who visited in the court of Kuntal king Pravarsen II as an ambassador to Chandragupta II.
source: UP Lower (Pre) Spl. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.101

subject: AP & Indian History
question: To which of the following revenue free agricultural land was provided during Gupta Empire?

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Rate of land revenue during Gupta period was:
explanation: The rate of land revenue during Gupta regime was 1/6 of actual production . Smriti epics during Gupta period allowed the emperor to charge 1/6 of actual production against the services provided by him for the public welfare.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1997-98 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.101

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During Gupta period, centers located in Gujarat, Bengal, Deccan and Tamil Rashtra (region) were related to :
explanation: Clothes weaving (manufacturing) was a major business during Gupta period. Gujarat, Bengal, Deccan and Tamil region were the major centre of textile industry. Uraiyur in Tamil Nadu was the most famous centre of cotton Textiles. Amarkosha mentioned about activities and equipments like weaving yarn and handicraft.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.101

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Pundravardhana Bhukti was located in:
explanation: Pundravardhana Bhukti (a province) during Gupta period has been identified in modern North Bengal region. The region was known as ‘Pundra Desh’ during ancient period. The provincial rulers appointed by Gupta emperors were known as ‘Uparika Maharaja’ in this province. The copper inscriptions of Gupta rulers gives information about it. It was from 443 to 543 AD.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2012 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.101

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Trading with north India during Gupta period was conducted from which port?
explanation: The north Indian trade was conducted from Tamralipti port during Gupta period. The parity of Tamralipti is established with Tamluk which is situated in Midnapur district of modern West Bengal. From here the trade to China, Sri Lanka, Java and Sumatra took place.
source: UPPCS Kanoongo Exam, 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.101

It is clear that the silk trade suffered a deep loss.

explanation: The land during Gupta period was categorized in 5 groups on the basis of quality and economic uses . The categories were as follows:- Land type Features Kshetra – Agricultural land Vasti – Habitable land Aprahata – Forest land Khila – Waste (barren) land Gopata Sarah – Pasture land

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements are correct? (i) The stone inscriptions, copper plates and coin writings of Gupta kings were written in pure Sanskrit. explanation: ● Brahmi Script or late Brahmi Script was used for writing sanskrit and is associated with the Gupta Empire of India, which was a period of material prosperity and great religious and scientific development. ● Kumarsambhav and Raghuvansha is written by Kalidasa. ● Panchasiddhantika was major work by ancient astronomer Varahmihira. Panchasiddhantika means five astronomical canons. The book was written during 575 CE.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following is/are not the works of Bhasa, the famous poet of the Gupta period? (I) Charudatta (II) Balacharita (III) Ravanavadha
explanation: Bhasa is one of the oldest known classical playwrights in the history of Sanskrit literature and may well be known as the father of Sanskrit drama. A prolific poet and dramatist, he was venerated by Kalidasa, Banabhatta, Rajashekhara and critics such as Abhinavagupta. Charudatta and Balacharita are works of Bhasa while Bhatti-kavya or Ravanavadha, composed by Sri Bhatti.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following was the first to explain that the rotation of the earth on its own axis accounts for the daily rising and setting of the sun?
explanation: Aryabhatta was a great mathematician and astrologer of Gupta period. He was the first to explain that the rotation of the earth on its own axis accounts for daily rising and setting of the sun. His famous books were- Aryabhattiya, Dashgitika and Aryabhatta Siddhanta.

explanation: Harishena was Sandhivigrahika-Mahadandanayaka and Kumaramatya during Samudragupta regime. He was a great poet too. He was the creator of Prayag Prasasti in Champu style and in Sanskrit language. Devichandraguptam and Mudra Rakshas are the creations of Vishakhdutta.
source: Chhattisgarh PCS (Pre) 2017-18 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.102

subject: AP & Indian History
question: From where the inscriptional evidence of Sati cult is found?
explanation: First Inscripted evidence about ‘Sati’ tradition is found from Eran edict of Bhanugupta built in 510 AD. The edict is located in Sagar district of Madhya Pradesh. According to information after the death of Bhanugupta’s friend and Military commander Goparaj during the battle, his widow (wife) had ended her life with the pyre of her husband. It was in Sanskrit language. The first inscriptional evidence of Sati Pratha has been found from Eran. It was nearly about 400 AD. According to Axel Michels, the first clear proof of the practice is from Nepal in 464 AD and in India from 510 AD.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. I Paper 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.102

explanation: Mandasor inscription 436 CE belonged to Gupta ruler Kumargupta located in Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh gives information about the construction and management of a sun temple by Silk weavers community. A trust (Akshayanivi) was established for the management of the temple. This temple is also called Pashupatinath Temple.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.103

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Bhumi Sparsha style of Buddha statue of Sarnath is related to the Period of :
explanation: The Bhumi Sparsha style of Buddha idols were the creation of Gupta period. Buddha idols of Sarnath, Sultanganj and Mathura are three notable idols of this kind. The artist has successfully shown the peace and spirituality in the idols of the Buddha.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Tradition of child marriage emerged in :
explanation: Emergence of critical caste system, untouchability, child marriage, purdah system etc emerged during Gupta period.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The period of establishment of Nalanda university is :
explanation: Located in Nalanda district of Bihar, ‘Nalanda University was renowned education centre during ancient Indian period. The university was established by Gupta ruler ‘Kumargupta’ (Shakraditya- seal was found which tells about it). He was also known as ‘Mahendraditya’. Chinese traveler Hiuen-Tsang had mentioned Shakraditya as the founder of this university whose parity is established with Kumargupta. This university was destroyedth by Muhammad-bin- Bakhtiyar-Khilji in late 12 century. He was a Turkish Military commander under Kutubuddin Aibak.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.103

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following classical books on literature were written during Gupta period? 1. Amarkosha 2. Kamasutra 3. Meghaduta 4. Mudra Rakshasa Choose the correct answer from the codes given below: Codes:
explanation: All the four books were composed during Gupta period. Amarkosh was the creation of Amarasimha, Kamasutra was the creation of Vatsyayana, a noted scholar of that period. Kalidasa had written various literary work namely, Meghdootam, Abhigyan Shakuntalam, Malvikagnimitram, Vikramorvashiyam, Raghuvansham, and Kumar sambhavam etc, while Mudra Rakshasa was the creation of Visakhadatta.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. Ist 2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.103

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Hero of the Malavikagnimitra, a play by Kalidas was?
explanation: Malvikagnimitram is a great dramatic act by Kalidas. It contains the love story of Agnimitra ‘the king of Vidisha’ and Malavika ‘the princes of Vidarbha (Malwa)’.It provides the detailed account of social and political situation during that period. Kalidas is recognized as Shakespeare of India.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1998 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.103

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who has mentioned about Kayastha a caste for the first time?
explanation: Emergence of Kayastha as a caste is the incidence of Gupta period. The early mention about Kayastha is found in Yagyavalkya Smriti while as a caste it was mentioned first in Aushanasa Smriti.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.103

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who introduced the law for the freedom of slaves at first?
explanation: Narad Smriti, which is the creation of Gupta period had produced the list of 15 types of slaves. It also talks about the ways to get rid of slavery.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.103

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to the scientific progress of ancient India which of the statements given below are correct? 1. Different kinds of specialized surgical instruments were in common use by the 1st century AD. 2. Transplant of internal organs in the human body had begun by the beginning of the 3rd century AD. 3. The concept of sine of an angle was known in the 5th century AD. 4. The concept of cyclic quadrilateral was known in the 7th century AD. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
explanation: A remarkable growth can be seen in the field of science and technology during ancient Indian period. The growth in the field of all the segment of science such as medical ,engineering and chemical field can be seen. The theories of sine, cosine and inverse sine were well known to Indians during Gupta period (5th century AD). The detailed account of these theories can be found in ‘Surya siddhant’ and Arya Bhattiyam. A Sanskrit book ‘Susruta samhita’ the creation of Maharshi Susruta during Gupta period provides the list of surgical equipments , diseases, and medicinal plants. It is notable that the theory of cyclic quadrilateral was initiated by Brahma Gupta during the 7th century BC.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. Ist 2012 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.104

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following had given permission to build a Buddhist Vihar in Bodha Gaya for the Sinhali monks?
explanation: The Sinhala (Sri Lanka) king Meghavarman had sent a mission in the court of Samudragupta and asked for the construction of a Buddhist Vihar for Sinhali monks in Bodh Gaya.
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S. 2000 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.104

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien attended the fourth Great Buddhist Council held by Kanishka. 2. The Chinese pilgrim Huien Tsang met Harsha and found him to be antagonistic to Buddhism. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Chinese traveler Fa-Hien came to india during the Gupta ruler Chandragupta II (375-415 A.D.) while Huien Tsang visited India during Harshvardhana time. He found Harsha to be a supporter of Buddhism. Ancient History
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2004 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.104

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Chinese pilgrim who visited India in early 6th century AD was:
explanation: Chinese traveler Sung-Yun visited India in 518 AD. He travelled at various Buddhist holy places and other religious place in India and gathered the Buddhist texts . Among other Chinese visitors Fa-Hien came during Chandragupta II regime, Hiuen Tsang had come during Harshavardhana period and I-tsing visited India in 7th century AD.
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) G.S. Ist 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.104

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The term Yavanpriya, mentioned in ancient Sanskrit texts, denoted :
options: a fine variety of Indian muslin
damsels sent to the Greek court for dance performance
explanation: The word ‘Yavanpriya’ used in primary sanskrit text stands for ‘Pepper’. During ancient period there was a huge export of pepper to Rome. Roman people liked pepper too much so the sanskrit scholars used the word Yavanpriya for pepper. D. Vakataka Dynasty
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1995 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.104

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following had offered four Ashwamedha Yajnas?
explanation: The ruler of Vakataka dynasty ‘Pravarsena’ is credited for offering four ‘Ashwamedha Yajnas’. He was the follower of Brahmin tradition. He owned the title of ‘Samrat’.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. Ist 2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.104

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following rulers had organised four Ashwamedh sacrificial acts (Yajna)?
explanation: The ruler of Vakataka dynasty ‘Pravarsena I had performed four Ashwamedh sacrificial acts (Yajna). Shunga ruler Pushyamitra Shunga had organised two Ashwamedh Yajnas while Gupta ruler Samudragupta organised one Ashwamedh Yajna. Vakataka Dynasty: ruled from the 3rd century to the 5th century after the fall of Satavahanas and before the rise of Chalukyas. They ruled in modern Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. They were the contemporary of Guptas and this dynasty was founded by Vindhyasakti. Pravarasena-I was the first ruler to perform four Ashwamedha Yajnas. 12. 1. From the decline of Guptas until the rise of Harshavardhana in the early seventh century, which of the following kingdoms were holding power in Northern India? 1. The Guptas of Magadha 2. The Paramaras of Malwa 3. The Pushyabhutis of Thanesar 4. The Maukharis of Kannauj 5. The Yadavas of Devagiri
source: UPPCS (Mains) GS.2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.104

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The Maitrakas of Valabhi Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation: The Guptas of Magadha, The Pushyabhutis of Thanesar, the Maukharis of Kannauj, and the Maitrakas of Valabhi, were holding power from the decline of Guptas unitl the rise of Harshavardhana in the early seventh century. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.
source: UPSC (IAS) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.105

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During which period untouchability existed clearly?
explanation: Scholars characterize untouchability as a relatively later development after the establishment of the varna and caste system. Historian Vivekanand Jha notes that earliest Vedic text, Rigveda makes no mentions of untouchability and even the later Vedic text, which reveal certain groups such as the chandalas, do not suggest that untouchability existed in the contemporary society. According to Jha, in the later period, several groups began to be characterized as untouchable, a development which reached its peak and shown clearly in Post Gupta period.

explanation: Dhruvasena II was a ruler of the Maitraka dynasty which ruled in Western India.The Maitraka dynasty was founded by Bhatarka. The capital of the dynasty was in Vallabhi . Dhuruvasena II ruled the dynasty from 627-641 and become a vassal after his defeat to Harshavardhana. ● Harsha used to celebrate a solemn festival at Prayag (Allahabad) at the end of every five years. He also used to organize the Mahamoksha Parishad at Prayag. He used to do a lot charity in the parishad. His court poet Banabhatta wrote Kadambari. explanation: ‘Harshacharita’ and travelogue of Hiuen Tsang ‘si-yu-ki ‘are the major source of information about socio-religious and political situation and personal beliefs of Harshavardhan. Harshavardhan was an ardent devotee to lord ‘Shiva’ and deity ‘Sun’ like his ancestors. He became a Buddhist after meeting with Diwakar Mitra ‘a Buddhist monk’. He provided the state patron to Buddhism. He had organized a council for the scholars and prominent religious personalities from various sects of the time. He also used to organise religiousth gathering at Prayag in every five years. It was the 6 such gathering in which Hiuen Tsang had participated. He also called a great religious assembly in his capital at Kannauj on the bank of the river Ganga in the year 643 AD.

question: Chinese traveller Yuan Chwang (Hiuen Tsang) who visited India recorded the general conditions and culture of India at that time. As regards punishment for offences, ordeals by fire, water and poison were the instruments for determining the innocence or guilt of a person. 3. The tradesmen had to pay duties at ferries and barrier stations. Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
explanation: Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang visited India during Harshavardhan regime (606-647 AD). He has mentioned that travelling during these days was not completely safe. It is notable that Hiuen Tsang himself had been looted twice by the robbers. Thus the statement I is false. He further tells that fire, water and poison were applied to ordeal with criminal acts. He also informs that the traders had to pay tariff and other taxes. Thus the statement II & III are true.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who had sent Hiuen Tsang as an emissary in the court of Harsha?
explanation: Though Hiuen Tsang was contemporary to Chinese ruler Tai-Sunga but he visited India in his individual status. He came to India through silk route in about 629-630 AD during Harshavardhan regime. He stayed in India for more than 15 years. He visited various monuments related to Buddha and studied in Nalanda University for 6 years. He has mentioned Shakraditya as the founder of Nalanda University. While he returned to China he got a warm welcome by Chinese king ‘Taai-Sunga’ who appointed him as his spiritual advisor. He composed his travelogue named as ‘Si-Yu-Ki’ on request of the king. It is notable that the king was against the tour of western region earlier and had imposed ban on western tour. Hiuen Tsang is regarded as ‘Prince of Travellers’. He is remembered by the Indians because of his creation ‘Si-Yu-Ki’.
source: U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) G.S. 2007 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.107

question: The reign of Harshavardhana was marked by vigorous political activity. Which of the following statements is/are correct in this reference? (I) Devagupta, the king of Malava, accepted the suzerainty of Harshavardhana. (II) Bhaskaravarman, the king of Kamarupa, entered into a treaty of friendship with Harshavardhana. (III) Harshavardhana defeated Sasanka, the king of Gauda.
explanation: Devagupta was the king of Malwa. He is known for the alliance formed with Sashanka in order to counteract the growing power of Harsha’s empire. Hence, statement (1) is incorrect. Bhaskaravarman, the last of the Varman dynasty, was perhaps the most illustrious kings of the medieval Kamarupa. After being captured by the Gauda king during the reign of his father, he was able to re-establish the rule of the Varman's. He made political alliances with Harshavardhana of Thaneswar, against the alliance of the Gauda and East Malwa. Hence, statement (2) is correct. Sashanka, king of Gauda in eastern Bengal, entered Magadha as a friend of Rajyavardhana (elder brother of Harshavardhana and king of Kannauj) but in secret alliance with the Malwa king Devagupta treacherously killed Rajyavardhana. After hearing about the murder of his brother Harsha resolved at once to march against the treacherous king of Gauda and killed Sashanka in a battle. Hence statement III is also correct. B. Other Dynasties

(2) The Valabhi Era used by the Maitrakas was the same as Gupta Era. (3) The Valabhi ruler Dhruvasena II was a contemporary of Budhagupta .
explanation: Bhatarka was a military governorth under the Gupta empire. At the end of the 5 century, he established an independent Kingdom in Gujarat, Valabhi, Gujarat was the capital city. The Maitraka dynasty ruled western India from approximately 475 to approx 776 CE from their capital at Valabhi who followed the Mithraic mysteries, they were followers of Shivism. Their origin is uncertain but they were probably Chandravanshi Kshatriyas. It is identical to the Valabhi era, which was used in the Saurashtra region of Western India although regional differences lead to a slightly different calculation for the conversion of Valabhi era years to common era. The Valabhi ruler Dhruvasena II was not a contemporary of Budhagupta.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-26.12.21 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.108

explanation: The Vikramshila University was one of the three most important Buddhist Monastries in India during Pala empire along with Nalanda and Odantpuri University. Vikramshila was one of the largest Buddhist Universities at that time, Vikramshila was a centre for Vajrayana and employed Tantric preceptors, apart from Vajrayana other subjects like Astronomy, Logic, Law, Grammer and Philosophy were also taught here. Hence, only statements I & II are incorrect.

To save their sanctity Rajput women used to commit suicide collectively, by jumping into fire which was known as Jauhar.

question: With reference to Chausath Yogini Temple situated near Morena, consider the following statements : 1. It is a circular temple built during the reign of Kachchhapaghata Dynasty. 2. It is the only circular temple built in India. 3. It was meant to promote the Vaishnava cult in the region. 4. Its design has given rise to a popular belief that it was the inspiration behind the Indian Parliament building. Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: The Chausath Yogini temple is in Morena district in M.P. The temple was built by the Kachchhapaghata king Devapala (r.c. 1055-1075). 1. It is not the only circular temple built in India. 2. Also known as Ekattarso Mahadeva Temple because of the Presence of Multitude of shivlingas inside its cells. So it promotes Shaivism. 3. The uniqueness of this yogini temple is its circular shape that is popularly believed to have inspired the design of the Indian parliament. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements are correct regarding Gandhara School of Art? (1) It is recognized for the first sculptural demonstrations of the Buddha in human form. (2) The Gandhara School of Art & Sculpture used spotted red sandstone for construction. (3) The art of the Gandhara School was chiefly Mahayana and shows Greco-Roman impact
explanation: Gandhara School of Art mostly flourished in the areas of Afghanistan and Present North –Western India. The prominent locations were Taxila, Peshawar, Begram and Bamiyan. Grey sandstone (Blue-grey Mica schist to be precise) is used in Gandhara School of Art. The art of the Gandhara School was chiefly Mahayana and shows Greco-Roman impact. Therefore, the correct statements are (1) and (3) only. Hence the correct answer is option (b).
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-26.12.21 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.113

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements are correct regarding Paintings? (1) Bundi School of paintings is characterized by a fondness for lush vegetation and dramatic night skies (2) "What happens to human life after death" is a theme used in Paitkar paintings (3) Jain miniature paintings employed only White and black colours. (4) Manjusha paintings is also known as Snake paintings
explanation: The Bundi School is characterized by a fondness for lush vegetation, dramatic night skies, a distinctive way of depicting water by light swirls against a dark background, and vivid movement. Hence statement 1 is true. Paitkar Paintings is from a small village, Amadubi situated in the Eastern part of Jharkhand which is also called the village of Paitkar. ‘Paitkar’ is the traditional painting of this village. They are based on themes like gods and goddesses and “What happens to human life after death”, etc. Hence statement 2 is also true. Jain miniature painting in India was executed in the traditional tempera technique. After mixing colours in water along with a binding medium they were applied on the drawing. First, the sketch was freely drawn in black over which a white priming was given. Hence statement 3 is also true. Manjusha painting is an art form that belongs to the Bhagalpur region of Bihar. These paintings revolve around the folklore of Bihula-Bisahari. It is also known as Angika art, where ‘ang’ refers to one of the Mahajanpada. Since snake motifs are always present, it is also called snake painting. Hence statement 4 is also true. So option (a) is the correct answer.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-26.12.21 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.114

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In which of the following stupas, the features of a platform with ‘Aryaka-Pillars’ are found?
explanation: The features of a platform with 'Aryaka Pillars' are found in Amaravati stupa. Aryaka platforms consist of four projections projected from the drum, with each projection bearing five pillars. Amaravati stupa is the largest one in the state of Andhra Pradesh. It was built during the reign of Ashoka, Maurya and enlarged under the Satavahana and Ikshvaku patronage. It consisted of a huge solid dome standing on a cylindrical drum-like platform which was fully decorated. In contrast to Amaravati stupa, the Great Stupa at Nagarjunakonda in Andhra Pradesh was only sparsely decorated and no railings around. Ghantasala stupa is also situated in Andhra Pradesh. Bodhgaya stupa is located in Bihar.
source: UPPSC (Pre) 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.114

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements are correct? (1) In Dravidian style temples, a covered ambulatory is kept encircling the square sanctum with a large square encircling it and riches were projected by the pilasters on the outer side of the wall. (2) The spires of the Dravidian style are made up of different stories getting narrower while going upwards. (3) The thrust of Nagara Style spire is horizontal whereas the thrust of Dravidian style spire is vertical.
explanation: Nagara Temple Style: - ● In North India it is common for an entire temple to be built on stone platform with steps leading up to it. ● Further, unlike in South India it does not usually have elaborate boundary walls or gateways. ● While the earliest temple had just one tower, or Shikhara, later temples had several. ● The garbhagriha is always located directly under the tallest tower. ● The second major type of architectural form in the Nagara order is the Phamsana, which tends to be broader and shorter than latina ones. ● The third main sub-type of the Nagara building is generally called the Valabhi type. Dravidian or South Indian Temple:- ● Unlike the 'Nagara' temple, the dravida temple is enclosed within a compound wall. ● The front wall has an entrance gateway in it's centre, which is known as Gopuram. ● Kanchipuram, Thanjavur or Tanjore, Madurai and Kumbakonam are the most famousth templeth towns of Tamil Nadu where during the 8 - 12 centuries, the role of the temple was not limited to religious matters alone.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-26.12.21 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.114

question: Which of the following statements regarding Ajanta caves are correct? (1) 26 caves have been made by carving out the mountain (2) The paintings in these caves have been made at different periods (3) The pictures of the birth of Gautam Buddha, Mahabhinishkraman and Mahaparinivarana have been depicted in the paintings
explanation: The Ajanta Caves are 30 (approximately) rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments from the 2nd century BC to about 480 CE in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra state, India . Hence statement 1 is wrong. The Ajanta Caves were built by the Mahayana sect of Buddhism. Monasteries and worship-halls of different Buddhist traditions were carved into approximately 250-feet wall of rock. The caves also present paintings depicting the past lives and rebirths of the Buddha, pictorial tales from Aryasura's Jatakamala, and rock-cut sculptures of Buddhist deities.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-26.12.21 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.115

question: Which school of art used spotted sandstone as material for sculptures?
explanation: The Mathura school of art was entirely influenced by Indianism. The stone used in the Mathura school of art was red sandstone. They mostly used the spotted red sandstone for making sculptures and statues. The initial images of the Buddha and Bodhisattva are happy and fleshy figures.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: At which one of the following sites, the boar incarnation of Vishnu has been depicted in a sculpture?
explanation: The sculpture at Udayagiri Cave, Vidisha (Madhya Pradesh) depicts a Varaha Avatar (boar incarnation) of Vishnu. It was built during the reign of Chandragupta II in the fourth century. These caves were built in the hill of Udayagiri to commemorate the victory over Malwa by Chandragupta II's general Viresena. Some of the oldest Hindu temples and paintings of India are preserved in these caves. These caves are the most important archaeological sites in India and a protected monument by the Archaeological Survey of India.
source: UPPSC ACF Mains Paper I 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.115

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statement is/are correct about Gandhara School of Art? (1) Gandhara School of Art was one of the major schools of art in the history of ancient India and it is uniquely associated with the Greco-Roman style of art. (2) Gandhara style of art was closely associated with Mahayana Buddhism and hence the main theme of this art was Lord Buddha and Bodhisattvas. (3) It mostly flourished in the areas of Afghanistan and present North-Western India and the prominent locations were Taxila (Takshashila), Peshawar, Begram and Bamiyan.
explanation: Gandhara School of Art was one of major schools of art in the history of ancient India. Although being an intricate part of Indian history. It is uniquely associated with the Greco-Roman style of art. • This style of art was closely associated with Mahayana Buddhism and hence the main theme of this art was Lord Buddha and Bodhisattvas. This can be conjectured that idea and conception of this style was Indian and in execution it was foreign. Example of the Gandhara style of art is the Bamiyan Buddha statues. • It mostly flourished in the areas of Afghanistan and present North-Western India. The prominent locations were Taxila, Peshawar, Begram, and Bamiyan. The period around which the Gandhara school of art flourished could be said to be from the 1st century BCE to 4 century CE.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-2019 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.116

The total number of these temples built between the ninth and twelfth centuries on the banks of the Wainganga river in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, was 24, out of which 18 have now been ruined .This temple complex is being renovated by the Archaeological Survey of India from the year 2017.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Brahmanical cave temples of Mogal-rajapuram and Undavalli are assigned to :
explanation: Brahmanical cave temples of Mogal- rajapuram and Undavalli are assigned to Vishnukundins. These caves are dedicated to Anantha Padmanabha and Narashimha.th These caves are said to be formed in the 7 century. But one can see the Guptath styleth of rock-cut architecture which goes back to the 4 - 5 century CE. Most of the emperors of Gupta’s were Vaishnavas. So we can see many sculptures of Narasimha, Vishnu, and Ramayana stories. Note - Vishnukundins (420-624 CE) were a major dynasty since the fall of the Satavahans which enjoyed imperial status over the entire Andhra region including Kalinga (Odisha) and some parts of Maharastra.
source: APPSC Group-II Screening-2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.116

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements are true about temple architecture? (i) The freestanding (mortar & stone) temples are supposed to have originated in the Gupta period. (ii) Ladkhan, which is one of the earliest temple belongs to Chalukya of Badami. (iii) In Khajuraho temples, all the compartments of the temple are connected internally and externally. (iv) Kailashnath temple at Kanchi is the earliest freestanding temple of Dravid style. Choose the correct answer :
explanation: The art of temple construction originated during Gupta period. All kinds of temples whether they are elevated temples or the freestanding temples (lime stone) were constructed in Gupta period. The Ladkhan temple located in Bijapur district of Karnataka, is one among the temples of Dravidian style, that belongs to the Aihole group of temples. The temple was constructed by Chalukya dynasty of Badami. The temples of Khajuraho were constructed by Chandela rulers in between 950 to 1050 AD. These temples are related to Hindu, Buddhist and Jain sects. Kailashnath temple of Kanchi was constructed by Narasimha Varman II (Rajsimha) during the 8th century AD. Devoted to lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. It is not the freestanding temple but actually it is the earliest rock cut temple of Dravid style.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.116

subject: AP & Indian History

Among the described Sun Temple, Sun temple in Arassavalli (Andhra Pradesh) was constructedth by Kalinga ruler Devendra Varma in the 7 century AD. Omkareshwar temple is devoted to lord Shiva, it is located in Khandawa district of Madhya Pradesh and is among the twelve Jyotirlingas of lord Shiva. Amarkantak is located in Anuppur district of Madhya Pradesh and situated at the origin place of Narmada and Son rivers.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to the history of Indian rock-cut architecture, consider the following statements: 1. The caves at Badami are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India. 2. The Barabar rock-cut caves were originally made for Ajivakas by Emperor Chandragupta Maurya. 3. At Ellora, caves were made for different faiths. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Badami Cave Temples, located in Bagalkot district of Karnataka were built in the 6th & the 7th century AD during Chalukya regime. Barabar caves are the most ancient caves locatedrd in Bihar were built by Mauryan emperor Ashoka in 3 century BC. The caves were donated to Ajivakas and Buddhists. Devichandraguptam and Mudrarakshash are his major acts. These epics are important to know about social and cultural situation during Gupta period. Varahamihira was a noted scholar and astrologer. Brihatjataka, Panchsiddhantika, Brihat- Samhita and Laghu jatak are his famous works. Prabandha Chintamani wasth the creation of Merutunga,a noted jain scholar of 13-14 century AD. subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements is/are correct? (I) Charak Samhita deals basically with surgery. (II) The palm-leaf manuscript of Sushrut Samhita is preserved at Kaiser library of Nepal. Ancient History 14 (III) The three 'doshas' central to Ayurveda are 'vata' (wind), 'pitta' (bile) and ‘kapha’ (phlegm).
explanation: The Charaka Samhita is a Sanskrit text on Ayurveda (Indian traditional medicine). However, Sushruta Samhita deals with surgery. Hence, statement (1) is incorrect. One of the oldest Sushruta Samhita palm-leaf manuscripts is preserved at the Kaiser Library, Nepal. Hence, statement (2) is correct. Ayurveda is one of the world's oldest forms of holistic medicine and still widely used today. Combining physical, psychological and spiritual health, Ayurveda focuses on whole-body healing and states that person's dosha, a type of bodily human, determines his personality and health. Vata consists mostly of the two elements air and space (also known as ether) and is generally described as cold, light, dry, rough, flowing and spacious. Autumn represents vata for its cool, crisp days. Kapha is based on earth and water. It can be described as steady, stable, heavy, slow, cold and soft. Spring is known as Kapha season, as many parts of the world slowly exit hibernation. Pitta dosha is based on fire and water. It's commonly described as hot, light, sharp, oily, liquid and mobile, Summer is known as pitta season for its sunnys, heat days. Hence, statement (3) is correct.
source: GUJARAT PSC CIVIL PRE-PAPER-I (21-3-2021) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.136

explanation: Seleucid Empire (312-64 BCE) was an ancient empire that at its greatest extent stretched from Thrace in Europe to the border of India. It was carved out of the remains of Alexander the Great’s Macedonian empire by its founder, Seleucus I Nicator. Bactria, also called Bactriana or Zariaspa, ancient country lying between the mountains of the Hindu Kush and Amu Darya (Ancient Oxus River) in what is now part of Afghanistan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan. Bactria was especially important between about 600 BCE and about 600 CE, serving for much of that time as a meeting place not only for overland trade between East and West but also for the cross currents of religious and artistic ideas. After the Seleucid-Mauryan War the Mauryan Empire declined and lost control over the Indian Subcontinent is incorrect statement.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-26.12.21 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.139

explanation: Ratnavali" is a Sanskrit drama about a beautiful princess named Ratnavali, and a great king named Udayana. The Nagananda is a play in five acts which describes the self-sacrifice of Jimutavahana, prince of Vidyadharas. The Priyadarshika is also a natika in four acts, having the theme- the union of Udayana and Priyadarshini, daughter of Emperor Dridhavarman.

question: The upper three varnas, Brahman, Kshatriya and Vaishya were called......... .
explanation: The upper three varnas, Brahman, Kshatriya and Vaishya were called Dwija. explanation: Bhavabhuti was a famous Sanskrit playwright who wrote famous plays like Mahaviracharita, Malati madhava etc. He is believed to be the court poet of King Yashovarman of Kannauj. Sarnath is a holy place for Buddhist and Hindu community. Lord Buddha had delivered his first sermon here after enlightenment. subject: AP & Indian History
question: The following persons came to India at one time or another : I. Fa-Hien II. I-Tsing III. Megasthanese IV. Hiuen-Tsang The correct chronological sequence of their visits is :
explanation: Chinese traveller Fa-Hien visited India in 399 AD during the rule of Chandragupta II. He wrote a travelogue named as ‘Fo-kwo-ki’. He had mentioned about society and culture of India during the period, but he had not mentioned the name of Chandragupta II. Another Chinese traveller I-Tsing visited India in 673 AD and went to various Buddhist places. He stayed in Nalanda University for more than 10 Years. Hiuen- Tsang was also a Chinese traveller who visited India during Harshavardhan reign in ancient times between 627-643 AD. He wrote a travelogue ‘Si-yu-ki’. Hiuen- Tsang was regarded as the prince of ‘Travellers’. Megasthanese was Greek ambassador of Seleucus Nicator to Chandragupta Maurya. He came into the court of Magadh Emperor in 305 BC. He wrote an epic named ‘Indica’.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.143

question: What is the correct chronological order in which the following appeared in India? 1. Gold coins. 3. Iron plough. 2. Punch-marked silver coins. 4. Urban culture. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
explanation: The origin of urban culture in India can be traced in Indus Valley Civilization, about 4500 years ago (2500-1750 BC). Uses of iron plough in India started during later vedic era (1000-600 BC). Punch- marked silver coins introduced in India between the 7th - 6th century BC. Gold coins in India were circulated by Indo-Greek rulers in 270 BC.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1998 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.143

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Match the list I with list II and select the correct answer using the code given below: List-I List-II A. Gandhar art 1. Menander B. Junagarh rock 2. Patika inscription C. Milindapanho 3. Kushan D. Taxila inscription 4. Rudradaman I Codes : A B C D A B C D
explanation: Gandhar School of art was developed during Kushan period. There was extensive use of black stone and stucco. Bluish-Grey sandstone and Grey sandstone were prominent. The art was influenced with Greek art. Junagarh rock inscription was related to Shaka satrap Rudradaman. It gave information about construction of Sudarshan lake by Mauryan ruler Chandragupta Maurya. Milindapanho is a Buddhist epic written in dialogue form which took place between Buddhist monk Nagasena and Indo-Greek ruler Menander. Taxila copper plate is also known as Moga inscription. ` Thus the correct match is: Gandhar art - Kushan Junagarh Inscription - Rudradaman Milinda panho - Menander Taxila Inscription - Patika
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S.1 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.143

question: Consider the following statement and select the correct answer from the code given below: 1. Vikram Samvat began in 57 BC. 2. Shaka Samvat began in 78 AD. 3. Gupta era began in 319 AD. 4. The era of Muslim rule in India began in 1192 AD. Codes:
explanation: Vikram Samvat was introduced by the Parmar king of Ujjain, Vikramaditya in Memory of his victory over Shakas in 57 BC. It is notable that this Vikramaditya is not the Chandragupta II Vikramaditya of Gupta dynasty. Shaka Samvat was initiated by Kanishka, the ruler of Kushan dynasty in the year of his coronation (78 AD). Gupta era was started in 319 AD by Chandra Gupta I and the Muslim rule in India began in 1192 AD with the victory of Muhammad Gori over Prithviraj Chauhan.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.144

question: Who among the followings was a famous jurist during medieval India? 1. Vigyaneshwar 2. Himadri 3. Rajshekhar 4. Jimutavahan Choose the correct answer from the codes given below : Codes :
explanation: Vigyaneshwar, Jimutavahan and Himadri were the jurists during medieval period. Vigyaneshwar wrote a comment on Yagyavalakya Smriti. His epic is named as Mitakshara. He argued against the division of paternal assets during the life time of father. He favoured the right of daughters on women’s assets (stri- dhan). He was in the court of Chalukya ruler (Kalyani) Vikramaditya VI (1076-1126). Jimutavahan was the resident of Bengal during the rule of Pal dynasty. He wrote a book on Hindu law named ‘Dayabhaga’. Himadri was also a great scholar during medieval period. Rajshekhar was in the court of Pratihara ruler Mahendra Pal I & Mahipal. He wrote an epic named ‘Kavyamimansa’.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1995 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.144

too many divisions in the social structure
the absence of vast areas of fertile land

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Sayana, the famous commentator of the Vedic texts, was patronized by-
explanation: Sayana, the famous commentator of the Vedic texts, was patronized by Vijaynagar rulers. Sāyaṇa, also called Sayaṇacarya was a Sanskrit scholar from the Vijayanagara Empire of South India . An important commentator on the Vedas, he flourished under King Bukka Raya I and his successor Harihara II. More than a hundred works are attributed to him, among which are commentaries on nearly all parts of the Vedas; some were carried out by his pupils, and some were written in conjunction with his brother Vidyaraṇya or Madhavacharya. Sayana was a minister, and subsequently Prime Minister in Bukka Raya's court, and wrote much of his commentary, with his brother and other Brahmins during his ministership.
source: UPPCS (mains) G.S. 1 paper 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.145

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Heliodorus, of Besnagar inscription was the resident of which place?
explanation: Heliodorus, of Besnagar inscription was the resident of Taxila. Heliodorus’ was an ambassador of Greek ruler Antialcidas. He accepted the Bhagawat religion and established a pillar (Garuda Stambha) on the bank of river Betawa (Vetravati) and declared himself as ‘Param Bhagawat’. The name of ‘Vasudev’ is mentioned on the pillar. The Besnagar (Vidisha) pillar edict is the first archaeological evidence of Bhagawat sect. The pillar was devoted to God Vishnu. The pillar was erected around 113 BC in central India.
source: UP UDA/LDA (Pre) 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.145

subject: AP & Indian History

After the death of Muhammad Ghori, Qutub-ud-din Aibak became the first Muslim sultan of Delhi in 1206 and founded the Slave dynasty and thus became the first ruler of the slave dynasty.
