subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following Sultans called himself as 'Naib of Caliph' in his inscription on the mosque of Garhmukteshwar?
explanation: Balban called himself the ‘Naib of Caliph’ in his inscription on the wall of the mosque of Garhmukteshwar.
source: UP RO/ARO (M) 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.154

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statement in reference to Balban is not true?
options: He propounded the theory of 'Niyabat-i- Khudai'
He ended the influence of 'Turkan-i- Chahalgani'
He suppressed the revolt of Bengal Medieval History
explanation: The Iqtadari system was started by Iltutmish in India. Iqta is a type of revenue collection right that was granted by providing land areas. Those who received it, were called Muqti or Vali. Balban appointed an officer named Khwaja in each Iqta to assess the income of the Iqtadars. Balban declared the sultan to be the representative (Niyabat-e-Khudai) and reflection of God (Jille Ilahi). Balban consolidated his power by destroying Turkan-i-Chahalgani, it was formed by Iltutmish. He suppressed the revolt of Tugril Khan in Bengal.
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.154

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Fawazil in the Sultanate period meant—
options: extra payment made to the nobles
revenue assigned in lieu of salary
excess amount paid to the exchequer by the Iqtadars
illegal exactions extracted from the peasants
explanation: Fawazil was the extra money to be deposited in the government treasury by the Iqtadars, which was considered surplus land revenue . It was started from the time of Balban.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1998 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.154

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The complete name of Delhi sultan Balban was-
explanation: The complete name of Delhi Sultan Balban was Ghiyasuddin Balban. Balban was the first ruler of Delhi sultanate to consolidate the position and authority of the sultan.
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S. 2004-05 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.154

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following sultan concentrated complete one year to suppress the Meos/Mayos and cutting the forest near Delhi?
explanation: The law and order situation in Delhi and adjoining areas and doab had deteriorated during Balban’s time. Meos (people of Mewat) were so courageous and defiant that they used to plunder the people of Delhi in broad daylight. Balban adopted the policy of blood and iron to deal with these people. He concentrated complete one year to suppress the Mewatis and cutting the forest near Delhi.
source: UPPSC Asst. Forest Conservation Exam 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.154

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who established 'Diwan-i-Arz' department in Delhi sultunate?
explanation: Sultan Balban of the Delhi Sultanate established a military department named 'Diwan-i-Arz'. The chief of Diwan-i-Arz was called 'Ariz-i-Mamalik'. 05.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.154

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements regarding Alauddin Khalji. A. He set up three distinct markets one for food grains, one for cloth and the third for horses. B. A Shahna was postcd in the market. C. The Peasants had to pay land revenue in kind. D. Slaves were transacted in market during his time. Which of the following are correct?
explanation: Alauddin's measures to control the markets and price regulations were one of the most important policy initiatives of his reign. Alauddin Khalji established four separate markets in Delhi- (i) Grain market (Mandi) (ii) Cloth and groceries market (Sarai Adl) (iii) Markets for slave, horse and cattles (iv) Markets for miscellaneous commodities. The market superintendent called Sahana-i-Mandi. Alauddin Khalji was the first Sultan of Delhi who ordered for the measurement of land. Land revenue was collected in cash to peasants. Since a separate market for slaves were exit at that time thus slaves were transacted in market during his time
source: Odisha PSC (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.155

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During Kakatiya period, three Acharyas were popularly known as ''Pandita-traya". Identify them.
options: Sripati Pandita, Mallikarjuna Pandita and Manchana Pandita
Sripati Pandita, Palkuriki Somanatha and Manchana Pandita
Mallikarjune Pandita, Palkuriki Somanatha and Visvesvara Pandita
Visvesvara Pandita, Mallikarjune Pandita and Manchana Pandita
explanation: During Kakatiya Period, three Acharyas were popularly known as Pandita-Traya named as- Mallikarjuna Pandita, Sripati Pandita, Manchana Pandita.
source: TSPSC (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.155

subject: AP & Indian History
question: For which of the following items, Alauddin Khilji sought to fix the cost? (i) Sugarcane (ii) Diamond (iii) Grain (iv) Fish Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
explanation: During the reign of Khalji, Alauddin Khalji issued Regulation to fix the cost of all commodities.
source: Assam PSC (Pre) 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.155

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Arrange the following conquests of Alauddin Khilji in chronological order. 1. Ranthambor 2. Gujarat 3. Warangal 4. Chittor Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code:
explanation: The correct chronological order of conquests of Alauddin Khilji is - Gujarat (1299) Ranthambore (1301), Chittor (1303), Malwa (1305), Siwana (1308), Warangal (1310), Dwarasamudra (1311)and Jalore (1311).
source: UPPCS Pre 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.155

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to Indian history, consider the following statements: 1. The first Mongol invasion of India happened during the reign of Jalal-ud-din Khalji. 2. During the reign of Ala-ud-din Khalji, one Mongol assault marched up to Delhi and besieged the city. 3. Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq temporarily lost portions of north-west of his kingdom to Mongols. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Statement:1 The first Mongol invasion of India happened during the reign of Behram Shah in 1241 AD. Hence statement 1 is not correct. Statement: 2 During the reign of Alauddin Khilji, Mongols invaded India and put a siege around Delhi in
source: UPSC IAS 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.155

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During the reign of which of the following Sultan of Delhi, Hindu gods and Goddesses were worshiped in royal palaces?
explanation: Hindu Gods and Goddesses were worshiped in Delhi Sultanate during the reign of Nasiruddin Khusro Shah (1320). He was the only converted Hindu who sat on the throne of Delhi. According to the Delhi Chronicles Amir Khusrau, Khusrau Khan and his brother belonged to a Hindu military caste or group called Baradu. He killed Mubark Shah to occupy the throne. Ghazi Malik Tughluq the governor of Dipalpur refused to acknowledge Khusro Shah's ascension, so he killed Khusro Shah and ascended the throne of Delhi under the title of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.
source: UPPSC RO-ARO (Pre) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.156

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following Sultan appointed a Special army to protect the boundaries of the empire:
explanation: Sultan Alauddin Khilji (1296 -1316 A.D) maintained a powerful special army to protect boundaries of the empire. He also constructed a fort named Siri for the soldiers protecting the boundaries. He protected his empire from the invasion of Mongols and expanded his empire to a great extent. Medieval History
source: UPPSC RO-ARO (Pre) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.156

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched? State Ruler
explanation: The correct match is as follows- State/Kingdom Ruler Devagiri – Shankaradeva, Ramachandra Deva Warangal – Rudradeva II/Prataprudra Hoysala – Veer Ballal Madurai – Veer Pandya Ramchandra provided Military assistance to him (Rudradeva II) during the siege of Warangal (1310). Prataprudra/ Rudradeva was the last ruler of Kakatiya dynasty.
source: UPPCS (Pre)-2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.156

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Why did Alauddin Khilji introduce a market policy of fixed prices for food grains?
options: For better return to the farmers
To ensure that consumers can directly purchase from farmers
To ensure that market price is equal to the fair price
To ensure that soldiers can live comfortably with low salary
explanation: Alauddin introduced a market policy of fixed prices for food grains specially to ensure that soldiers can live comfortably with low salary, as Allauddin required more soldiers due to recurrent Mongol invasions. Alauddin's economic changes, are regarded as "miracles of medieval history" Alauddin's market policy are as follows- 1. He imposed price restrictions and other reforms. He set prices for various commodities like cereals fabric, slaves & animals. 2. He restricted hoarding, hired supervisors & appointed spies to enforce the rules and severly punished those who broke them.
source: APPSC Group-II 26.02.2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.156

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following introduced land survey and settlement system for tax purpose
explanation: Alauddin Khilji introduced the land survey and settlement system for tax purpose. He imposed a 50% Kharaj tax on the agricultural produce and ordered his ministry to collect the revenue directly from the peasant by eliminating the intermediary village Chiefs.
source: NAGALAND NCS PRELIMS, 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.156

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Assertion (A): Southern expeditions of Alauddin aimed at collection of wealth. Reason (R): He wanted to establish control on Southern states. Code:
options: A & R both are true and R is correct explanation of A
A & R both are true but R is not correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Alauddin wanted to plunder the wealth to strengthen himself for the throne of Delhi. He was not interested in establishing his control on southern states.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1997 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.157

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Assertion (A) : Alauddin introduced price control system in Delhi. Reason (R) : He intended to give minimum salary to the laborers engaged in construction of his palace in Delhi. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below: Code:
options: A & R both are true and R is correct explanation of A
A & R both are true but R is not correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Alauddin Khilji introduced market control system to maintain a regular and strong army. Ziauddin Barani has mentioned about economic reforms of Alauddin Khilji. Alauddin decided the values of foodgrains. He was the first ruler who introduced 'Rationing system'. Alauddin was the first ruler who paid salary to armymen in cash. Statement (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. Ist 2005 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.157

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements related to Alauddin Khilji: I. He charged the land revenue on the basis of measurement of agricultural land II. He executed this revenue system in whole of the sultanate III. He abandoned the rights of provincial governors Choose the correct answer using the codes given below:
options: I , II and III Medieval History
explanation: Alauddin introduced a new system of land measurement called Masahat. Land revenue system introduced by Alauddin was not implemented in the whole state. This land revenue system was implemented only in Delhi and nearby region.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.157

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who had established Diwan-i-Mustakhraj?
explanation: Diwan-i-Mustakhraj was the department of agricultural affairs related to collection of land revenue. Alauddin introduced this department because there was no proper system for determination and collection of land revenue.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.157

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which one of the following Kings of the medieval India began the 'Public Distribution System'?
explanation: Public distribution system was introduced by Sultanate ruler Alauddin Khilji. He introduced Market Control System and made it binding on all traders to sell their product on a fix price determined by the state.
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. Ist Paper 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.157

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Market control system was introduced by:
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1992 UP Lower (Pre) 1998, 200, MPPSC (Pre.) G.S. Ist 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.157

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the ruler of Warangal when it was invaded by Sultanate forces?
explanation: In 1308 AD, Pratap Rudradeva I ( Kakatiya ruler of Warangal) was defeated by Allauddin Khilji's army. After the war, the Koh-i-Noor diamond passed from Kakatiya ownership to that of Alauddin Khilji, along with 20,000 horses and 100 elephants.
source: GUJARAT PSC CIVIL PRE-PAPER-I (21-3-2021) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.157

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The measures taken by Alauddin to control the market price-
options: Enlarged the distance between emperor (sultan) and common man
explanation: Market control system, introduced by Alauddin Khilji, was successful and it ensured the maintenance of a large and regular army. It assured the availability of foodgrains and other products at a fix price. Black marketing (hoarding) was abandoned.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S.-Ist 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.157

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which Sultan of Delhi had charged land revenue at the rate of 50% of the production?
explanation: Alauddin Khilji had introduced the all time highest rate of land revenue (Kharaj) by increasing it up to 50% of actual production determined on the basis of land measurement. Not only this, but, he also imposed house tax (Ghari) and pasture tax (Cherai) on agrarian population. It is to remember that landth revenue rate for Muslim community was only 1/4 of actual production. Khalisa land during Alauddin's reign increased, this was because he withdrew all the land provided to the religious persons and scholars, earlier under various grants. Land granted as 'Inam' and 'waqf' was also taken back.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. - 2006 Jharkhand PSC (Pre.) G.S. Ist Paper, 2013 Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) G.S. 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.158

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During the reign of which Sultan Khalisa land developed maximum?
source: BPSC (Pre) 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.158

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the ruler of Devagiri at the time of Alauddin's invasion?
explanation: Alauddin Khilji invaded Devagiri, state of south India in 1296 AD. Raja Ramchandra Dev was the ruler of Devagiri at that time. Ramchandra was ready to pay Alauddin tax, the tribute. But during 1305-1306 he did not send tax to Delhi. As a result Alauddin sent an army under the leadership of Malik Kafur in 1308. He defeated Ramchandra and arrested him. Kafur brought Ramchandra to Delhi where Alauddin Khilji honoured Ramchandra Dev with the title of ‘Rai Rayan’ (king of kings) and returned his state. Ramchandra Dev returned to Devagiri to rule as a vassal of the Delhi sultanate.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2004-05, 2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.158

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Match the List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer using the codes given below the list : LIST I LIST II A. Ranthambore 1. Karna Dev B. Chittor 2. Raja Rai Ramachandra Medieval History 16 C. Devagiri 3. Hammir Dev D. Gujarat 4. Rana Ratan Singh Code : A B C D A B C D
explanation: The correct match is as follows - Ranthambore Hammir Dev Chittor Rana Ratan Singh Devagiri Raja Rai Ramachandra Gujarat Karna Dev
source: UPPSC RO/ARO (Pre) 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.158

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following Sultans had held the title of Sikandar II?
explanation: Alauddin Khilji was an ambitious ruler. His original name was Ali Gurshap. He held the title of ‘Sikandar-i-Sani’ or Sikandar II. He also wished to introduce new religion but could not do so due resistance of Ulemas.
source: UP Lower (Pre) 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.158

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which Sultan was intended to promulgate a new religion, but Ulema opposed it?
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S., 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.158

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which Sultan of Delhi had held the title of Khalifatullah?
explanation: Qutbuddin Mubarak Khilji (1316-1320), the son and successor of Alauddin Khilji denied the supremacy of Abbasid Caliphate of Baghdad and declared himself as ‘Khalifatullah’ (representative of God). He was murdered by Khusro Khan in 1320 which ended Khilji dynasty.
source: UPPSC Food Safety Inspector Exam. 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.158

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the, map given below: – The route indicated in the map was followed, during the course of his military exploits, by
explanation: The route mentioned in the map was followed by Malik Kafur, the commander of Alauddin Khilji, during his southern expedition.
source: I.A.S. (Pre) G.S. 1995 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.158

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Among the Alauddin’s commanders, who died in the battle against Mongols?
explanation: During Alauddin's reign Delhi Sultanate faced four Mongolian attacks in 1297, 1298, 1299 and 1303 AD. Alauddin faced these attacks successfully and defeated Mongols. In 1299 AD Mongols attack under the leadership of Qutlugh Khwaja which was failed by Alauddin's commander Zafar Khan but Zafar Khan lost his life during the battle (Battle of Kili).
source: BPSC (Pre) 1996 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.159

subject: AP & Indian History
question: “He was free from the rules and the orders of Shariyat, when he attained the Kingship”. This statement of Barani is referred to which Sultan?
explanation: Aforesaid statement is of Ziauddin Barani, which is associated with Alauddin Khilji. Alauddin Khilji was the first Sultanate ruler who denied the interference of Ulemas in state affairs. After ascending to the throne of Delhi, Alauddin told that kingship and religion are two different things which could not be inter-related. All the state affairs should be guided by the laws of state not as per the religious views. He said that the laws of the state are binding for the king. He told to Qazi Mughisuddin that 'he doesn’t care whether any law is as per shariyat norms or not, he will take all necessary steps to protect the interest of the state and its subject as well.'
source: BPSC (Pre) 2003-04 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.159

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Whose army was defeated by the army of Kakatiya rulers in 1303 at Warangal?
explanation: After consolidating himself in Delhi, Alauddin invaded South India in 1303 AD. His first attack was on Warangal, the capital of Kakatiya dynasty in 1303. Warangal army defeated Alauddin’s army this time but again he sent an expedition lead by Malik Kafur in 1309 AD, which was successful. Medieval History
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. Ist 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.159

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What was the boundary between the Delhi Sultan and Mongols during the period of Alauddin Khilji after 1306 A.D.?
explanation: Sindhu (Indus) river was the boundary between Delhi Sultanate and Mongols. Number of attacks were made by Mongols during Alauddin's reign but were restricted up to Indus (Sindhu) river only.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.159

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following commanders of Alauddin became the first Sultan of Tughlaq dynasty?
explanation: Ghazi Malik, was a commander under Alauddin Khilji. He was appointed as the governor of Dipalpur in 1315. He used this period to strengthen himself and after the death of Alauddin Khilji in 1316, he emerged as the most powerful person. In 1320 he killed Khusrau Khan and ascended the throne of Delhi and founded the new (Tughlaq) dynasty. He proclaimed the title of 'Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq'.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.159

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The first Sultan of Delhi who charged ‘Ghari’ or Griha kar (house tax) was?
explanation: Alauddin Khilji was the first Sultan of Delhi who charged house tax (Ghari) on houses and herding tax (Charai) on milk-giving animals.
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. Ist 2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.159

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who constituted military on the basis of decimal system?
explanation: Sultanate ruler Alauddin had established a large army based on decimal system. He was the first sultanate ruler who kept a centralized army. The army was arranged in the group of 10, 100, 1000, and 10000.
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) G.S. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.159

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which dynasty of Delhi Sultanate ruled for shortest period?
explanation: Among these dynasties of Delhi Sultanate Khilji ruled for the minimum period of thirty (30) years only. Tughlaq dynasty ruled for a maximum period of 94 years. Sayyid and Lodhi ruled for the period of 37 and 75 years respectively. Slave dynasty ruled for a period of 84 years. 06.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. Ist 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.159

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following translated 300 volumes of Sanskrit books collected by Firoz Tuglaq during the campaign of Nagarkot?
explanation: The Sanskrit books collected by Firoz Shah Tughlaq during Nagarkot campaign were translated by Azizuddin Khan under the title "Dalail-i-Firoz-Shahi". It is noteworthy that Firoz Shah attacked Nagarkot in Himachal Pradesh in the year 1365 AD and collected those Sanskrit manuscripts from Jwalamukhi Temple Library.
source: UPPCS (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.160

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following Sultans of delhi imposed 'Jizya Tax' on Brahmins for the first time?
explanation: Jizya was a religious tax collected to non- muslims (except Brahmin) in sultanate period, Firoz Shah Tughlaq was the first sultan of Delhi imposed Jizya even from Brahmins.
source: UPPSC (J) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.160

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements regarding Tughlaq architecture.' A. The striking feature of the Tughlaq architecture was the sloping walls, called 'batter' B. The 'batter' is extensively used by Firuz Tughlaq in his buildings. C. Tughlaq generally used costly red sandstone in their buildings Choose the correct answer :
explanation: The striking feature of Tughlaq architecture was the battered wall, it's base much wider than it's top the battered wall is extensively used by Ghyasuddin Tughlaq. Tughlaqs used the cheaper and easily available grey colour stones. Hence statement (A) is correct while statements B and C are incorrect.
source: JKPSC (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.160

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following Sultan had named Devgiri as ‘Quwwat-ul- Islam’?
explanation: Muhammad Bin Tughlaq named Devgiri as Quwwat-ul-Islam' when he shifted the capital to Devgiri from Delhi.
source: UPPSC Asst, Forest Conservator exam 2015 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.160

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Isami, Barni and Ibn Batuta were contemporaries of which Muslim ruler?
explanation: Isami, Barani and Ibn Battuta were contemporaries of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Isami's text 'Futuh Us Salatin' describes the politicals, socio- economic condition of South India in the 14th century and the revolts in South India during the time of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Ibn Battuta was a Moroccan traveler who came to India during the time of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. The name of his book is 'Rihla' in which his travelogue has been described. Ziauddin Barani was a historian and political thinker who wrote 'Tarikh-e-Firozshahi'.
source: UPPSC ACF Mains Paper I 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.160

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which Sultan of Delhi wrote his autobiography?
explanation: Firoz Shah Tughlaq was the ruler of Delhi Sultanate from 1351 to 1388. Firoz Shah wrote his autobiography which is entitled 'Futuhat-e-Firoz Shahi'.
source: UK RO-ARO (Pre.) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.160

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The Sun temple built at Gaya during the sultanate period has an inscription containing the name of a Sultan twice. Who is the Sultan?
explanation: Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq was a Muslim ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty and he reigned over the Sultanate of Delhi. The Dakshinaarka temple in Gaya is an ancient Shrine to the Sun god.
source: OPSC Pre-2020 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.160

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which district was known as 'Shiraj-e-Hind' during the Mughal Era?
explanation: Jaunpur district of Uttar Pradesh is known as 'Shiraj-e-Hind' since the Mughal Era. The city was established by Firoz Shah Tughlaq in 14th century in the memory of his cousin Muhammad Bin Tughlaq (Jauna Khan). In 1394 AD, Malik Sarawar established the Sharqui dynasty in Jaunpur. Sharquis were patrons of art and architecture. They commissioned many temples and mosques in this city. This city was famous as an important centre of learning.
source: ACF/RFO (Mains) Ist 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.160

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the Jain scholar who was consulted and honoured by Sultan Muhammad-bin- Tughlaq?
explanation: In early period of his rule, Muhammad Bin Tughlaq was a secular ruler. He was the first sultan of Delhi who participated in celebration of Hindu festivals publically like Holi. Jain scholars Jinaprabha Suri and Rajshekhar were consulted and honoured by him. Later after the criticism of his Muslim subject and Ulema he showed his inclination for Muslim laws.
source: Haryana PSC (Pre) 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.160

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the Sultan of Delhi to participate in celebration of Holi Festival publically?
source: UPPCS (mains) G.S.2004 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.161

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The Delhi Sultan who constructed canals to the Yamuna and Sutlej rivers for irrigation purpose was______.
explanation: The first known ruler to introduce canal irrigation in India was Firoz Shah Tughlaq. The Sultan of Delhi who is reputed to have built the biggest network of Canal in India was Firoz Shah Tughlaq. He constructed a double system of Canals from Yamuna and Sutlej.
source: TPPSC Group-II Pre-11.11.2016 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.161

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Firoz Shah Tughlaq established a fort in 1354;
explanation: Hisar fort was established by Firoz Shah Tughlaq in 1354 AD. There were four gates in this fort– Delhi gate, Mori gate, Nagauri gate and Talaki gate. It was called Hisar-e-Firoza or Fort of Firoz.
source: Haryana PSC Pre 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.161

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Assertion (A): Muhammad bin Tughlaq issued a new gold coin which was called Dinar by Ibn Batuta/Battuta. Reason (R): Muhammad bin Tughlaq wanted to issue token currency in gold coins to promote trade with West Asian and North African countries. Codes :
options: A and R both are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A and R both are true but R is not correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Muhammad Bin Tughlaq wanted to circulate token currency in Brass and Copper coins because there was shortage of silver in whole world.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.161

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements: Assertion: (A) Token currency plan of Muhammad Bin Tughlaq was failed. Reason: (R) Muhammad Bin Tughlaq had no appropriate control on circulation of currency. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below :
options: A and R both are true and R is correct explanation of A
A and R both are true but R is not correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true Medieval History
explanation: The token currency plan of Muhammad Bin Tughlaq failed because of inappropriate management and non co-operation of state officials and the common people as well. They suspected this plan is against the people’s interest. Muhammad Bin Tughluq promised to exchange the token currency with the gold and silver as and when it is asked by the people. People used to exchange their token money to convert it into gold. Some non state peoples started melting of illegal token coins. This all caused the failure of plan.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.161

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Assertion (A): Muhammad bin Tughluq left Delhi, and, for two years lived in a camp called Swarga-dwari. Reason (R): At that time, Delhi was ravaged by a form of plague and many people died.
options: Both A and R is individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R is individually true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Muhammad Bin Tughlaq’s time is also known for natural disasters along with his failed plans. In this sequence , there was a famine of 12 years under his rule. question: Who were 'Polygars' in South India?
explanation: Polygars or Palaikars were provincial rulers and military commanders in Vijayanagra Empire.
source: UPPCS (Pre) Re-Exam. G.S. 2015 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.169

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements is/are correct? (I) The battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi fought in 1565 CE brought an abrupt end to the Vijayanagar Empire. (II) Domingo Paes and Barbosa visited Vijayanagar. (III) Due to his patronage of art and letters king Krishnadevaraya was known as 'Andhra Bhoja'.
explanation: The battle of Talikota was fought between Sultanates of Deccan and Vijaynagar kingdom on 26 January 1565 AD. The Vijaynagar kingdom suffered a defeat in the battle fought near the villages of Rakshasi and Tangdi. The city of Vijayanagar was mercilessly destroyed and the city was totally abandoned within a few years. So now the focus of the empire shifted to the east where the Aravidu dynasty ruled from Penukonda and it was tried to maintain the identity of the Vijayanagar empire. As a patron of literature and art king Krishnadeva Raya earned the title of Andhra Bhoja.
source: GUJARAT PSC CIVIL PRE-PAPER-I (21-3-2021) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.170

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who owned the title of ‘Andhra Bhoj’?
options: Vijaya Nagara King Krishna Deva Raya
explanation: The ruler of Tuluva dynasty Sri Krishna Deva Raya was famous for his humanity, kind heartedness and judgement. He earned the title of 'Andhra Bhoj' and 'Kannad Rajya Rama Ramana'.
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) GS 1st 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.170

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which one of the following Vijayanagar ruler was the author of 'Amuktamalyada'?
explanation: Amuktamalyada was written by Krishnadeva Raya. It is a master piece of Telugu literature. Krishnadeva Raya was the king of the Vijayanagar Empire reigning between 1509-1529. He was the third ruler of the Tuluva Dynasty.
source: GUJARAT PSC CIVIL PRE-PAPER-I (21-3-2021) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.170

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements and choose the correct answer using the code given below- Statement 1 : Krishnadevaraya, ruler of Vijaynagar wrote the treatise Amuktamalyada Statement 2 : Krishnadevaraya is also known by the name of Andhra Bhoj Statement 3 : Allasani Peddana, the poet laureate well versed in Sanskrit and Tamil, adorned his court. Code :
options: Both the Statements 1 and 2 are true
All the three statements are true Medieval History
explanation: Amuktamalyada is a Telugu epic poem composed by Krishnadevaraya. Hence, Statement (1) is correct. Krishnadevaraya was also called as Andhra Bhoj because of his effort in spreading the Telugu Language. Hence, statement (2) is also correct. However Allasani Peddana was well versed in Sanskrit and Telugu Language and not in Tamil. Hence, statement (3) is incorrect.
source: RAS/RTS (PRE.) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.170

subject: AP & Indian History
question: According to Portuguese writer Nuniz, the women in Vijayanagara Empire were expert in which of the following areas? 1. Wrestling 2. Astrology 3. Accounting 4. Soothsaying Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation: Fernao Nuniz, Portuguese traveller visited the Vijayanagara empire during the reign of Achyuta Deva Raya. According to Nuniz a large number of women were employed in royal palaces as dancers, domestic servants and palanquin bearers. There were also wrestlers, astrologers and soothsayers among them. Some women were also appointed as accountants, judges, bailiffs, and watch women. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.
source: UPSC (IAS) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.170

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to Indian history, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. The Nizamat of Arcot emerged out of Hyderabad State. 2. The Mysore Kingdom emerged out of Vijayanagara Empire. 3. Rohilkhand Kingdom was formed out of the territories occupied by Ahmad Shah Durrani. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation: The Nizamat of Arcot was a dependency of Hyderabad and was under the legal purview of the Nizam of Hyderabad, until its demise. Later it emerged out of Hyderabad. Hence statement (1) is correct. Mysore kingdom emerged as a powerful state under the Wodeyar dynasty, which initially served as a vassal of Vijaynagar empire. Statement (2) is also correct. Rohilkhand state arose in the modern districts of Rampur, Bareilly etc. under the declining Mughal empire in 1721. Ahmad Shah Durrani started invading India from 1748. Hence option C is wrong.
source: UPSC (IAS) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.170

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Nayankara system of the Vijaya-Nagar Empire was modelled on the:
explanation: Under Iqta System- •••• The land of the empire was divided into various large and small tracts known as Iqta and rulers assigned these Iqtas to his soldiers, officers and hobbles. •••• The top grade officers of the army were known as Nayaks or Poligars in the Nayankara system of Vijay Nagar Kingdom. •••• The Nayankara system was modeled on the Iqta system and Iqta system was of sultanate period.
source: OPSC Pre-2020 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.170

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following wrote the text Amuktamalyada?
explanation: Amuktamalyada was composed by Krishnadevaraya,th the emperor of Vijayanagara in the early 16 century. Amuktamalyada is a Telugu epic poem. Krishnadevaraya was the third ruler of the Tuluva Dynasty who presided over the Vijayanagara Empire at its zenith.
source: NAGALAND NCS PRELIMS, 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.171

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During whose reign the Persian envoy Abdur Razaak came to Vijayanagara:
explanation: The Persian envoy Abdur Razaak comes to Vijayanagara Kingdom at the time of Devaraya-II in the year 1443. He was a timurid chronicler and a scholar. Vijaynagar is located in the modern era Indian state of Karnataka along the bank of the Tungabhadra River. Note- Megasthenes, ambassador of Seleucus I Nicator was the first foreign traveler to India.
source: NAGALAND NCS PRELIMS, 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.171

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Persian ambassador, who took a tour of Vijayanagar Empire was
explanation: Abd-ur-Razzak was a Persian ambassador, who took a tour of Vijaynagara Empire during the period of Deva Raya II.
source: UP PSC ACF/RFO (Mains) 2020 Paper I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.171

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Abd-ur-Razzak came to Vijaya Nagara during—
explanation: Deva Raya II was a great Emperor of Vijayanagara Empire. He belonged to Sangama dynasty. Persian ambassador Abd-ur-Razzak visited Vijayanagara Empire during 1443-1444 AD. He gave a brief account of Vijayanagara Empire and praised the Vijayanagara administration and its prosperity.
source: UP UDA/LDA (M) 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.171

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Ghatika Yantra was a time measuring device under the Reddy's rule. What was it called?
explanation: The Ghatika Yantra, a water-based clock invented by ancient Indians, is a unique sort of clock. Ghatika Yantra was a time measuring device under Reddy's rule called 'Ghatikagara'. Time was measured in ancient India by a water clock called Ghatika.
source: APPSC Group-II Screening-2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.171

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What was the important part in coastal Andhra where theth shipth building activity flourished during 16 and 17 centuries?
explanation: Masulipatnam is a city in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh. Masulipatnam, sometimes known as Machlipatnam, is a town on the Krishna River's delta. Masulipatnam literally means "fish port town." The shipbuilding activity in Machilipatnam (Masula) flourished during 16th and 17th centuries.
source: APPSC Group-II Screening-2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.171

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Identify the chief item of export during Vijayanagar rule :
explanation: The Vijayanagar Kingdom developed into a centre of trade. The Chief items of exports were cotton and silk cloths, spices, rice, iron and sugar.
source: Nagaland NCS Prelime-2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.171

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Building 'Kalyana Mandapas' was a notable feature in the temple construction in the kingdom of
explanation: In the Vittala/Vitthala temple of Hampi, pavilions or mandaps that were meant to celebrate the marriages of deities were known as Kalyana Mandapas. These were the features of Vijayanagara empire.
source: IAS (Pre) 2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.171

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What was the practice adopted by the Vijayanagar Kings to protect the inhabitants within a fortified area from starvation due to sieges by enemy armies?
options: Large granaries were built within the fortified area to store grains
Secrete pathways were maintained to transport groceries into fortified areas
Large agricultural tracts were incorporated within the fortified area
The forts were built on hills to prevent siege by the enemy
explanation: The large agricultural tracts were incorporated within the fortified area adopted by the Vijayanagar kings to protect the inhabitants.
source: APPSC GROUP-I (7-5-2017) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.171

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements in reference to taxation system of Vijayanagara ruler Krishnadev Raya: 1. Land revenue was determined on the basis of the quality of land. 2. Owners of the Private factories were paying industrial tax. Which of the above statements is/are true?
explanation: Land revenue was determined on the basis of the quality (fertility) of theth land.th The rate of land revenue varied from 1/6 to 1/4 of production. Industrial tax was also levied on various industries in the Empire.
source: IAS Pre 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.172

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements— 1. Narasimha Saluva ended the Sangama dynasty and established new Saluva dynasty clinching their throne. 2. Veer Narsimha clinched the throne from last Saluva ruler 3. Veer Narsimha was succeeded by his younger brother Krishnadeva Raya 4. Krishna Deva Raya's half brother Achyutadeva Raya succeded him. The true statements among the above is/are-
explanation: Veerupaksha Raya II was the last ruler of Sangama dynasty. He was dethroned by one of his chieftains Saluva Narasimha who founded the new dynasty called Saluva dynasty. Killing the last ruler of Saluva dynasty 'Narasimha Raya II,' Vira Narasimha founded the ‘Tuluva dynasty’. He was succeeded by his younger brother Krishnadeva Raya. Achyuta Deva Raya was the cousin brother of Krishnadeva Raya who became the successor of Krishnadeva Raya. Thus all the statements are true.
source: IAS Pre 2004 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.172

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Sayana, ‘A noted commentator on Vedic Epics existed during which one of the following’s period?
explanation: Sāyaṇa, also called Sayanacharya was a Sanskrit Mimansa scholar from the Vijayanagara Empire of South India. An important commentator on the Vedas, he flourished under King Bukka I and his successor Harihara II. His major work is Vedartha Prakasha commentary on the Vedas. Sayana was a minister, and subsequently prime minister in Bukka Raya's court, and wrote much of his commentary, with his brother and other Brahmins during his minister-ship.
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) 2002-03 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.172

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The remains of which of the following places represents the ancient capital of Vijay Nagar Kingdom?
explanation: Hampi is the place which represents the capital of Viyayanagara Empire. Hampi was declared world heritage site in 1986. Hampi, now a village and a temple town in Karnataka is one of the most historically rich places. Hampi is also known as Pampa Kshetra. This name was derived from the famous Tungbhadra river Pampa.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2008, 2007 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.172

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which city had Krishna Deva Raya founded?
explanation: Krishna Deva Raya had founded the city of Nagalapur in the memory of his mother, Nagala Devi and built tanks, temples, gopurams etc.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.172

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who were the eight jewels in the court of Krishna Deva Raya?
explanation: Krishna Deva Raya (1509-1529 AD) was a great ruler of Vijayanagara. He was a great warrior and poet and patron of scholars. There were eight great poets of Telugu language in his court known as Ashtadiggajas. These were Allasani, Nandi Thimmana, Ramanbhadrudu, Pingali Surana, Ramarajabhushanudu, Tenali Ramakrishna, Bhattumurty, Dhurjati. The Rule of Krishna Deva Raya was the golden period of Telugu literature. He himself was a great scholar of Telugu and Sanskrit. His major creations are ‘Amuktamalyad’ in Telugu and Jambavati-Kalyanam, Madalasacharita and Satyavadu-Parinaya in Sanskrit.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S.2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.172

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Ruler of famous Vijaya Nagara Empire Krishna deva Raya was the golden period of which literature?
source: UP UDA/LDA (Pre) 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.172

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Eight Jewels were in whose court?
source: UP UDA/LDA spl 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.172

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The famous temple of Vijaya Nagara ‘Hazara Temple’ was constructed during whose reign?
explanation: Hazara temple is dedicated to Lord Ram situated at Hampi built in early 15th century by Deva Raya II. The name was Hazara Rama literally meaning thousand Ram. It has story of Ramayana depicted on its walls.
source: MPPSC Pre 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.172

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following ruler of Vijaya Nagara had started the recruitment of Muslims in his army?
explanation: Deva Raya II was the first Vijayanagara ruler who recruited Muslim archer in his army. He imported the Arabian horses for cavalry. He was defeated by Bahmani ruler Ferozshah and married his daughter with Sultan and surrendered a part of Raichur Doab in his favour. This enabled him to cross Tungabhadra river and to recover Mudkal.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.172

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which ruler of Vijayanagara had sent an Embassy to the Emperor of China?
explanation: Vijayanagra ruler Bukka I (1356-77) sent an embassy to China. His title was Vedamarga Pratisthapaka.
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.173

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was Niccolo-de' Conti?
options: An Italian traveler who visited Vijay Nagar Empire
explanation: Niccolo-de' Conti was an Italian traveler who visited Vijayanagara Empire during the reign of Deva Raya I of Sangama dynasty. He gave a brief account of Vijaynagara Empire.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S.1st 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.173

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which was the biggest administrative unit in Tamil region of Vijaya Nagara Empire?
explanation: In terms of administrative convenience, the Vijayanagara Empire was divided into several smaller units. This division were as follows: Mandalam (Province)-Kottam or Walnadu (district)- Nadu (Paragana)-Melagram-Ur. Some group of villages were called Sthal or Sima.
source: Ancient & Medieval History GS · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.173

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What was the main feature of financial system of Vijaya Nagara Empire?
explanation: Like other kingdoms of the contemporary period land revenue was the main source of income of Vijayanagara Empire. Some other taxes levied in Vijaynagar Empire were- wealth tax, Industrial tax, custom duty from ports, trade tax, marriage tax etc. No marriage tax was levied from the pairs in case of widow remarriage.
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S.1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.173

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What is meant by ‘Athavan’?
explanation: Athavan during Vijayanagara Empire was the department of land revenue and it was responsible for the collection of land revenue.
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) G.S. · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.173

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Two statements are given below one is assertion A and second is reason R: Assertion- (A) : Saluva Narsimha put an end to old dynasty and assumed the royal title. Medieval History 18 Reason- (R) : He wanted to save the kingdom from further degeneration and disintegration. Which of the following is true in reference to above statements?
options: A and R both are true and R is correct explanation to A
A and R both are true but R is not the correct explanation to A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Saluva Narasimha clinched the throne of Vijayanagara and established a new dynasty ‘Saluva’ because he wanted to maintain the law and order situation in the kingdom which was destabilized after the death of Virupaksha and his son Praudh Raya's inability to reinstate the kingdom and save the kingdom from further decline. Thus both the statements are true and R is the correct explains of A.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.173

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following Vijaya Nagara ruler had permitted Portuguese to construct a Church in Vellore?
explanation: Venkatapati Raya or Venkata II (1585–1614 AD) was the ruler of Vijayanagara Empire with bases in Penukonda, Chandragiri and Vellore. His reign of three decades saw a revival of the strength and prosperity of the empire. Venkatapati shifted his capital from Penukonda to Chandragiri, which was in further south near the Tirupathi hills. After 1604, he shifted capital from Chandragiri to Vellore Fort, which was used as a major base. Venkata II had permitted Portuguese to construct a Church in Vellore.
source: UP UDA/LDA spl.2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.173

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following had established a new city on south bank of the tributary river of Krishna and started ruling in the region as representative of the deity about which it is said that all the land in south of Krishna river belonged to that Deity.
explanation: Harihara-I and Bukka brothers rebelled against Muhammad Bin Tughlaq of Delhi Sultanate and established a Hindu Kingdom of Vijayanagara located on the bank of Tungabhadra river.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1st 2015 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.173

subject: AP & Indian History
question: When Wadiyar dynasty established in Mysore, who was the ruler of Vijaya Nagara Empire?
explanation: Venkata II of Aravidu dynasty was the king of Vijayanagara at the time of establishment of Mysore state by Wadiyar in 1610 AD.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.173

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Poetess who had mentioned about the victory expeditions of her husband in poetic form in her creation ‘Madura Vijayam’ was:
explanation: Ganga Devi and her Sanskrit poetic work Madura Vijayam have made immense contribution to South Indian History. Gangadevi was the chief queen of Kumara Kampana II (1343-1379), the son of Bukka I. She accompanied her husband in his southern expedition. She gave minute details of her husband’s expedition and the condition of Madurai in her creation Madura Vijayam.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2000 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.173

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Identify the Vijaya Nagara ruler who clinched Goa from Bahmanians?
explanation: The third ruler of Sangama dynasty of Vijaya Nagara Harihara II had clinched Goa from Bahmanians.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1995 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.174

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With whom had Vijaya Nagara ruler Krishna Deva Raya fought the battle of Golconda?
explanation: Quli Qutub Shah, Sultan of Golconda attacked on Vijayanagara and took possession on some part of Vijayanagara Empire while Krishna Deva Raya was busy in the battle with Gajpati ruler of Odisha. Krishna Deva Raya sent his army led by Saluva Timma against Golconda. Quli Qutub Shah was defeated in the battle in 1512.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.174

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Coronation of which of the following has completed more than 500 Years?
explanation: Coronation of Krishna Deva Raya (Tuluva dynasty), who became the ruler of Vijayanagara in 1509 AD has completed more than 500 years.
source: UPPCS (Mains) spl. G.S. 1 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.174

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The Ruling Dynasties Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva were associated with
explanation: The Ruling dynasties Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva were associated with Vijaynagar kingdom. Sangam dynasty was first ruling dynasty of Vijaynagar.
source: CGPSC Pre 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.174

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The capital of Vijaynagar Empire was situated on the bank of which river?
explanation: The Vijaynagar empire was established in 1336 by Harihara-I and Bukka Raya-I. The capital city of Vijaynagar empire was Hampi, which is situated at the bank of river Tungabhadra. B. Bahamani Dyansty
source: JPSC (Pre) 2024 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.174

subject: AP & Indian History
question: He dominated and extended the Bahmani kingdom further south. He was granted the title 'Chief of the Merchants' (Malik-ul- Tujjar), He divided the kingdom into eight provinces or tarafs. He was also a great patron of arts and built a magnificent madarasa in the capital, Bidar. Who was the person referred to above?
explanation: The person who referred to above was Mahmud Gawan. He was the vakil as well as the wazir of Muhammad Shah-III the Bahamani Kingdom saw a resurgence under his guidance. As per Meadows Taylor after the death of Mahmud Gawan the Bahmani kingdom began to decline and disintegrate.
source: JKPSC (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.174

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Mahmud Gawan was the minister of
explanation: Mahmud Gawan was a prime minister in the Bahamani Kingdom of Deccan.
source: Kerala (KAS) PSC-2020 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.174

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During which year Bahmani kingdom was founded?
explanation: Bahmani kingdom was founded by Alauddin Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu) in 1347 AD during Muhammad Bin Tughlaq reign. His capital was Gulbarga. The last ruler of Bahmani kingdom was Kallimullah Shah.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S.1 2005 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.174

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the founder of Bahmani Kingdom?
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S.2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.174

question: Bahmani Kingdom was established by-
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) G.S. 2002-03 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.175

question: Who among the following was the founder of Bahmani Kingdom in south?
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1993 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.175

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Bahmanith Kingdom was foundedth in-
explanation: Bahmani kingdom was founded in 14th century AD.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.175

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which statements is/are correct regarding the book ‘Mirat-e-Sikandari’? 1. There is a description of the happiness and prosperity of the Kingdom of Sultan Mahmud Begada of Gujarat. 2. There is a description of proper arrangement for the security of trade routes. Select the correct answer from the code given below : Code :
explanation: The book Mirat-e-Sikandari was written by Sikander Bin. Muhammad Majhu, the book describes the happiness and prosperity of kingdom of Sultan Mahmud Begada of Gujarat and also describes proper arrangement for the security of trade routes. Hence, both statements are correct. C. Other Provincial Dynasties
source: UPPSC RO/ARO 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.175

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Arrange these Medieval Rulers of Mewar in chronological order: (1) Hammir (2) Rana Kumbha (3) Rana Mokal (4) Rana Lakha Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The correct chronological orders of rulers of Mewar is as - Rana Hammir, one of important sisodia rulers extended the frontiers of his kingdom and his influence was recognised by neighbouring territories. Kshetasimha, the son and successor of Hammir killed in family quarrel and was succeeded by two weak rulers, Lakha and Mokala respectively and then succeeded by Rana Kumbha Karan.
source: Himachal PSC (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.175

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During the Qutb Shahi period, both the Hindu and Muslim elite wore dresses consisting of Kulah and Qaba. What do these two terms mean?
explanation: During the Qutb shahi period, both the Hindu and Muslim elite wore dresses consisting of Kulah and Qaba which was generally known as cap and coat respectively.
source: TSPSC (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.175

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah of Bijapur is better known as
explanation: The tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah of Bijapur is better known as Gol Gumbaz. Gol Gumbaz is the most famous monument in Vijayapura. It is the second largest dome ever built, next in size only to St. Peter's Basilica in Rome.
source: Sikkim PSC (Pre) 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.175

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The famous ruler of Mewar who got repaired the fort of Achalgarh?
explanation: Achalgarh fort situated in the north of Mount Abu, is the only hill station in Rajasthan. The fort was originally built by the Paramara dynasty rulers and rebuilt, modernized and named as Achalgarh by Maharana Kumbha in 1452. The Achaleswar Mahadeva Temple is nearby where a toe of Lord Shiva is worshipped.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S.2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.175

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Find the pair not correctly matched:
explanation: Yusuf Adilshah was the founder of the sultanate of Bijapur, not Ahmednagar.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2004 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.175

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following ruler of medieval Rajasthan was known as ‘Abhinav Bharatacharya’?
explanation: Maharana Kumbha was the ruler of Mewar from 1433 to 1468 AD. He was regarded ‘as Hindu Surrtran’ and 'Abhinava Bharatacharya'.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 1996 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.175

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following place represents ‘Dwarsamudra’ the capital of Hoysala Kings?
explanation: Halebeedu or Halebidu is a town located in Hassan district of Karnataka, India. Halebidu represents ‘Dwarasamudra’ the regal capital of the Hoysala Empire in the 12th century.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.175

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the last ruler of Sharqi dynasty of Jaunpur?
explanation: Hussain Shah was the last ruler of the Sharqi dynasty of Jaunpur. This dynasty was founded by Malik Sarwar in 1394 AD. It is noteworthy that the city of Jaunpur was founded in the 14th century by Firoz Shah Tughlaq in memory of his cousin Muhammad Bin Tughlaq, whose real name was 'Jauna Khan'.
source: UPPSC ACF Mains Paper I 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.176

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the last ruler of 'Jaunpur State'?
explanation: The city of Jaunpur was established by Ferozshah Tughlaq in the memory of his brother Muhammad Tughlaq. Sharqi dynasty was established by Khwaja Jahan in 1394 AD. The last ruler of Sharqi dynasty was Hussain Shah. Bahlul Lodi defeated him and merged the Jaunpur state in Delhi Sultanate.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. I 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.176

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which one of the following Muslim rulers was called ‘Jagadguru’ by his subjects due to his faith in secularism?
explanation: Ibrahim Adilshah was a secular ruler of Bijapur Sultanate. He was a good administrator, artist, poet and patron of the arts and scholars and had a title Jagadguru Badshah. His subjects called him ‘Jagadguru’ and ‘Adil Baba’.
source: (I.A.S. (Pre) G.S. 2000) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.176

explanation: The Sankaracharya was a great thinker, distinguished philosopher andth leader of the Hindu revivalist movement of the 9 century andth Ramanuja was born in modern day Chennai in the 12 century. Hence statement (A) is incorrect. question: The world's second tallest statue in sitting pose of Ramanuja was inaugurated by the Prime Minister of India at Hyderabad recently. Which one of the following statements correctly represents the teachings of Ramanuja?

explanation: Ramanuja was deeply influenced by the Alvars. He firmly believed that intense devotion to Vishnu was the best means to attain salvation. He propounded the doctrine of Vishishtadvaita. The outdoor 216-ft Statue of Equality is the world’s second tallest statue featuring a sitting posture. It is composed of ‘panchaloha’, a combination of five metals comprising gold, silver, copper, brass, and zinc. subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statements are correct? (i) Tukaram the Bhakti Saint of Maharashtra is known for creating a background for Maratha nationalism and also opposed all social distinctions (ii) Chaitanya, also known as Sri Gauranga was a popular Vaishnava saint and reformer from Bengal (iii) Chishti was the earliest sufi order to have entered in India (iv) Gujarat was an important centre of the mystic saints or Sufis Medieval History
explanation: Bhakti saint of Maharashtra Tukaram (AD 1598-1650),was a contemporary of Shivaji. He was responsible for creating a background for Maratha nationalism. He opposed all social distinctions. The importance of women in society also increased because the Bhakti movement gave equal importance to them. Chaitanya (1486-1533 AD) also known as Sri Gauranga, was a popular Vaishnava Saint and reformer from Bengal. He was born of Brahmin parents at Nadia, West Bengal. After his education he became a teacher. Chisti order was the earliest Sufi order to arrive in India. It was introduced by the Moinuddin Chishti in Lahore (Punjab) and Ajmer in the middle of the 12th century CE. He was eighth in the line of succession from the founder of the Chishti Order.. During the Muslim rule (A.D. 1206 to 1707) Muslim Sultans of Gujarat had given asylum to Sufi saints. These saints were putting before the people Mohammad Saheb's principles of socio-economic equality and brotherhood in simple style. As a result a number Hindus turned towards Islam and Gujarat became an important centre of the mystic saints or Sufis.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-26.12.21 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.178

explanation: Warkari is a sect (religious movement) within the bhakti spiritual tradition of Vaishnavite Hinduism and geographically associated with the Indian state of Maharashtra. The promoter of Warkari sect was Saint Dhyaneshwar. Warkaris worshiped Vitthal (also known as Vithoba), the Presiding deity of Pandharpur, regarded as incarnation of Lord Krishna. Saints and gurus of the bhakti movement associated with the Warkaris include Dhyaneshwar, Namdev, Eknath, and Tukaram, Gadge Maharaj. All of these were accorded the title of Saint.

question: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the famous sattriya dance? (i) Sattriya is a combination of music, dance and drama (ii) It is a centuries-old living tradition of Vaishnavites of Assam (iii) It is based on classical Ragas and Talas of devotional songs composed by Tulsidas, Kabir and Mirabai
explanation: Sattriya originated in Sattra, monastery, as a part of the Neo-Vaishnavite movement started by Srimanta Sankardev in Assam. He propagated the “ek sharan naama dharma”(chanting the name of one God devotedly). It was introduced in the 15th century A.D. Sattriya was given the status of classical dance in the year 2000 by the Sangeet Natak Akademi. The themes performed are mostly on Radha Krishna and other myths. It consists of dhemali, drum playing, known as gayan bayan, where several men play drums, in various talas (rhythms) and also use hand gestures. Popular Artists are Guru Jatin Goswami and Sharodi Saikia among others. It is based on devotional songs composed by Sankardeva.

question: Which of the following statements are correct? (1) Tulsidas and Mirabai are included in the Nirguna sect of saints (2) Two branches, Ram Bhakti and Krishna Bhakti, became popular in Saguna Bhaktidhara (3) Pustimargiya thought is depicted in the speech/words of Surdas
explanation: The Bhakti movement of Hinduism saw two ways of imaging the nature of the divine (Brahman) - Nirguna and Saguna. The major exponents of Nirguna school were Kabir Das and Guru Nanak while followers of Saguna sect were Vallabhacharya, Tulsidas, Surdas, Mirabai, Chaitanya, etc. Saguna was envisioned and developed as with form attributes. There are two branches of Saguna: Ram Bhakti and Krishna bhakti. Pushtimarg was expanded by Surdas, Krishnadas, Kumbhanadas, Parmananda Das, etc. who were disciples of Vallabhacharya.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-26.12.21 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.179

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Growth of vernacular literature in Medieval India was the greatest contribution of
explanation: Growth of Vernacular Literature in Medieval India was the greatest contribution of Bhakti movement. In the rise of vernacular tradition bhakti, particularly Vaishnava Saguna Bhakti tradition played a key role. The Bhakti movement empowered the underbelly of Indian society in fundamental ways and also provided the required impetus for the growth of vernacular literature. In the Indian culture, traditionally religious or scholarly works were written in Prakrit, Tamil and Sanskrit. With the rise of the Bhakti movement from the 8th century on-wards, religious works began to be created in Kannada, and Telugu, and from the 12th Century onward in many other Indian languages throughout the different regions of India. For example, the Ramayana, one of Hinduism’s sacred epics in Sanskrit, had vernacular versions such as Ramacharitamanasa, a Hindi version of the Ramayana by the 16th century poet Tulsidas.
source: Kerala (KAS) PSC-2020 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.179

They are venerated especially in Vaishnavism, which regards Vishnu or Krishna as the Supreme Being.
source: UPPCS Pre 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.182

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following leaders of the Bhakti sect was influenced with Islam?
explanation: Namdev was only Bhakti Saint who was influenced with Islamic thoughts. He travelled far and wide and engaged in discussion with Sufi Saints in Delhi.
source: UP UDA/LDA spl. (Pre) 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.182

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Maluk Das was a saint poet of—
explanation: Sant Maluk Das (1574-1682 AD) was a saint of the medieval Hindu renaissance born in Kara, near Allahabad. Maluk Das was a great poet-saint of India with a universal message of equality, brotherhood among men, and oneness of God. Living at a time when India was passing through a period of spiritual and physical turmoil he, like other known saints, appeared to revive the true spirit of religion and bring peace and harmony among mankind.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.183

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Vaishnavism in Kamarupa was popularized by :
explanation: The initiator of ‘Ekasarana’ Sect, Shankar Deva was propagator of Vaishnavism in Kamroop (Assam) region. Born at Alipukhari village in Navagoan district of Assam in 1449 AD, Shankar Deva was a noted scholar, poet and dramatist of Assamese language. He had written various religious epics namely, Kurukshetra, Gunamala, Kaliyadaman Yatra, Rukmini harana, Parijat harana, etc. His creation ‘Bhakti Ratnakar’ in Sanskrit language is basic religious epic for the Vaishnavites in Assam. He is recognized as Chaitanya of Assam. He was against idol worship and sacrificial acts. He was the only saint of Krishna bhakti school of Vashnavism who was against the idol worship (idolatry) of lord Krishna.
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.183

Ibrahim Lodi lost the battle of Panipat in 1526 and Babur rose to power, hence Guru Nanak was preaching at the time of decline of Lodi dynasty and the coronation of Babur. Tyagaraja was a composer and vocalist of carnatic music. He was born in may 1767 in Tiruvarur and died in January. 1847.

explanation: The verses of Farid-ud-din are found in Adi- Granth of Sikhs. Farid-ud-din was the disciple of Qutb- ud-din Bakhtiyar Kaki his activities were limited to Hansi and Ajodhan (in modern day Haryana and Punjab respectively). explanation: The Sufi saints made themselves popular by adopting musical recitation called, 'Sama' to create a mood of nearness to God. Sufi music refers to the devotional music of the Sufis, inspired by the work of Sufi poets like Khwaja Gulam, Baba Farid, Amir Khusrou, Bulleh Shah etc.

question: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A

question: Consider the following statements in reference to Sufism in the history of India- 1. Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi was contemporary of Ibrahim Lodi. 2. Sheikh Nasiruddin Chiragh-e-dehlavi was the disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya. 3. Aurangzeb was the contemporary of Sheikh Salim Chisti. 4. Qadiriyya Order of Sufism in India was introduced at first by Sheikh Nizamatullah and Makhdoom Muhammad Jilani. Which of these statements are true?
explanation: Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi was an Indian Islamic scholar, a Hanafi jurist, and a prominent member of the Naqshbandī Sufi order. He was contemporary of Mughal Emperors Akbar and Jahangir. Sheikh Nasiruddin Chiragh-e-Dehlavi was the disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya. Aurangzeb was not contemporary of Salim Chishti. Qadiriyya order of Sufism was introduced in India by Sheikh Niamatullah and Makhdoom Mohammad Jilani. Thus only statement 2 & 4 are true.

It is a pilgrimage site for Muslims. Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya was born in Badayun district of Uttar Pradesh in 1238 AD. Amir Khusrau and Amir Hasan Dehlavi were among his disciples. Rahim was among the nine gems of Akbar. He was honored with the title of ‘Khan-e-Khana’ by Akbar. He is credited for the translation of Baburnama in Persian language. Raskhan was a devotee of Krishna.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following is said to have witnessed the reigns of eight Delhi Sultans?
explanation: Abul Hasan Yamin-ud-din Khusrou (1253- 1325 AD) was a Sufi singer, musician, poet, historian and scholar who lived under the Delhi Sultanate. He was born in Patiyali town of Uttar pradesh in 1253. He was an iconic figure in the cultural history of Medieval India. He was a mystic and a spiritual disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya of Delhi, India. He wrote poetry primarily in Persian, but also in Hindavi. A vocabulary in verse, the Ḳhāliq Bārī, containing Arabic, Persian, and Hindavi terms is often attributed to him. Khusrau is sometimes referred to as the "voice of India" or "Parrot of India" (Tuti-e-Hind), and has been called the "father of Urdu literature including Khari Boli (Hindavi)" He was also regarded as the 'father of Qawwali.' He introduced the Ghazal style of song in India. Khusrau is credited for the invention of the Sitar. His major works are: Qiran-us-Sa'dain, Khazain-ul-Futuh, Tughlaqnama, Ashiqa, Deval Rani and Khizr Khan, Nuh-i-Siphir, Ezaz-e-Khusravi, Afzal ul-Fawaid, etc. He died in 1325 AD.He had witnessed the reign of eight Delhi Sultans and adorned their courts. These were- (i) Ghiyasuddin Balban (ii) Kaikubad (iii) Shamsuddin Kayumars (iv) Jalaluddin Firoz Khilji (v) Alauddin Khilji (vi) Qutubuddin Mubarak Shah Khilji (vii) Khusrau Khan (viii) Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.194

explanation: The Mughal Empire was founded by Babur. • He founded the Mughal Empire after his victory in the Battle of Panipat (1526) and the Battle of Khanwa. • He was a direct descendant of Timur, from the Barlas clan, through his father and also a descendant of Genghis Khan through his mother.

question: Two statements are given below, one is assertion A and another is reason R. Examine these statements carefully and choose the correct answer using the codes given below: Assertion (A) : The battle of Khanwa was certainly more decisive and significant than the First Battle of Panipat. Medieval History 20 Reason (R) : Rana Sanga, the Rajput hero, was certainly a more formidable adversary than Ibrahim Lodi. Codes:
options: Both A and R are individually true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true, but R is NOT a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
explanation: After winning the battle of Panipat, Babur diverted his attention to Rana Sanga, the formidable Rajput King. On 17th March, 1527 the armies of Babur and Rana Sanga fought against each other in the battle of Khanwa. Once again the Canons and Guns of Babur wreaked havoc in the opposition camp. The Rajputs under Rana Sanga were defeated and Babur became the undisputed ruler of India. In fact, winning the battle of Khanwa was more important for Babur than the Battle of Panipat.

question: What was the main cause behind the victory of Babur in the battle of Panipat?
explanation: Victory of Babur was due to the scientific combination of cavalry and artillery. After all these, Babur was an efficient military organizer and commander which contributed in his victory.

question: The Mughal Emperor whose life teaches the lesson of patience and determination was—

He was defeated and ousted from his kingdom and became a wanderer but due to his determination and enthusiasm, not only he retained his kingdom but also successfully established a large Empire in India which lasted for more than 300 years.

question: What was the exchange rate of copper Dam and silver Rupiya during Sher Shah's period?
explanation: Sher Shah issued coins in silver and copper. The silver coins were known as Rupiya, which is still used in India as a general term for money. The copper coins in which the large numbers of transactions were made by the masses were known as Dam. The Rupiya of Sher Shah can be used as a rich source of historical facts. The ratio of exchange between the Dam and the Rupiya was 64 : 1. The ratios between the various gold coins and the silver ones were fixed on a permanent basis.

During the British rule of colonial India, the road was renamed as the Grand Trunk Road.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Reforms Initiated by Sher Shah Suri Include— 1. Revenue reforms 2. Administrative reforms 3. Military reforms 4. Reforms in currency system Choose the correct answer from the following codes:
explanation: Some important reforms of Sher Shah Suri are : 1. Sher Shah first of all constructed roads and inns for the growth of trade and commerce. It now became easier for the merchants and travellers to travel from one part of the country to the other. 2. In order to make taxation system simple, he abolished all the duties on the goods except two. Only goods brought into the country were charged and duties were levied on the goods that were sold. 3. Sher Shah established the reformed system of currency that lasted throughout the Mughal period. It was maintained by the East India Company down to 1835 and was the basis of the British currency thereafter. 4. Sher Shah abolished the inconvenient coinage of mixed metal and struck well-executed tri-metal pieces in gold, silver and copper. These were produced according to a fixed standard of both weight and fineness.
source: Uttarakhand UDA (Pre) 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.202

Akbar issued a Declaration or Mahzar. Mahzar means pronouncement, declaration an option. It also implies petition. He removed the Chief Preacher at Fatehpur Sikari and himself mounted the pulpit of Jama Masjid, Fatehpur Sikri on June 22, 1579. question: The “Dahsala” system developed by Raja Todar Mal was for

Measurement of land once in 10 years for fixing area of assessment
Collection of revenue on the basis of average of produce and prices in the last 10 years
Sharing of crop between the farmer and the State for 10 years
explanation: Dahsala System or Zabti System was introduced by Raja Todar Mal, the able finance minister of Akbar who had honed his skills under his first master Sher Shah Suri. In this system the average produce of 10 years was derived. One-third of this average produce was fixed in Rupees per Bigha and fixed as a share of the state. subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who had introduced Mansabdari System in India?
explanation: Mansabdari system was introduced by Akbar. It was an outstanding feature of the Mughal administration. Under this system, every officer of the Mughal empire was given a rank or ‘mansab’. The lowest rank in the system was 10 whereas the highest was 10000 for the nobles. It was a grading system used by the Mughals to decide the rank, salary and military responsibilities of the Nobles. The ranks were divided into 'zat' and 'sawar'. 'Zat' fixed the personal status of a noble and the salary paid to him. The 'sawar' implied the number of cavalrymen or sawar, a mansabdar was required to maintain. For every ten cavalrymen, the mansabdar had to maintain twenty horses.The mansabdars got their salaries in terms of revenue assignments called 'jagirs'.
source: UP RO/ARO G.S. 1st 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.204

source: NAGALAND NCS PRELIMS, 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.205
