question: Arrange the following events of Akbar’s period in chronological order— 1. Abolition Of Jaziya/Jizya 2. Construction of Ibadatkhana 3. Sign on Mahzar 4. Introduction of Din-i-Ilahi Choose the correct answer from the codes given below:
explanation: The correct chronological order is: 1. Abolition of Jaziya/Jizya: Jizya was abolished by the third Mughal emperor Akbar, in 1564. 2. Construction of Ibadatkhana: The Ibādat Khāna (House of Worship) was a meeting house built in 1575 AD by the Mughal Emperor Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri to gather spiritual leaders of different religions, so as to conduct a discussion on the teachings of the respective religious leaders. 3. Sign of Mahzar: A declaration called ‘Mahzar’ was passed by Akbar in order to vest in himself the power to choose between different interpretations of the Islamic law. This declaration helped him to strengthen his power with respect to several interpretations of law in his empire.
source: UP UDA/LDA (Pre) 2006 UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.205

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Akbar’s rule is known for— (1) Winning of territories (2) For his administrative system (3) For Judicial administration (4) For religious orthodoxies Choose the correct answer from the codes given below:
explanation: The rule of Mughal Emperor Akbar is known for not only for stability and prosperity but also for the expansion of territory of the Empire and it’s unique administrative and judicial system.
source: Uttarakhand UDA (Pre) 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.205

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following observations relating to the reign of the Mughal Emperor Akbar : 1. Akbar strengthened his control on the nobility and the army by introducing the mansabdari system. 2. Under the mansabdari system, every officer was assigned a rank (mansab). 3. The ranks were divided into three : zat, sawar and chehra. Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
explanation: Mansabdari system introduced by Akbar was unique. The system was derived from Genghis Khan’s administration and applied in Indian circumstances with some modifications. By introducing the mansabdari system Akbar strengthened his control on the nobility and the army. Under the mansabdari system, every officer was assigned a rank (mansab). The salary of the Mansabdars were decided on the basis of their rank. In Mansabdari system ranks were divided into 'Jat' & 'Sawar' only.
source: UPSC CAPF G.S. 1st 2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.205

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Assertion (A) : During the time of Akbar, for every ten cavalrymen, the mansabdars had to maintain twenty horses. Reason (R) : Horses had to be rested while on march and replacements were necessary in times of war.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
explanation: Mansabdars had to maintain 20 horses on each 10 personnels. The basic thought behind it was to provide rest to the horses while on long march and replacements were necessary during the war.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.206

subject: AP & Indian History
question: ‘Ain-i-Dahsala’ a famous land revenue system during Akbar's regime was introduced by whom?
explanation: Raja Todar Mal had prominence in the field of land revenue and financial system. As a finance minister of Akbar, he brought new system of revenue collection known as ‘zabti’ and ‘dahsala’ system, which was a system of taxation. Under this system he took a careful survey of crop yields and prices cultivated for a period of 10 years. Under the Dahsala system as instituted by Akbar, the average produce of different crops as well as the average prices Prevailing over the last ten years was calculated.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.206

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following was a chain of continuance between Sher Shah and Akbar?
explanation: Raja Todarmal was a chain of continuance between Sher Shah and Akbar. Raja Todar Mal, a Khatri served in his youth under the administration of Sher Shah Suri and had gained priceless experience in management of Land and revenues. Later he carried out various reforms in land revenue system under Akbar. It is notable that Sher Shah Suri is known to have made a systematic surveys and measurements of the entire cultivable land of his empire using a unit called 'Sikandari Gaj'.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S.1st 2007 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.206

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Zabti system was the creation of—
explanation: Dahsala system or Zabti System was implemented by Raja Todarmal during Akbar reign. This remained a standard system of revenue assessment during the greater part of the Mughal Empire.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.206

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Mansabdari System introduced by Akbar was borrowed from the system of which country?
explanation: Mansabdari System introduced by Akbar was borrowed from Mongolia. This system was earlier introduced by Genghis Khan in Mongolia. Mansabdari system was the base of Mughal military organization during Akbar's reign and later.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.206

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which historian had recognized 'Din-i-Ilahi' as a religion?
explanation: Historian Abdul Qadir Badayuni called 'Din- e-Ilahi' as a religion. Akbar established 'Din-e-Ilahi' in 1582. Badayuni said that Akbar has gradually turned away from Islam, he called the masters of each religions such as Hindu, Christian, Parsi etc. and estasblished a religion which was named Din-e-Ilahi. Birbal was the only hindu to adopt this religion.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2000 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.207

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The concept of ‘Sulh-i-Kul’ (universal peace & brotherhood) adopted by Akbar was based on–
explanation: The concept of ‘Sulh-i-Kul’ (universal peace & brotherhood) adopted by Akbar was based on, Political liberty, Religious lenience and Liberal cultural view. The policy of Sulh-i-kul was considered as the cornerstone of enlightened rule. Akbar pursued this policy in order to establish peace and accommodate various ethnic and religious communities in the Empire. All religions and school of thought were given freedom of expression, but the emperor stood above all religions and ethnic groups. No community was to undermine the authority of the state and enough space and freedom were given to the existence of every culture so that they would not fight among themselves. This ensured that justice and peace Prevailed under the Mughals.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1998 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.207

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In which year had Akbar introduced 'Din-i- Ilahi'?
explanation: With a view to establish peace and harmony among all the religious communities in the Empire, Akbar introduced ‘Din-i-Ilahi’ as a religion of the state in 1582 AD.
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S. 2010-11 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.207

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri was:
options: The mosque for the use of Royal Family
The hall in which Akbar held discussions with scholars of various religions.
The room in which the nobles belonging to different religions gathered to discuss religious affairs
explanation: Ibādat Khāna was a meeting house built by Mughal Emperor Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575 AD to gather the spiritual leaders of different religious communities to conduct a discussion on the teachings of the respective religious leaders.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1st 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.207

question: Akbar's Ibadat Khana was the place where:
options: inter-faith debates and discussions were held
Akbar Preached his principles of Sulh-i-kul

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following rulers issued some coins with figures of Rama and Sita and Devanagari legend 'Rama-Siya'?
explanation: With a view to win the trust of his Hindu subjects Mughal Emperor Akbar had circulated the coins engraved with the figurine of Hindu God Lord Rama. A silver coin is engraved with the forms of Lord Ram, carrying his bow and arrows, and Sita; it read "Ram Siya". The inscription onth the other side read: "Amardad Ilahi 50", meaning the 50 year of the reign of Akbar.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.207

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which was the biggest Gold coin during Akbar's regime?
explanation: The Mughals attached a great importance to the coinage as Akbar started the practice of issuing coins and established royal mint with Abdus Samad the famous painter being the head of it. Muhar was the standard gold coin of about 170-175 grain and it was very popular. Jalali was a silver coin in square shape issued by Akbar. Shansab was largest Gold coin of about 101 Tola.
source: Uttarakhand RO/ARO 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.207

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The head of the military department under the reorganized central machinery of administration during Akbar’s reign was
explanation: Mir Bakshi: was the head of the military department holding the rank of imperial minister in the Mughal period. He was the general and the administrator of the army. Diwan: The Diwan was the finance minister responsible for collection of revenue and remittance of it to the imperial treasury. The office was sometimes combined with that of Wazir. Mir Saman:The officer in-charge of the royal Karkhanas, known as Mir Saman was responsible for all types of purchases and their storage for the royal households. His duty also included the supervision of the manufacturing of different articles to be used in the royal household. Bakshi : The Bakshi or the paymaster was the next provincial authority having duties of military establishment, salaries of Mansabdars and occasional duties like news writing for provinces.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1997 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.208

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The first person to be provided the full Grade of Diwan by Akbar was—
explanation: Muzaffar Khan Turbati was appointed the first Diwan by Akbar but he was dismissed later and Raja Todarmal was appointed the Diwan.
source: UP Lower (Pre) 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.208

subject: AP & Indian History
question: At the Dargah of which Sufi saint Akbar used to visit frequently?
explanation: Akbar used to visit the shrine of Sheikh Moinuddin Chishti frequently. Shrine of Moinuddin Chishti is located in Ajmer district of Rajasthan.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 2012 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.208

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following Jain Acharyas had been honoured by Akbar?
explanation: Jain Acharya Harivijay Suri was honored with the title of ‘Jagat Guru’ by Akbar. Harivijay Suri was one among the religious personalities to whom had Akbar called to discuss the religious issues at Ibadatkhana. Jinchandra Suri, another Jain saint was honored with the title of ‘Yug Pradhan’.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2012 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.208

subject: AP & Indian History
question: To which Sikh Guru had Akbar provided 500 Bigha of Land?
explanation: Akbar had provided 500 Bigha of land to fourth Sikh Guru Ramdas. The holy city of Amritsar, Golden temple and a pond was established there.
source: Uttarakhand UDA/LDA (m) 2007 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.208

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following Mughal ruler had provided the land for the construction of Golden temple at Amritsar?

subject: AP & Indian History
question: A Fatwa was issued from Jaunpur against which Mughal Emperor?
explanation: In 1580, an Ulema, Muhammad Yazdi from Jaunpur issued a ‘Fatwa’ against the Mughal emperor Akbar and asked all Muslims to rebel against him.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.208

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The famous painter during Akbar's period was—
explanation: There were a number of Painters in the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar. Some of them were Mir Sayyid Ali, Khwaja Abd-us-Samad, Farrukh Beg, Miskin, Mukund, Keshav Lal, Mahesh, Madhav, Jagannath, Tara, Basawan, Daswant etc. In the given question Daswanth was the famous painter during Akbar's reign. Daswanth was appointed as an official in the Mughal ‘Mint’. Daswanth belonged to Kahar community. He committed suicide later. Akbar had appointed Abd-us-Samad as Diwan of Multan. Abu al- Hasan was a Mughal painter of miniatures under the reign of Jahangir. Bishan Das was one of the most skilled painters in the court of emperor Jahangir who recognized his skills and sent him on a diplomatic mission to Persia to make portrait of the Shah and his chief courtiers. He remained in Persia from 1613 to 1620. Mansur was the leading painter of Nature at the court of the Mughal emperor Jahangir. The emperor took a passionate interest in the natural world and established a compendium of natural history with Mansur's help.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 1992 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.208

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In which year the battle of Haldighati was fought?
explanation: The battle of Haldighati was fought between Akbar and Maharana Pratap of Mewar in 1576 AD. Maharana Pratap was the only Rajput ruler who denied to accept the supremacy of Mughal Emperor Akbar. Akbar fought the battle of Haldighati to make Rana Pratap his subordinate.
source: BPSC Pre 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.209

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The main objective of Akbar behind the battle of Haldighati was—
options: to create conflict among the Rajputs
To satisfy the feelings of Mansingh
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 1992 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.209

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following was killed by Akbar himself?
explanation: Maham Anga's son Adham, who had grown up with Akbar, was a commander in his army, but was really swollen-headed and insolent. Once Adham Khan tried to hurt Akbar, this is why Akbar ordered the guards to throw him on the ground and kill him.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.209

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following rulers may be called as a conscious despotic?
explanation: A ruler who governs with an iron fist, caring little for the welfare of the people, may be called despotic . Mughal Emperor Akbar may be termed as conscious despotic because on one hand he was keen to expand the territory of his Empire for which he applied all means and fought various battles but on the other he tried his best for the welfare of his subjects without differentiation on the basis of their religious ground. He established communal harmony in the Empire.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.209

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following had ordered that a man should marry with only one women, he can go for another marriage only if his wife is sterile?
options: None of the above Medieval History
explanation: Polygamy was a social evil during medieval period and earlier in the society. Mughal Emperor Akbar had ordered that a man should marry with only one women, he can go for another marriage only if his wife is sterile. Akbar prohibited the marriage in close relations. He decided the age of marriage of boys and girls should not be below 16 years and 14 years respectively.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.209

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which Indian ruler was contemporary to the Queen Elizabeth of England?
explanation: Mughal Emperor Akbar (1556 AD-1605 AD)th was the contemporaryth to Queen Elizabeth I (7 September 1533 – 24 March 1603) of England.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.209

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following was the only woman Prime Minister during Mughal period?
explanation: Maham Anga was the only woman Prime Minister during Mughal period. Maham Anga led the group of caretakers during early four years of Akbar's regime.
source: MPPSC Pre 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.209

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Among the nine Jewels in Akbar’s court, which of the following did not belong to a family?
explanation: Faizi and Abul Fazl Allami were among the nine jewels of Akbar and belonged to same family. Abul Fazl's full name was Sheikh Abul Faizl Ibn Mubarak. Sufi Saint Sheikh Mubarak was the father of these two. Whereas, Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana (or Khanan) was the son of Bairam Khan. Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana also known as Rahim, was a devotee of Lord Krishna and composed a number of spiritual songs in Hindi. ‘Rahim ke Dohe’ are popular even today.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.209

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following province of South India was not the part of Mughal Empire during Akbar’s period?
explanation: Ahmad nagar, Berar and Khandesh were the part of Mughal Empire during Akbar's reign but Golconda was not the part of Akbar’s Empire. Golconda was merged in Mughal Empire during Aurangzeb's reign in 1687 AD.
source: UP UDA/LDA Spl. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.209

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following states of Rajputana had not accepted the subjection of Akbar?
explanation: Mewar was the only state of Rajputana which had not accepted the subjection of Akbar. Rajput policy of Akbar was based on the dual principle of suppression and cooperation for the stability and peace of the Empire. He suppressed Rajput rulers to accept his supremacy and forced some dynasties to establish marital relations like Amber, Marwar and Bikaner.
source: UP Lower (Pre) 2004 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.209

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following Mughal Emperor had initiated educational reforms?
explanation: Mughal Emperor Akbar showed much greater interest in education. He introduced certain changes in the existing curriculum of studies in educational institutions. Subjects like logic, arithmetics, astronomy, accountancy and agriculture etc. were included in studies. Akbar's thoughts regarding education are found in Ain-i-Akbari.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 1st 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.210

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following Muslim rulers had prohibited the Pilgrimage tax?
explanation: With a view to establish peace and harmony and get the confidence of all the communities, Mughal Emperor Akbar had abolished pilgrimage (1563), Jizya (1564), and all such taxes which were levied on his non- muslim subjects.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.210

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What was the root cause behind the conflict between Shah of Iran and Mughal rulers?
explanation: Kandahar was the root cause of conflict between Shah of Iran and Mughals. Kandahar was regarded as the gateway of India. Akbar and his successor Jahangir tried to establish their control on Kandahar. Jahangir had acquired Kandahar earlier but lost in 1621 at the hands of Abbas, the Shah of Iran.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.210

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following fact is not helpful to prove Akbar as a National Emperor?
explanation: Undoubtedly Akbar was the only ruler among the rulers of medieval India who attempted to foster the national feeling in India. He did succeed to some extent. However subsequent Mughal rulers failed to catch his spirit. The majority of historians regard Akbar as a great emperor. Administrative and cultural unity, common laws, and religious policy of Akbar played an important role to prove Akbar a national ruler.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 1994-95 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.210

subject: AP & Indian History
question: First British to reach the Akbar’s court was—
explanation: Ralph Fitch, Newberry, and William Leedes were the Englishmen to reach at first in the Akbar’s court at Fatehpur Sikri near Agra in 1584 AD.
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) G.S. 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.210

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Akbar had annexed Bengal and Bihar in Mughal Empire in—
explanation: Akbar attacked Bihar in 1574 A.D. and occupied it. He then left Munim Khan to complete the conquest of Bengal and Orissa and returned to the capital. Munim Khan captured Tanda and Daud fled away to Orissa. In 1575 A.D., Daud fought the Mughals for the first time at Tukaroi near the eastern bank of the river Subarnarekha. He was defeated. He accepted suzerainty of the Mughals and was assigned Orissa as his Jagir in return. But Munim Khan died very soon and Daud refused to accept these terms. He attacked Tanda and captured it. Akbar now sent Khan-i-Jahan as the governor of Bengal and Bihar who decisively defeated and killed Daud in a battle near Rajmahal in July 1576 A.D. Bengal was thus, finally annexed to the Mughal empire.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2007-08 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.210

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following families had established marital relation with Akbar at first?
explanation: Kachhwaha dynasty of Amer was the first Rajput family to establish matrimonial alliance with Akbar. The ruler of Amer king Bharmal (Biharimal) met Akbar during his visit to the shrine of Moinuddin Chishti at Ajmer. Bharmal proposed to marry his daughter Harkhabai with Akbar. Akbar accepted his proposal and thus Amer became the first Rajput state to establish marital relation with Mughals.
source: UPPCS Pre 2004, 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.210

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following system was the base of collection of land revenue in Deccan during Akbar’s reign?
explanation: Raja Todarmal introduced a new system of land revenue in 1580 under the reign of Akbar, known as Dahsala (Zabti) system. This system was implemented in Bihar, Allahabad, Lahore, Multan, Delhi, Awadh, Malwa and Gujarat earlier. The same was introduced in Deccan region later when Akbar conquered Ahmadnagar, Berar and Khandesh.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.210

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was responsible for the smooth functioning of the Mughal Mansabdari system?
explanation: The Mansabdari system was the administrative system intorduced by Akbar. Mir Bakhshi was responsible for the smooth functioning of Mansabdari system. 17.
source: JPSC (Pre) 2024 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.210

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to the Captain Hawking's, which of the following statements is correct? (1) He came to India in 1611 as an envoy of James–1. (2) He was very well versed in Turkish language. Code :
explanation: Captain Hawking's came to India in 1608 as an envoy of James-I and he was very well versed in Turkish language. Note: UPPSC has given option (a) as correct answer in the provisional answer key.
source: UPPCS (Pre) 2023 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.211

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following foreign travellers had mentioned the legend of 'Anarkali'?

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following Mughal emperors, after his recovery from illness, wore pearl earring as token of thanks of the Sufi Saint Khwaja Moin-ud-din Chisti?
explanation: Mughal Emperor Jahangir after his recovery from illness wore pearl earrings as a token of thanks of the Sufi Saint Khwaja Moin-ud-din Chisti.
source: OPSC Pre-2020 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.211

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following had rebelled against Jahangir? 1. Asaf Khan 2. Khurram 3. Mahabat Khan 4. Khusrau Codes:
explanation: Mughal Emperor Jahangir faced some internal rebels while ascending throne after Akbar. These were, rebel of his son Khusrau in 1606 AD, rebel of Khurram (Shah Jahan) in 1623 AD, rebel of Mahabat Khan 1626 AD.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.211

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Thomas Roe came to India as British ambassador during the reign of—
explanation: Sir Thomas Roe was an English diplomat who represented England in the court of Mughal Emperor Jahangir. On 18 September, 1615 he arrived at the Surat port as the ambassador of the English King, James I in Mughal emperor Jahangir's court. Thomas Roe's arrival in the Mughal court was a very important event as it was the first step to establish the paramountacy of the East India Company.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.211

question: At which place Jahangir gave the time to meet Thomas Roe?
explanation: Jahangir gave the time to meet Thomas Roe in Ajmer while he was on a visit to the shrine of Moinuddin Chishti in January 1615 AD. Hence Thomas Roe got 'Farman' for permission of trade.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2007 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.211

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Jahangir had protected which of the following art maximum?
explanation: Mughal Emperor Jahangir was a great patron of the painting, art and artisans. Jahangir had an artistic inclination and during his reign Mughal painting reached its zenith. Brush work became finer and the colors lighter. Most of the paintings created during the time of Jahangir depicts the durbar scenes, portraits, birds, animals and flower studies. Aqa Riza, Abul Hasan, Mansur, Bishan Das, Manohar, Goverdhan, Balchand, Daulat, Bhim and Inayat were the famous painters in the court of Jahangir. Mughal painting reached its zenith during Jahangir's regime. Jahangir was also deeply influenced by European paintings.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.212

explanation: East India Company had sent William Hawkins as its ambassador in the court of Mughal Emperor Jahangir. Jahangir had honored British ambassador William Hawkins with the title of ‘English Khan’ (Firangi Khan) and provided the Mansab of 400 to William Hawkins.

Mughal Emperor who banned the use of Tobacco was- (a) Akbar (b Babur (c) Jahangir (d) Aurangzeb UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2005 Ans. (c) : Tobacco use was a novelty in the first decade of the 17th century. But, its use became widespread by 1617, not only among the nobels but also among the common people. Jahangir had to issue a decree forbidding the use of tobacco to protect the health of the people and control the habit, but it was still rampant as per the travel accounts of Manucci.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Assertion (A) : During the reign of Shah Jahan, Dara Shikoh was sent on expedition to Balkh, Badakshan and Kandahar. Reason (R) :The expedition sent by Shah Jahan to the Middle-East was a marvellous success.

explanation: The Mughals taking advantage of the political turmoil and divisions in Central Asia decided to attack it. In 1653 Shah Jahan sent Dara Shikoh, with a large army and two of the heaviest artilleries of the empire, but after a five-month siege the Mughals couldn't manage to capture the city, and the attempt to breach their walls by canon fire also failed. explanation: The world famous Kohinoor diamond was Presented to Shah Jahan by his trader friend Mir Jumla. Mir Jumla brought highly valuable and rare gifts for the Mughal Emperor during his visit to Agra. He wanted Shah Jahan to wage a massive war against the kings of Golconda.

explanation: The Persian tradition of ‘Sijda and Paibos’ was introduced by Sultanate ruler Ghiyasuddin Balban. The tradition was continued up to Mughal period. Akbar prohibited it in his court but continued in private meetings. It was Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan who abolished the Sijda and Paibos practice in 1636-37 AD and started the practice of Chahar-Taslim at its place.

explanation: Dara Shikoh was the eldest son of Shah Jahan. He was expected to be the successor of Shah Jahan as Mughal Emperor. Shah Jahan honored Dara Shikoh as ‘Shah Buland Iqbal’. He translated the Upanishads from its original Sanskrit into Persian so that it could be read by Muslim scholars. This translation is often called "Sirr-e-Akbar" or 'The Greatest Mystery.'

Pandit Jagannath, the author of Rasgangadhar and Gangalahari and many other Hindu writers like Chintamani, Kavindracharya and Sunderdas also lived in Shah Jahan’s court. explanation: Shah Jahan’s period is called ‘ Golden Era of the Mughals’. He was fifth Emperor of Mughal dynasty. He ruled India from 1628 to 1658. He was the son of Emperor Jahangir and the grandson of Great Mughal Emperor Akbar. He was one of the greatest emperors of the Mughal period. He was founder, constructor or builder of many monuments such as Taj Mahal of Agra, Red fort and Jama Masjid of Delhi, Moti Masjid of Lahore, etc. These grand buildings tell about the prosperity of period of Emperor Shah Jahan and his history. Abdul Hasan was the brother of Noor Jahan (Mehr-un-Nissa), the wife of Jahangir. The real name of Mumtaj Mahal was ‘Arzumand Bano Beghum’. She was born in April, 1593 in Agra, Uttar Pradesh. Mumtaj Mahalth died in 1631 AD at the time of delivery of her 14 child. The world famous Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan in the memory of Mumtaj Mahal at the bank of river Yamuna in Agra. Taj Mahal is basically the tomb of Mumtaj Mahal and Shah Jahan was also creamated there. Roshanara was the daughter of Shah Jahan and Gulbadan Beghum was the daughter of First Mughal Emperor Babur.

Conquer Samarkand and Ferghana, the Mughal homelands
Fix the Mughal frontier on the ‘scientific line’, the Amu Darya
Expand the Mughal Empire beyond the sub-continent

question: Under which Emperor the number of Hindu commanders were maximum in Mughal army?
explanation: Aurangzeb has often been accused of closing the doors of official employment for the Hindus, but a study of the list of his officers shows this is not so. Actually there were more Hindu officers under him than under any other Mughal emperor. Though this was primarily due to a general increase in the number of officers, it shows that there was no ban on the employment for the Hindus during his period.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Saint Ramdas is being associated with whose reign?
explanation: Samarth Saint Ramdas was associated with the reign of Aurangzeb. Ramdas was spiritual guide and mentor of Shivaji who was contemporary to Aurangzeb. Ramdas had eleven hundred disciples, of whom three hundred were women. The women disciples were also expert Preachers and were virtuous. Ramdas sent his disciples to all parts of India to spread the Hindu religion. His disciples and Monasteries in the North directly or indirectly helped Shivaji and his efforts.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Aurangzeb is liable for the death of which Sikh Guru?
explanation: According to J.S. Grewal, a scholar of Sikh history, Guru Tegh Bahadur decided to confront the religious persecution of Kashmiri Brahmins by the Mughal officials. He did so after appointing his son the successor-Guru, leaving his base of Makhowal and entering Ropar where he was immediately arrested. The Mughal administration kept a close watch on his activities. Guru Tegh Bahadur was kept in jail for four months in Sirhind, then transferred to Delhi in November 1675. There he was asked to perform a miracle to prove his nearness to his God. The Guru questioned the idea that "occult powers were a proof of one's nearness to God", states Grewal. After his "refusement to perform a miracle", he was asked to Medieval History 22 convert to Islam, he refused. Three of his colleagues, who had been arrested with him, were then put to death in front of him. He continued his refusal to convert into Islam. Thereafter he was publicly beheaded in Chandni Chowk, a market square close to the Red Fort.
source: Chhattisgarh PSC (Pre) G.S. 2004-05 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.218

John Child was defeated by Aurangzeb in 1686 at Hooghly and evicted from India.

explanation: Muhi-ud-Din Muhammad Aurangzeb was the sixth emperor of the Mughal Empire. He ruled over most of the Indian subcontinent through Islamic Sharia. His reign lasted for 49 years from 1658 until his death in 1707. During this time, Aurangzeb greatly expanded the territory of the Mughal Empire. Victories in the south expanded the Empire to more than 4 million square kilometres. His empire was the world's largest economy, valued 27% of world's GDP. He was the last great and powerful ruler of the Mughal dynasty. After his death, the given map refers to the territory of Mughal Empire at the time of his death in 1707 AD. It consisted of 22 Provinces.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: To whom had Aurangzeb honored with the title of ‘Sahibat-uz-Zamani’?
explanation: Jahanara was the eldest daughter of Shah Jahan. She was Shah Jahan's favourite daughter and wielded major political influence during her father's reign, having been described as "the most powerful woman in the empire" at that time. During the war of succession which took place after Shah Jahan's illness in 1657, Jahanara sided with the heir-apparent Dara and ultimately joined her father in Agra Fort where he had been placed under house arrest by Aurangzeb. As a devoted daughter, she took care of Shah Jahan until his death in 1666. Later Jahanara reconciled with Aurangzeb who gave her the title Empress of Princesses and she replaced her younger sister, Princess Roshanara Begum, as First Lady. Jahanara died unmarried during Aurangzeb's reign. Aurangzeb honored her with the title of ‘Sahibat-uz-Zamani’.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.219

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During whose rule Jizya was re-introduced?
explanation: Jizya/Jaziya was reimposed by Aurangzeb in 1679. He appointed censors of public morals in all important cities to enforce Islamic law, and he tried to put down such practices as drinking, gambling, and prostitution. According to one of his order Hindus right to repair their temples was revoked and Subedars were ordered to destroy the temples and Paathshalas.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.219

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A) : Dara Shikoh could not be the emperor. Reason (R) : Dara Shikoh did not wished to be the emperor. Codes :

(A) is false but (R) is true Medieval History
explanation: Akbar was one of the greatest emperors in the history of India. However, during the reign of his great- grandson, Aurangzeb, the rebellious Jats under the leadership of Rajaram Jat, ransacked the Akbar's tomb, plundered and looted all the beautiful gold, jewels, silver and carpets, while destroying other things in the year 1688.
source: UPPSC ACF (Pre) 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.219

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Meaning of Jehad called by Aurangzeb was—
explanation: The meaning of Jehad manifested by Aurangzeb was Dar-ul-Islam, which according to Aurangzeb meant to wage holy war against non-Islamic nations (Dar-ul-Harb) till the time they are not converted to Islamic nations.
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S. 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.219

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider : Assertion-(A) Aurangzeb became the successor of Shah Jahan on Mughal throne. Reason- (R) The law of Right to accession of eldest son was followed. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below:
options: A and R both are true and R is correct explanation to A
A and R both are true but R is not correct explanation to A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Aurangzeb ascended the throne of Mughal Empire after the war of succession among various sons of Shah Jahan. Aurangzeb defeated Darashikoh, the eldest son of Shah Jahan and sat on the throne. He held his father Shah Jahan captive for 8 years. Thus the law of Right to accession of eldest son was not followed. Later Mughals Ans. (c) : As soon as Shah Jahan became ill on 6th September 1657 AD the gruesome war of succession began between his sons. Royal Army fought with the combined armies of Aurangzeb and Murad in a decisive battle near Shamugarh on 26th May, 1658 AD, in which the Royal army was defeated. The decisive battle between Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh was fought in Deorai in March 1659. In this battle Dara was finally defeated, captured and later executed and hence, he could not become the emperor, even though he fought to be one.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.219

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The last Subedar of 'Bengal, who was appointed by Mughal Emperor:
explanation: Mughal Emperor Farrukshiyar appointed Murshid Quli Khan as the Subedar of Bengal in 1717. He was Subedar of Bengal for a decade. After his death post of Subedar became hereditary. He shifted capital of Bengal to Murshidabad in 1719 AD. After his death Shuja-ud-din become Nawab of Bengal followed by Aliwardi Khan in 1739 and Siraj-ud-daula in 1756.
source: UPPSC RO-ARO (Pre) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.219

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Mark the correct statement : 1. "Mughal rule began and ended at Panipat". 2. Marathas were defeated in the Third Battle of Panipat. 3. French rule began with Panipat. 4. French power ended with Panipat.
explanation: Third Battle of Panipat was fought between the Marathas and Ahmadth Shah Abdali (The ruler of Afghanistan) on 14 January, 1761. In this battle Marathas were defeated.
source: Kerala (KAS) PSC-2020 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.220

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The term 'Dastak' implies:
explanation: The term 'Dastak' implies duty free trade which means an act of being able to purchase an item in particular circumstances without paying import, sales, value added or other taxes. In 18th century 'Dastak' was used as a pass for duty free trade, a trade permit sanctioned to East India Company by Mughal Emperor 'Farrukh Siyar Farman' for a custom free trade in the Bengal. Later Dastak was abolished by Nawab Mir Qasim.
source: NAGALAND NCS PRELIMS, 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.220

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Mirza Ghalib, a famous Urdu and Persian poet was a contemporary of_____.
explanation: Mirza Ghalib was a prominent Urdu and Persian Poet. He served during the last years of the Mughal Empire. He was contemporary of Bahadur Shah Zafar.
source: TPPSC Group-II Pre-11.11.2016 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.220

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Choose the correct chronological order of the following Muslim rulers from the codes given below: 1. Ahmad Shah Abdali 2. Muhammad Shah 3. Jahangir 4. Bahadur Shah
explanation: The correct chronological order is: Jahangir (1605-1627) Muhammad Shah (1719-1748) Ahamad Shah Abdali (1747-1769)-During this period Ahmad Shah Abdali invaded India for nine times and looted the wealth. Bahadur Shah (1837-1857) Medieval History
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2001 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.220

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During the reign of which Mughal empire, Nadir Shah attacked?
explanation: Nadir Shah, the ruler of Persia attacked the Mughal empire in 1739. Muhammad Shah was the Mughal emperor at that time. His army was easily defeated at the Battle of Karnal. Nadir Shah took away the famous Kohinoor diamond from the Peacock throne of Shah Jahan & plundered huge wealth.
source: UPPCS (Mains)spl. G.S. 2004 UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1993 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.220

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following was the last Governor of Bengal appointed by Mughal Emperor?
explanation: Murshid Quli Khan was the last governor of Bengal appointed by Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb. Murshid Quli Khan and his successor Nawabs administered Bengal, Bihar and Orissa as an independent rulers though they continued to send revenue to the Mughal emperor regularly. Governor Murshid Quli Khan (1717-1727 A.D.) transferred the capital from Dacca to Murshidabad. Shuzauddin became the next nawab in 1732 and ruled until Alivardi Khan took over in 1739. It was Alivardi Khan who broke the ties with Mughal Empire.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S.1st 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.220

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Bahadur Shah was the last Mughal Emperor. What was the name of his father?
explanation: Akbar II, also known as Akbar Shah II, was the penultimate Mughal emperor of India. He reigned from 1806 to 1837 AD. He was the second son of Shah Alam II and the father of Bahadur Shah II. Akbar Shah II had little de facto power due to the increasing British influence in India through the East India Company.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2005 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.220

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the last Mughal Emperor of India?
explanation: Abu Zafar Sirajuddin Muhammad Bahadur Shah Zafar, also known as Bahadur Shah or Bahadur Shah II (October 1775 -- 7 November 1862) was the last Mughal Emperor in India. He became the rallying point for the failed "Indian uprising" of 1857, when soldiers from undivided India rose against the British East India Company. He lead the revolt of 1857.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S.2000 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.220

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following Mughal Emperor was known as ‘Shah-i-Bekhabar’?
explanation: Bahadur Shah the seventh Mughal emperor of India, ruled from 1707 until his death in 1712. Mu’azzam (Bahadur Shah) was the third son of Aurangzeb. In his youth, he conspired to overthrow his father and ascend to the throne a number of times. Shah’s plans were intercepted by the emperor, who imprisoned him several times during 1696 to 1707. He took the title of Bahadur Shah and is also sometimes referred to as Shah Alam I. Khafi Khan has called him as Shah-i-Bekhabar, since he liked to appease all parties by profuse grants of titles and rewards and handled royal administrative affairs carelessly, was called Shah-i-Bekhabar.
source: UPPSC Asst. Forest conservator exam 2015 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.220

subject: AP & Indian History

source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2012 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.221

subject: AP & Indian History
question: How did the rule of Mughal Emperor Jahandar Shah ended before the time?
options: He slipped down the stairs and died
He was defeated by his nephew in a battle
He was dead due to illness caused by over drinking
explanation: Jahandar Shah was a Mughal Emperor who ruled for a brief period between 1712 and 1713. Shailendra Sen describes him as "a worthless debauch who became emperor after liquidating his three brothers". Jahandar Shah led a frivolous life, and his court was often enlivened by dance and entertainment. He chose a prostitute, Lal Kunwar, who was a mere dancing girl before her elevation to the position of Queen Consort. Together they choked the Mughal Empire and were even opposed by Aurangzeb's surviving daughter, Zeenat-un-Nissa. He was defeated in the battle at Agra on 10th January 1713 by Farrukhsiyar, his nephew and the second son of Azim-ush-Shan, with the support of the Sayyid Brothers.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.221

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During whose period there was supremacy of hijras and women?
explanation: Aḥmad Shah, was Mughal emperor from 1748 to 1754. He was characterized as good-natured but incompetent and without personality, training, or qualities of leadership. He was entirely dominated by others, including the queen, Udham Bai, and the eunuch superintendent Javid Khan.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2004 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.221

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following was the first Nawab of Awadh?
explanation: The founder of the Awadh was a Persian nobleman named Saadat Khan, who came to India in 1705 A.D. and soon won the favour of the Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah. He was appointed the Governor of Awadh in 1722 A.D. The Sheikhs of Lucknow were subdued by the new governor. He had to struggle hard to carve his state. He fought many battles to subdue the unruly elements. After him his nephew Safdar Jang and after him Shuja-ud-Daula became Nawab of Awadh.
source: UPPCS (Mains) spl. G.S. 1st 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.221

subject: AP & Indian History
question: On order of which Mughal Emperor Banda Singh was tortured to death?
explanation: It was Mughal Emperor Farrukhsiyar who ordered to torture Banda Bahadur until his death. The Battle of Gurdas Nangal was fought in March 1715, the army under the command of Abdus Samad Khan, the Mughal governor of Lahore, drove Banda Bahadur and the Sikh forces into the village of Gurdas Nangal, Gurdaspur, Punjab and laid siege to the village. The Sikhs defended the small fort for eight months under conditions of great hardship, but on 7 December 1715 the Mughals broke into the starving garrison and captured Banda Singh and his companions. Banda Singh Bahadur was put into an iron cage and the remaining sikhs were chained. The sikhs were brought to Delhi in a procession with the 780 sikh prisoners, 2,000 sikh heads hung on spears, and 700 cartloads of heads of slaughtered Sikhs used to terrorise the population. They were put in the Delhi fort and pressurized to give up their faith and become Muslims.
source: UPPCS Pre 2000 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.221

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following Nawab of Awadh was appointed as first Wazir of Mughal Emperor?
explanation: Safdar Jang succeeded his father-in-law and maternal uncle, Burhan-ul-Mulk Saadat Ali Khan I as Nawab of Awadh in 1739 AD and ruled from 19 March 1739 to 5 October 1754. The Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah gave him the title of "Safdar Jang". Safdar Jang was an able administrator. He was not only effective in keeping the control of Oudh, but also managed to render valuable assistance to the weakened Emperor Muhammad Shah. During the later years of Muhammad Shah, he gained complete control of administration over the whole Mughal Empire. When Ahmad Shah ascended the throne at Delhi in 1748, Safdar Jung became his Wazir-ul-Mumalik-i- Hindustan or Prime Minister of Hindustan.
source: RAS Opt. 2000 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.221

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which Mughal Emperor was known as Rangila?
explanation: Muhammad Shah also known as 'Rangila' was the Mughal Emperor who ascended to the throne in 1719 which he occupied till his death in 1748. His name was Roshan Akhtar and he was the grandson of Bahadur Shah I. He was born in 1702 at Fatehpur Sikri and was just 17 years old when the crown was placed on his head. His reign was that of decadence of the Mughal Empire as well as the degeneration of the Muslim society in India. The reign of Muhammad Shah 'Rangila' was the period in which the process of degeneration of the empire got inception in the right earnest. This period witnessed the rise of many independent and semi independent states like Bengal, Oudh, and South India and breaking away of Kabul. Similarly, splinter groups got strength and motivation from the growing weakness of the tottering Mughal Empire.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 1st 2015 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.222

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following Mughal Emperor had issued an important farman (order) to help the British in their trading?
explanation: Farrukhsiyar was the Mughal Emperor from 1713 AD to 1719 AD. In 1717, Farrukhsiyar issued a farman giving the British East India Company the right to reside and trade in the Mughal Empire. They were allowed to trade freely, except for a yearly payment of 3,000 rupees. This was because William Hamilton, a surgeon associated with the company cured Farrukhsiyar of a disease. The company was given the right to issue dastak (passes) for the movement of goods, which was misused by company officials for personal gains.
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S. 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.222

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the last Mughal Emperor to sit on ‘Peacock Throne’?
explanation: In February 1739, the Persian forces with Nadir Shah as their leader captured Delhi. However they left the city in May 1739, taking with them, the precious Peacock Throne as the trophy of victory. Hence, Muhammad Shah is said to be the last Mughal Emperor who sat on the Peacock throne. Medieval History
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S.1995 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.222

After the treaty of Sangola Peshwa became the most powerful and the real ruler. Shahu’s successors had no real power. Various Maratha Sardars emerged during this period. They were under the Peshwa.

explanation: British concluded Treaty of Surat in March, 1775 with Raghunath Rao. By this Treaty, Raghunath Rao, one of the claimants to the throne of the Peshwa, agreed to cede Salesette and Bassein fort to the English in consideration of being himself restored to Poona. The military operations that followed are known as the first Anglo-Maratha War. question: Mark the incorrect statement: 1. Ashtapradhan is associated with Shivaji. 2. Shivaji was the organizer of Maratha Rajya. 3. Sulh-i-kul was the organizer of Maratha Rajya. 4. Treaty of Purandar took place with Shivaji.
explanation: Sulh-i kul is an Arabic term literally meaning “peace with all,” “universal peace,” or “absolute peace,” drawn from a Sufi mystic principle. As applied by the third Mughal Emperor of India, Akbar (who reigned 1556-1605), it described a peaceful and harmonious relationship among different religions.

explanation: Shivaji conquered Chakan, Purandar in 1556. Shivaji's confrontations with the Mughals began in March 1657, when two of Shivaji's officers raided the Mughal territory near Ahmednagar. explanation: The silver coin Prevalent in the Kingdom of Chhatrapati Shivaji were – Lari, Taka (Asharfi Taka), Ruka. Other coin currencies Prevalent in the Maratha empire were Fanam, Chakram, Padshahi Hoon, Nishani Hoon, Tiraca, Paisa, Dam etc. Silver in the form of currency as ‘Rupya’ was not Prevalent or in circulation in Maratha Empire. Medieval History

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The Maratha claim of revenue for protection is known by what name?
explanation: Other than land revenue, Shivaji's main source of income was 'Chauth'. It was collected from neighbouring states. It was 1/4th (25%) of the total revenue of the concerned state. This tax assured the protection of the state from attack and invasion by Marathas. Whereas Sardeshmukhi was additional tax, which was 10% of the land tax, levied by Shivaji. As Shivaji was Sardeshmukh of Maharashtra, he considered it to be his legal right.

subject: AP & Indian History

explanation: According to Encyclopedia.com, Shivaji was born on April 10, 1627 (February 19, 1630, according to some sources), in Shivneri Fort, Poona (Pune), India. His father was Shahji Bhonsle and mother was Jija Bai. His spiritual mentor was Samarth Ramadas. He was the real founder of the Maratha kingdom in India. His coronation took place in 1674 at Raigarh, which was the capital of Shivaji Empire. Shivaji was crowned as Chhatrapati by Pt. Ganga Bhatt of Banaras. Shivaji had enthroned himself with great fanfare as an independent sovereign. The surpressed Hindu majority rallied to him as their leader. He ruled his domain for six years. He died in 1680.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following streamlined the Maratha administration after Sambhaji?
explanation: Balaji Vishwanath Bhat (1713-1720), better known as Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath, was the 1st Peshwa and the first of a series of hereditary Peshwas hailing from the Bhat family who gained effective control of the Maratha Empire during the 18th century. Balaji Vishwanath assisted a young Maratha Emperor Shahu to consolidate his grip on a kingdom that had been racked by civil war and persistently intruded on by the Mughals under Aurangzeb.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Maratha woman who led the Marathas Struggle against Mughal Empire after 1700 AD onward, was?
explanation: Tarabai Bhosale was the regent of the Maratha Empire of India from 1700 until 1708. She was the queen of Chhatrapati Rajaram Bhosale, daughter-in- law of the empire's founder Shivaji and mother of Shivaji II. She is acclaimed for her role in keeping alive the resistance against Mughal occupation of Maratha territories after the death of her spouse, and acted as regent during the minority of her son. She was leading the Maratha Empire at the the time of Aurangzeb's death.
source: UPPCS (Pre) Spl. G.S. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.227

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What was the immediate reason for Ahmad Shah Abdali to invade India and fight the Third Battle of Panipat?
options: He wanted to avenge the expulsion by Marathas of his viceroy Timur Shah from Lahore
The frustrated governor of Punjab Adina Beg Khan invited him to invade Punjab .
He wanted to punish Mughal administration for non-payment of the revenues of the Chahar Mahal (Gujarat, Aurangabad, Sialkot and Pasrur).
He wanted to annex all the fertile plains of Punjab up to the borders of Delhi to his kingdom
explanation: The Immediate reason for the Ahmad Shah Abdali to invade India and fight the third battle of Panipat was to avenge the expulsion by Marathas of his viceroy Timur Shah from Lahore. Other major reasons for the third Battle of Panipat were Ahmad Shah Abdali wanted to plunder the wealth of India. Maratha inspired by the feelings of Hindu Pad Padshahi wanted to conquer Delhi.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following was not a reason behind emergence of Marathas?
explanation: Mughal Invasion in Deccan and ensuing socio-economic backwardness was the primary reason for discontent in the region which created conditions ripe for a rebellion. Building of a number of forts on the mountains provided them stronger defense which Marathas used to their advantage against Mughal attacks. The seeds which were sown through the call for social unity during Bhakti movement by Tukaram, Ramdas, Vaman Pandit and Eknath helped in unification of the Maratha Empire. The revivalist political ideology of Hind-swarajya was a major driving force for Marathas and able leadership paved the way for the rise of Marathas.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1992 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.228

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who had stated that, “We should attack on the trunk of the old tree, branches will fall itself, thus the Maratha flag should be hoisted from Krishna to Sindhu?
explanation: Baji Rao I was a great Maratha Peshwa who succeeded his father Balaji Vishwanath as Peshwa in 1720 and formulated a bold plan for the expansion of Maratha Empire. In the twilight of the Mughal Empire he suggested, - "let us strike at the trunk of the withering tree, the branches will fall of themselves. Thus Maratha flag will be hoisted from the Krishna to the Indus."
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) G.S. 2008 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.228

subject: AP & Indian History
question: That General who was sent by Sultan of Bijapur to suppress Shivaji in 1659?
explanation: Sultan of Bijapur sent Afzal Khan against Shivaji Maharaj with a large army in 1659 with a instruction to bring Shivaji to the court of Bijapur Sultan whether dead or alive. This was the battle of Pratapgarh near Satara in Maharashtra where both of them met. There Afzal Khan tried to deceive Shivaji by huging him but Shivaji was alert and he killed Afzal Khan.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.228

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The ‘Modi script’ was employed in the documents of the
explanation: Modi script was used by Marathas. The script was used to write the Marathi language spoken in the Indian state of Maharashtra. It originated as a cursive variant of the script during the 17th century CE. Modi was used until the 1950's when Devanagari replaced it as the script of the Marathi language. Medieval History
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1995 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.228

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the map given below: The shaded area in the map shows the kingdom of the
explanation: The given map is associated with the Maratha Empire. After the death of Aurangzeb in 1707, Shahu, grandson of Shivaji, was released by the Mughals. Following a brief struggle with his aunt Tarabai, Shahu became the ruler and appointed Balaji Vishwanath and later, his descendants, as the Peshwas or prime ministers of the empire. Balaji and his descendants played a key role in the expansion of Maratha rule. The empire at its peak stretched from Tamil Nadu in the south, to Peshawar (modern-day Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan) in the north and Bengal Suba in the east.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.228

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The Maratha King became a non-entity and the Peshwa the virtual ruler from the time of:
explanation: Shahu appointed Balaji Bajirao as Peshwa after the death of Bajirao in 1740. Now the designation of Peshwa became patrimonial. By the Sangola agreement of 1750, the Maratha king became a king only for namesake and the Mayor of Palace, and the Peshwa emerged as the real and effective head of Maratha Confederacy and de facto ruler.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2007 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.228

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Shivaji defeated the Mughals in the battle of
explanation: The Battle of Salher was a battle fought between the Maratha Empire and the Mughal Empire in 1672 CE. The battle was fought near the fort of Salher in the Nashik district. The result was a decisive victory for the Maratha Empire.This was for the first time when Marathas decisively defeated Mughal army in the battlefield. Battle of Ambur Khird took place on Feb 1661 in the mountain range of Sahyadri. The battle was fought between Maratha army under Chhatrapati Shivaji and General Kartalab Khan of Mughal forces. Maratha defeated the Mughal forces.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2005 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.228

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The year in which Shivaji had defeated Shaista Khan?
explanation: After Aurangzeb's accession to the throne and the dramatic death of Afzal Khan by Shivaji's hand, Aurangzeb sent Shaista Khan as viceroy of the Deccan with a large army to defeat Shivaji. In January 1660 Shaista Khan arrived at Aurangabad and quickly advanced, sieging Pune, The Maratha were banned from entering the city of Pune and Mughal distance from the locals turned out to be an error. On the evening of 5 April 1663, a wedding had obtained special permission for holding a procession.Shivaji and his nearly 400 men disguised as the bridegroom's procession members entered Pune. Others entered in small parties dressed as labourers and soldiers of Maratha generals serving under Shaista Khan. After midnight, they raided the Nawab's compound and then entered the palace in an attempt to assassinate Shaista Khan.
source: BPSC (Pre) GS 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.229

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following was known as Deshmukh, Patil and Nayak?
explanation: Heads of the villages during Maratha Empire were known as Deshmukh, Patil or Nayaka. They were responsible for maintaining law and Order and collection of revenue. They were granted the land in lieu of the services rendered by them.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What was the name of the mentor of Shivaji?
explanation: Samarth Ramdas, also known as Sant Ramdas or Ramdas Swami or simply Ramdas was an Indian Hindu saint, philosopher, poet, writer and spiritual master. He was initially named as Narayan. He was a devotee of the Hindu deity Rama. He was the mentor of Shivaji Maharaj.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In which city Shivaji was arrested and afterwards escaped from the captivity?
explanation: Shivaji was held as captive in Agra by Aurangzeb. Shivaji arrived in Agra with his eldest son, Sambhaji, and a small contingent of soldiers on May 12, Aurangzeb’s 50th birthday. Shivaji held a ceremony honouring Pandit Kavindra Paramananda who had come to meet him. He also gave away his elephants and horses after announcing that he had decided to become a fakir. He then dressed up as a fakir. His close associate and trustee, Niraji Raoji, dressed himself as Shivaji and emerged from his house, mingled with the other pandits and then escaped from Agra.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 2003-04 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.229

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who had established Gwalior state?
explanation: Mahad Ji Scindia was the founder of Scindia (Maratha) dynasty in Gwalior. Mahadji became the regent of Mughal affairs and also got the title Amir-ul-Umara in 1784. He was also responsible for limiting the Nizams to south of Deccan. He signed a peace treaty with Tipu Sultan of Mysore in 1792 after which he used his influence to protect Tipu Sultan from the Nizams and the British.
source: MPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2003-04 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.229

explanation: Surat was a premier Port of the Mughals which was attacked and looted by Shivaji in 1664. Battle of Surat, also known as the sack of Surat, was a land battle that took place on January 5, 1664 between Maratha ruler Shivaji and Inayat Khan, a Mughal captain. The Marathas defeated the Mughal force, and sacked the city of Surat for six days.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following monument of Delhi is example of Indian and Persian style of architecture?
explanation: Built-in 1564 A.D. in India, Humayun's tomb is the perfect example of Persian architecture and its beauty. After the death of Humayun, his wife Hamida Begum built this tomb in memory of her husband. This tomb is also of historical and cultural importance as it was the first garden- tomb built in the Indian subcontinent and use of Charbagh system in tomb architecture. Another importance of Humayu's tomb is that it has maximum number of burials than any other tomb.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S.2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.233

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Where is the tomb of Akbar situated?
explanation: The tomb of Mughal Emperor Akbar is located in Sikandra near Agra City. The mortal remains of the Mughal Emperor Akbar was burried there, Akbar in his lifetime himself had completed the tomb and laid out a beautiful garden. However, the topmost portion of mausoleum in marble was constructed by his son, Jahangir.The shape of tomb is pyramidical and consists of five storeys. The entire tomb is constructed of red sandstone but top storey is constructed in white marble. This tomb doesn't have dome for which it is criticised by historians.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1992 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.233

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In which Mughal tomb of North India, use of minaret is found at first?
explanation: The use of minaret in north India is found at first in the tomb of Mughal Emperor Akbar located in Sikandra. Medieval History

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which monument is not situated in Fatehpur Sikri?
explanation: Swarn Mahal, Panch Mahal and Jodhabai palace are situated in Fatehpur Sikri while Akbari Mahal is located in Agra fort which was used for residential purpose. It was Akbar’s Haram used by his wives.
source: Uttarakhand PCS(Pre) 1st 2014-15 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.233

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The great monuments constructed by Akbar are located at-
explanation: Akbar established Fatehpur Sikri in respect of Saint Salim Chishti after the birth of Salim. Fatehpur Sikri (the City of Victory) was the capital of the Mughal Empire for only 10 years. The Jama Masjid (one of the largest mosques), Panch Mahal, Jodhabai Mahal, Buland Darawaza, etc are the major monuments at Fatehpur Sikri.
source: RAS/RTS G.S.1994-95 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.233

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following built the tomb of her Emperor husband?
explanation: Hamida Banu Begum or Haji Begum was the wife of the second Mughal emperor Humayun and the mother of his successor, the third Mughal emperor Akbar. She is also known by the title Maryam Makani, which was given to her by her son, Akbar. She got the tomb of her husband Emperor Humayun built in Delhi. It was designed by Mirza Ghiyas and his son Sayyid Mohammad.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2004 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.233

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following Mughal Emperor had constructed the Jama Masjid of Delhi?
explanation: ‘Masjid e Jahan Numa’, commonly known as the Jama Masjid of Delhi, is one of the largest mosques in India. It was built by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan between 1650 and 1656 at a cost of one million rupees, and was inaugurated by Imam Syed Abdul Ghafoor Shah Bukhari from Bukhara, Present- day Uzbekistan.

explanation: The tomb of Rabia-ud-Daurani, wife of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb, is regarded as the second Taj Mahal (Bibi ka Maqbara) or Daccani Taj. The tomb was built by Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb in Aurangabad district of Maharashtra, copying the architecture of Taj Mahal.

explanation: &d) : The tombs of two Mughal Emperors are not in India. The tomb of Jahangir is located in Shahdara Lahore, Pakistan and the tomb of Babur is located in Kabul Afghanistan.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Where was the first observatory Jantar- Mantar established by Sawai Raja Jaisingh?
explanation: Jai Singh II (3rd November 1688–21st September 1743) was the Hindu Rajput ruler of the kingdom of Amber, he later founded the fortified city of Jaipur and made it his capital. He was born at Amber, the capital of the Kachwahas. He moved his kingdom's capital from Amber to the newly-established city of Jaipur in 1727, and performed two Ashvamedha sacrifices, once in 1734, and again in 1741. Five observatories were built at Delhi, Mathura, Benaras, Ujjain, and his own capital of Jaipur. The first observatory was built in Jaipur. His astronomical observations were remarkably accurate. He drew up a set of tables, entitled Zij Muhammadshahi, to enable people to make astronomical observations. He had Euclid's "Elements of Geometry" translated into Sanskrit as also several works on trigonometry, and Napier's works.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1991 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.234

question: Famous saint Salim Chishti was dwelling at-

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Jahangiri Palace is situated at—
explanation: Jahangiri Palace is located inside the Agra Fort. It was built by Akbar. It is a square shaped structure. Mostly red sandstone is used in this monument. The Jahangiri palace is the copy of Mansingh's palace of Gwalior.
source: MPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1990 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.234

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The shape of which monument constructed by Akbar is like a Buddhist Vihar?
explanation: Built on the pattern of a Buddhist Temple, Panch Mahal was basically a pleasure palace of emperor Akbar. He primarily used it for relaxation and entertainment purpose. The structure has been so designed that each storey is pillared and is smaller than the other as you move upwards. While no less than 84 columns support the ground floor, the uppermost domed floor has only 4 columns. The whole structure is very airy and was styled to give respite from the scorching summers of Agra.
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) G.S. 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.235

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following monument is said to be ‘Pride of Fatehpur?
explanation: Jama Masjid located in Fatehpur Sikri is regarded as the 'Pride of Fatehpur Sikri'. The Mosque was built by Mughal Emperor Akbar.

explanation: Pyramid shaped Panch Mahal was constructed by Akbar, in Fatehpur Skri. The Panch Mahal is a five storeyed building which is known for its exceptional structure. The architecture of Panch Mahal was inspired by that of the Buddhist temple. Panch Mahal was used by Akbar for the purpose of relaxation and entertainment. B. Painting

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With respect ot Mughal paintings, consider the following statements. A. Daswant and Basawan were two famous painters of Jahangir's court. B. Mughal paintings reached a climax under Jahangir C. Aurangzeb's lack of interest in paintings led to a dispersal of artists to different palces. Choose the correct answer :
explanation: Dawant and Basawan were two famous court artist during Akbar's court. Mughal paintings reached at climax under Jahangir's reign, the renowned painter of his time included Bishan Das, Madhu, Anant, Manohar, Govardhan and Ustad Mansur. Aurangzeb did not patronise any arts due to lack of interest in paintings led to a dispersal of artists to different places. Hence, option (b) is correct. Medieval History

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements regarding Mughal period paintings; 1. Daswant and Baswan were two of the famous painters of Akbar’s court. 2. During Shah Jahan’s reign, Mughal paintings reached their zenith. The correct statement/s is/are :
explanation: Hindu Painters Basawan and Daswant were the Chief painters is the court of Akbar. Hence 1st statement is correct Humayun introduced painting is Mughal period however it was the reign of Jahangir when Mughal painting reached its zenith. Hence, 2nd statement is incorrect.
source: J & K PSC Pre 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.235

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following medieval town was famous for the printed cotton cloth known as ‘Chinth’?
explanation: The term 'Chinth' referred to printed Indian cotton textiles, which was imported by Europeans from India. In 1720, the British govvernment eracted a legislation banning the used of printed cotton textiles- Chints- in England. This Act was known as the calico Act.
source: MPPSC Pre 2022 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.235

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following Mughal Emperors shifted emphasis from illustrated manuscripts to album and individual portrait?
explanation: Mughal Emperor Jahangir shifted emphasis from illustrated manuscripts to albums and individual portraits. During Jahangir's reign, art and painting were developed very well. He himself was a great admirer of Art and Painting. The main themes of paintings during this period revolved around the events from Jahangir's own life, along with portraits, birds, flowers, animals, court scenes etc. Paintings made during Jahangir's reign continued the trend of naturalism and were influenced by resurgence of Persian styles.
source: IAS (Pre)-2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.236

explanation: Painting during Jahangir's reign reached its zenith. A painting gallery was established in Agra under the supervision of Aqa Riza. Farukh Beg, Bishandas, Ustad Mansur, Daulat, Manohar and Abul Hasan were among the famous painters during Jahangir's regime. Jahangir had honored Abul Hasan with the title of ‘Nadir-uz-Zaman’.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: By whom ‘Dastan-e-Amir-Hamza was portrayed?
explanation: Mir Sayyid Ali was a famous Persian painter in the court of Humayun. He got excellence in miniature paintings. He came to India with Mughal Emperor Humayun, when Humayun returned to India in 1555 AD. After the death of Humayun he survived in the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar. Akbar ordered to prepare the miniature painting of ‘Hamzanama’, a history of Amir Hamza, the uncle of the prophet Muhammad. Mir Sayyid Ali alongwith Abdus Samad completed this world famous painting.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2003-04 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.236

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The Mughal School of Painting formed the spinal column of the various schools of Indian miniature art. Which one of the following painting styles was not affected by Mughal painting?
explanation: Kalighat school of painting was distinctively developed painting style with no effect of Mughal school of paintings on it. Kalighat painting is a school of modern art that originated in 19th century in Calcutta, India, which was then the capital of British India. Made on mostly cloth or paper scrolls, Kalighat paintings are so named due to the thriving settlement of the Patuas or cloth-painters around the temples of Kali at Kalighat in Kolkata. The theme of these paintings were mostly mythological characters that later evolved to civil life in Calcutta along with other secular and contemporary themes. The brushwork on these paintings are deemed by experts as deft, seamless, flowing and one of the smoothest art forms in India.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1995 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.236

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which Mughal ruler out of the following learnt Hindu Music from Lala Kalawant?
explanation: Akbar was fond of Music. He was a learned musician. He studied Hindu vocalization under Lala Kalawant, who taught him every sound breathing and technique that is concerned with the Hindi language.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In Mughal paintings one notices the adoption of principle of reshortening whereby near and distant people and things could be placed in perspective. This was due to the influence of:

subject: AP & Indian History
question: During whose reign Mughal paintings developed?
explanation: Mughal painting was developed not during the reign of any one ruler. It was initiated by Mughal Emperor Humayun with the help of two Persian painters Abdus Samad and Mir Sayyid Ali. It was furthered by Akbar during his period. Mughal paintings reached its climax during Jahangir's period. In his autobiography he states that he can identify painting made by any artist either dead or alive.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which statement is true in reference to Mughal paintings?
explanation: Mughal paintings immediately took a much greater interest in realistic portraiture than that of typical Persian miniatures. Animals and plants were the main subject of many miniatures for albums, and were more realistically depicted. Subjects are rich in variety and include portraits, events and scenes from court life, wild life and hunting scenes, and illustrations of battles. Thus all types of paintings were prepared in Mughal School of paintings. Different painters were expert in dfferent type of arts.

question: Abul Hasan was one of the most eminent painter of Jahangir's reign. He painted the well known Mughal Darbar scene describing:

explanation: Abul Hasan was an excellent painter of miniature painting. He Prepared various scenes based on Jahangir’s court. Most of the scenes were associated to Jahangirs interaction with the public. Abu al-Hasan's main task was the documentation of events at the imperial court, which resulted in many superb portraits. Jahangir rewarded Abul Hasan with title of 'Nadir-ul- Jama'.

question: Many Muslim scholars translated different parts of Mahabharat in Persian. What is this compilation called?
explanation: Many Muslim scholars translated various parts of Mahabharata into Persian and this compilation is called Razmnama. Naqib Khan, Badayuni, Sheikh Sultan translated Mahabharata into Persian. In 1539 AD, Badauni translated Ramayana. Haji Ibrahim Sarhindi translated the Atharvaveda, Faiji translated the mathematical treatise Lilavati and Muhammad Khan Gujrathi translated an essay on astrology into Persian language.
source: UPPSC ACF Mains Paper I 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.238

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In which book Mughal and Chand dynastic relation has been described?
explanation: The relation between Mughal and Chand dynasty has been described in 'Jahangirnama,' the official biography of Jahangir. The Chand kingdom was established by Som Chand. One of the most powerful ruler of Chand dynasty was Baz Bahadur (1638-78) AD, who met Shah Jahan in Delhi and in 1655 joined forces with him to attack Garhwal, which was under its king, Pirthi Sah and subsequently captured the Terai region including Dehradun, which was hence separated from the Garhwal kingdom.

question: Title of Persian translation of Mahabharat is :
explanation: The Razmnama (Book of War) is a Persian translation of the Mahabharata. In Persian, “Razm” means “war” and "nama" means “tale” or “epic”; the name Razmnama, therefore, means a tale of war. Rajatarangini, Ramayana and Mahabharata into the Persian language. question: Which of the following Mughal sources was translated into Persian by Painda Khan?
explanation: Baburnama Tuzuk-i-Babari is the memories of Mughal Empire Babur; it was an autobiography, written by Babur. It is written in the Chagatai Turki language, the spoken language of the Andijan-Timurids. During the reign of Emperor Akbar, the work was translated into Persian, the usual literary language of the Mughal Court, by a Mughal Courtier, Abdul Rahim Khan-i- Khanan, in 1589-90 CE. It was also translated into English first by John Leydon and William Erskine and later by Quentalist scholar Annette Beveridge. Humayun Nama was written by Gulbadan Begum daughter of Babar. question: Which of the following statements are correct? 1. Kalhana composed Rajatarangini in Sanskrit. 2. Ibn Battuta was appointed as the Qazi of Delhi 3. Tansen is remembered for his epic Dhrupad composition, creating several new ragas as well as for writing two classical books on music i.e. Shree Ganesh Stotra and Sangita Sara.

explanation: The real name of Tansen was Ramtanu Pandey. He was born in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. The title of 'Tansen' was not given to him by Akbar. Regarding this there are two opinions among Historians some say that the title of 'Tansen' was given to him by Raja Vikramjeet Singh Tomar of Gwalior where as other say that it was given to him by Raja Ramchandra Singh. Rest all statements are correct.

subject: AP & Indian History

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Upanishads were translated into Persian during the reign of:
explanation: Upanishads were translated into Persian during the reign of Shah Jahan. During the reign of Shah Jahan, his son Dara Shikoh, well versed in Indian religion and philosophy, translated the Upanishads into Persian which was named as Sirr-i-Akbar (Great mystery), Dara Shikoh devoted much effort towards finding a common mystical language between Islam and Hinduism. Towards this goal he completed the translation of fifty Upanishads from their original Sanskrit into Persian so that they could be studied by Muslim scholars. His most famous work, Majma-ul- Bahraina ("The Confluence of the Two Seas"), was also devoted to a revelation of the mystical and pluralistic affinities between Sufic and Vedantic speculation. Medieval History
