subject: AP & Indian History
question: Akbarnama was completed by Abul Fazal in—
explanation: Akbarnama was written by Abul Fazl in seven years. Akbarnama is written in three part. The first volume of Akbarnama deals with the birth of Akbar, the history of Timur's family and the reigns of Babur and Humayun and the Suri Sultans of Delhi. The second volume describes the detailed history of the reign of Akbar till 1602, and records the events during Akbar's reign. It also deals with that how Bairam Khan and Akbar won the Battle of Panipat against Hemu, an Indian warrior. The third volume is named Ain-i-Akbari and it deals with the Akbar's administration as well as containing the famous "Account of the Hindu Sciences". It also deals with Akbar's household, army, the revenues and the geography of the empire. It also produces rich details about the traditions and culture of the people living in India.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.241

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which one of the following is NOT the charactristics of 'Iqta System'?

Siyasatnama was the source of informatics for Iqta System.
Revenue from Iqta was directly deposited in Sultan's account
Muqti was supported to maintain troops out of the revenue collected from Iqta
explanation: Iqta system was introduced in India by Iltutmish. Iqta is an arabic word which means 'Land'. Iqta sytem has been elaborated by Nizam-ul-Mulk in his book 'Siyasatnama'. Muqtis or Iqtedars were the officials authorised to collect taxes. Muqti had no other right over the subjects in matter of collection of taxes. The money collected was used to pay landowner's army, which could be called by Sultan any time; making up for a relatively quick mobilisation and highly professional soldiers. A part of revenue was also paid directly to the sultan.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements: 1. In the revenue administration of Delhi Sultanate, administration of revenue collection was know as 'Amil'. 2. The lqta system of Sultanate of Delhi was an ancient indigenous institution. 3. The office of 'Mir Bakshi' came into existence during the reign of Khalji Sultans of Delhi. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: In the revenue administration of Delhi sultanate, officer responsible for revenue collection was known as 'Amil'. The Iqta system was a main feature of Delhi Sultanate. The main aim of this system was to end feudalism prevalent in Indian society and to integrate the farthest started in Iltutmish's reign. The office of 'Mir Bakshi' came into existence during the Mughal Period. Under the Iqta system, the land of the empire was divided into several large and small tracts called Iqta and assigned these Iqtas to the soldiers, offices and nobles. It was introduced by Delhi sultans, was originally of central Asian and west Asian origin and was not an ancient indigenous institution.
source: IAS (Pre)-2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.247

explanation: The correct chronological order of these dynasties is: 1. Slave/Mamluk Dynasty - (1206-1290 AD) 2. Khilji Dynasty - (1290-1320 AD) 3. Sayyid Dynasty - (1414-1451 AD)
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2012 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.248

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Arrange the following in their chronological order— 1. Ruknuddin 2. Mubarak Shah 3. Firuz Shah Tughlaq 4. Alam Shah Choose the correct answer from the codes given below:
explanation: The correct chronological order is: 1. Ruknuddin Firuz- was the son of Mamluk ruler Iltutmish. He ascended the throne after the death of his father in April 1236 AD. He ruled the Sultanate for only seven months up to Nov. 1236 AD. 2. Mubarak Shah- was the son of Alauddin Khilji who ascended the throne after the death of Alauddin in 1316 AD. Mubarak Shah ruled the Sultanate for the period of 1316-1320 AD. 3. Firuz Shah Tughlaq- was the cousin of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. He ruled the Delhi Sultanate for the period of 1351-1388 AD.
source: UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 2003 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.249

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who were called ‘Dastar Bandan’?
explanation: In the Sultanate period, individuals (ulema) holding high religious and judicial positions were collectively called ‘Dastar Bandan’ (turban wearers) as they wore turban.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.249

subject: AP & Indian History
question: At which of the following place in India had Portuguese constructed their first fort?
explanation: Vasco da Gama, discovered the sea route to India in 1498. Portugueseth reached India at southwestern coast in late 15 century. The Portuguese navigator Pedro Álvares Cabral founded the first European settlement in India at Kochi in 1500. The Portuguese Viceroy Alfonso de Albuquerque built the first European fort in India there in 1503 AD. Medieval History
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. Ist 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.249

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The first European country to establish trade relations with India was-
explanation: With the arrival of Vasco-da-Gama at Calicut in 1498 AD, Portuguese became the first European to establish trade relations with India. They established Goa as their Capital in 1530 AD.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 1993 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.249

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which is the correct chronological order of the visit of following travelers? 1. Ibn Battuta 2. Tavernier 3. Al-Biruni 4. Manucci
explanation: The correct chronological order is as follows: 1. Al-Biruni, came to India in 1017 AD at the time of Mahmud Ghazni’s invasion of India. He wrote a book named ‘Qitab-ul-Hind’. 2. Ibn Battuta– The native of Morocco visited India in 1333 AD during Muhammad-Bin-Tughlaq's reign. His travelogue is known as ‘Rihla’. 3. Tavernier, was a French traveler came to India during Shah Jahan's reign (AD 1627-1658). He was a jeweller by profession. He witnessed the battle of succession among the sons of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.
source: UP Lower (Pre) spl. 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.249

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following events: 1. Reign of Vijaya Nagara ruler Krishna Deva Raya 2. Construction of Qutub Minar 3. Arrival of Portuguese 4. Death of Feroz Tughlaq Correct chronological order of these events is:
explanation: The correct order is : 1. Construction of Qutub Minar - 1199 AD 2. Death of Feroz Tughlaq - 1388 AD 3. Arrival of Portuguese - 1498 AD
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2000 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.249

explanation: The correct match is as follows : LIST I LIST II Feroz Tughlaq Construction of canals Balban Nauroz Alauddin Diwan-i-Riyasat Jahangir Sir Thomas Roe

question: Which of the following pairs of Sultan and the departments created by them is false?

source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 2016 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.250

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Two statements are in this question, One is assertion A and another is reason R. Examine these statements and choose the correct answer from the codes given below: Assertion : (A) Earlier Turkish administration was military based. Reason : (R) State territory was divided into Iqtas among the high level commanders.
options: A and R both are true and R is correct explanation of A
A and R both are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Turkish administration was based on military in early period. Iqtas were provided to higher military commanders during Delhi Sultanate. Both the statements are true and R is correct explanation of A.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1995 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.251

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Two statements are given below. One is statement A and another is reason R. Read them carefully- Assertion: (A)th Nalanda Mahavihar declined at the end of 12 century AD. Reason: (R) State support to Mahavihar was stopped. Which of the following is /are true in reference to above statements?
options: A and R both are true and R is correct explanation to A
A and R both are true but R is not correct explanation to A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Nalanda Mahavihara declined in the 12th century AD because it could not get state support after the formation of Muslim rule in India. It was fully destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khilji in 1200 AD.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1996 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.251

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following musical instrument was termed as the best inclusion of Hindu-Muslim musical instruments?
explanation: Sitar is an instrument introduced by Amir Khusrau with the inclusion of Sarangi and lute. He also created musical instruments like Sitar and Tabla and also composed new ragas like Yaman and Zeelaf. He was also the creator of musical forms such as Qawwali, the khayal and the Tarana.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. Re-exam 1999-2000 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.251

subject: AP & Indian History
question: When did Vasco-da-Gama reach India?
explanation: Vasco-da-Gama reached at Calicut (India) on the sea coast of Malabar in 1498, where he was welcomed by the king ‘Zamorin’ of Calicut. It is notable that Arab traders were against the entry of Portuguese traders.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 1995 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.251

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Coins of Sultanate period Tanka, Shashgani and Jital were made of which metal?
explanation: Tanka, Shashgani and Jital were the coins during Sultanate period made of Silver and copper. Tanka and Shashgani were the silver coins whereas Jital was made of copper.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1994 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.251

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following statement is true in reference to medieval Indian rulers?
options: Alauddin Khilji started a new Dept. ‘Diwan-e Ariz’.
Balban introduced the system of branding his horse.
After Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq his uncle was coronated on the throne of Delhi.
Feroz Tughlaq had established a new dept. for Slaves.
explanation: Diwan-e-Ariz was established by Sultan Balban. The system of branding the horses for identification was introduced by Alauddin Khilji. The successor of Muhammad Bin Tughlaq was his cousin Feroz Tughlaq, not his uncle.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.251

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Historian Barani had not accepted the Indian rule under sultans as an Islamic State because-
options: Most of the population was not following the Islam.
Along with Muslim laws Sultans had introduced their own laws.
Religious freedom was provided to non-Muslims.
explanation: Historian Ziauddin Barani did not recognize Indian rule under Delhi Sultans as Islamic, because most of their subjects were non Muslims and they did not follow Shariat strictly.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.252

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Apbhransha words were used in Medieval Sanskrit epics-
options: To denote the community from Rajputs who ousted from their caste.
To denote the prohibition of Vedic rituals.
To denote the early forms of some modern Indian Language.
To denote the words different from Sanskrit.
explanation: Apbhransha words were used in Medieval Sanskrit epics to denote the early forms of some of the modern Indian languages.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1996 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.252

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following crop is not mentioned in Ain-i-Akbari?
explanation: &c): There is a list of various Rabi and Kharif crops given in Ain-i-Akbari but there is no mention of Tomato and potato in the list. UP public service commission has accepted the Option ‘b’ as its answer.
source: UPPSC ACF (Pre) 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.252

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The game of polo introduced in India by-
explanation: Polo is a horseback mounted team sport. It is one of the world's oldest known team sport. Polo was first played in Persia (Iran) at dates given from the 6th century BC to the 1st century AD. The game of ‘Polo’ in India was introduced by Turks.
source: UPPCS (PRE) G.S. 2001 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.252

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Prophet Hazrat Muhammad was born in-
explanation: Prophet Hazrat Muhammad was an Arab religious, social, and political leader and the founder of Islam. He was born in 570 AD in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. He died in 632 AD in Medina, Saudi Arabia.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1996 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.252

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The maximum Number of Amirs and Sultans during Sultanate period belonged to which community?
explanation: The most of Amirs and Sultans during Sultanate period belonged to the Turkish community.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1991 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.252

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which one of the following term was used for land measurement during Sultanate period?
explanation: The term ‘Masahat’ was introduced by Alauddin Khilji. Masahat was a system of measurement of land for the assessment of land revenue.
source: Up UDA/LDA sol. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.252

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What was the chief of military staff called during Sultanate period?
explanation: The chief of military staff during Sultanate period was called 'Ariz-e-Mumalik'. The official during the sultanate period was responsible for the administration of the army, including recruiting, payment of salaries, supplies, and transportation of army.
source: UP UDA/LDA (spl. 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.252

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which among the following was not associated with Slave dynasty?
explanation: Ibrahim Lodi was not associated with Slave dynasty. Ibrahim Lodi was the Afghan ruler of Lodi dynasty, founded by Bahlul Lodi.
source: Uttarakhand Lower (Pre) 2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.252

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The apex official of land revenue at village level during Sultanate period was—
explanation: Apex revenue official at village level during Sultanate period was Chaudhary.
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S. 2003-04 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.252

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following does not denote the tax levied on land produce?
explanation: Kharaz was the tax levied on the lands owned by the Hindus and it varied from one-tenth to one-half. Ushraf was the land tax charged on the lands held by the Muslims. It was usually one-tenth of the total produce. Khums was a type of tax levied from muslim community from any assets earned by any means, which is excess than their use.th It may have been obtained in the battles. It was 1/5 of the total wealth obtained. Muqtai was also a land revenue which was accepted by the peasants. Thus it is clear that Khums was not a land revenue.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1995 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.252

subject: AP & Indian History
question: To which Bandagan-i-khas denotes during the regime of Delhi Sultans?
explanation: Bandagan-i-Khas during Sultanate period denotes the Slaves engaged in Royal duty.
source: UPSC CAPF G..S. 1st 2012 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.253

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Ayn-al-Mulk did not serve during the period of which of the following ruler?
explanation: Ayn-al-Mulk Multani was a military commander and official who served the Khalji and Tughlaq dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate. He served as Alauddin Khalji's governor of Malwa and Devagiri. He served during the period of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq and later in the regime of Muhammad Bin Tughlaq, he was the Governor of Awadh.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 1st 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.253

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The name of queen Padmini is co-related with the victory of Alauddin over Chittore. What was the name of her husband?
explanation: Queen Padmavati or Padmini was the wife of Rana Ratan Singh, the King of Chittor. Malik Muhammad Jayasi has elaborated the story of Queen Padmini and Rana Ratan Singh in his book Padmavat.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1999 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.253

subject: AP & Indian History
question: When was the use of paper begun in India?
explanation: Paper was invented by Cai Lun of China. It was invented during rule of Han kingdom in 202 CE. In India its use began from 12th century and the first paper mill was setup in Kashmir by Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin.
source: BPSC (Pre) G.S. 2017-18 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.253

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Identify the two main currencies of Sultanate period from the following codes- 1. Dam 2. Jital 3. Rupiya 4. Tanka Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
explanation: Sultan Iltutmish was the first Sultanate ruler to introduce pure Arabic coins. He introduced the famous silver 'Tanka' and Copper 'Jital' coins. He also introduced the trend of inscribing name of mint town on coin.
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2001 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.253

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What was the term used for the religious officer in Mughal Administration?
explanation: The Muhtasib under Mughal Administrator was the regulator of public business who controlled trade and enforced Islamic injunctions. This term was also used for the religious officer. Mir Saman was incharge of imperial household (Karkhanas). Mir-i- Atish under Mughal Administration was the head of ordinance department.
source: OPSC (OCS) Pre 2021 Paper-I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.253

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements: 1. It was during the reign of Iltutmish that Chengiz Khan reached the Indus in pursuit of the fugitive Khwarizm prince. 2. It was during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq that Taimur occupied Multan and crossed the Indus. 3. It was during the reign of Deva Raya II of Vijayanagara Empire that Vasco da Gama reached the coast of Kerala. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Statement – 1 (Correct) – Khwarizm ruler Jalaluddin who was being pursued by Chengiz Khan fled to Delhi. Sultan Iltutmish, who was ruling Delhi at that time, refused the request of Jalaluddin for asylum. Statement – 2 (Not correct) – Muhammad Tughluq died in 1351 and Timur had started his career of conquest in 1370. He crossed Indus during the reign of Firoz Shah Tughluq. Statement – 3 (not correct) – Deva Raya – II died in 1446 and Vasco Da Gama arrived in 1498 at Calicut. Hence, Option (a) is the correct answer.
source: UPSC (IAS) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.253

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the code given below the lists- List-I List-II (Emperor) (Diwan) A Akbar 1 Ghiyas Beg Itmad- ud-Daulah B Jahangir 2 Asad Khan C Shah Jahan 3 Muzaffar Khan D Aurangzeb 4 Sadullah Khan Code : A B C D A B C D
explanation: The correct match is as follows :- (Emperor) (Diwan) Akbar Muzaffar Khan Jahangir Ghiyas-Beg-Itmadud Daulah Shah Jahan Sadullah Khan Aurangzeb Asad Khan
source: UPPSC RO-ARO Mains 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.253

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In the times of Mughals the region of Jharkhand was known as................
explanation: The region of Jharkhand was known as ‘Kukra’ during the time of Mughals, Akbar first paid attention to this region. The main reasons for the focus on this area were political, strategic and to some extent economic. During the reign of Akbar, there were three major rulers – the Nag dynasty of Khukhra, the Chero dynasty of Palamu and the Singhbhum’s Singh dynasty. These three dynasties accpted suzerainty of Akbar.
source: 7th JPSC (Pre) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.253

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Government of medieval period was a composite structure. It was a fusion of :
explanation: The structure of the government of the medieval period was a mixture of Persian, Arab, Turko- Mongol and Indian elements. The medieval period government or system of government was formed as a result of the combination of Muslim rulers from the Persia and the Arab countries, then the Mughals (Turk- Mongols) and then Indian system of governance.
source: 7 JPSC (Pre) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.254

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following was declared as his successor by Guru Nanak?
explanation: Guru Nanak appointed Lehna as his successor in 1539, renaming him as Guru Angad. Guru Nanak Dev was the founder of Shikhism and he was also the first Guru of Shikhism.
source: UPPSC RO-ARO (Pre) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.254

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and other as Reason (R): Assertion (A) : The Mughal Empire was an original Military state. Reason (R): The vitality of the development of the Central Government system depended on its military power. Select the correct answer using the codes given below: Codes:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: A military state is a state that structures its economic model on the sustainment of its armed forces usually in times of prolonged or severe conflict. In such states vitality of the development of the central government system depends on its military power. Characteristically military state will subject a citizen to high taxation. Hence A and R both are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
source: UPPCS (pre.) 2021 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.254

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In what context does 'Panahi' and 'Upanah' mention in the medieval Indian History?
explanation: The ‘Panahi’ and ‘Upanah’ in medieval India are another name for shoes/sandals etc. Medieval History
source: MPPCS (Pre.) 2020 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.254

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Zawabit were_______.
explanation: Zawabit means- secular rules and regulations of the state. It is the word of Persian language. This term is specially used in Mughal peirod. Aurangzeb issued secular decrees called Zawabits. The collection of these decrees are in “Zawabit-e-Alamgiri”.
source: UP PSC ACF/RFO (Mains) 2020 Paper I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.254

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to 'Mustafi Mumalik' of Mughal Period, which of the following statement/s is/are correct? 1. In charge of Revenue Department. 2. Auditor General of State Select the correct answer using the codes given below Codes :
explanation: Mustafi-e-Mumalik worked just like modern CAG. He was the Auditor General during the Mughal period. Diwan was the in-charge of Revenue Department.
source: UP PSC ACF/RFO (Mains) 2020 Paper I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.254

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following : I. Tughlaqabad Fort. II. Lodi Garden. III. Qutub Minar. IV. Fatehpur Sikri. The correct chronological order in which they were built is:
explanation: The construction of Qutub Minar was started by Qutub-ud-din Aibak in 1199 AD. It was completed later by Iltutmish. Tughlaqabad fort was constructed by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq in 1321. Lodi gardenth was developed by Sayyid and Lodi rulers in 15 century. Bara Gumbad and Mosque was constructed here in 1494 AD. The Tombs of last Sayyid ruler Muhammad Shah and Sikandar Lodi is located here. Fatehpur Sikri was built by Mughal ruler Akbar in 1569. It was the Mughal capital from 1571 to 1585 AD during the reign of Akbar.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 1998 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.254

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists : List-I List-II (Monuments) (Builders) A. Alai Darwaza, Delhi 1. Alauddin Khalji B. Buland Darwaza, 2. Akbar Fatehpur Sikri C. Moti Masjid, Agra 3. Shah Jahan D. Moti Masjid, Delhi 4. Aurangzeb Code : A B C D A B C D
explanation: All the pairs are correctly matched. Alai Darwaza, Delhi - Alauddin Khalji Buland Darwaza, Fatehpur Sikri - Akbar Moti Masjid, Agra - Shah Jahan Moti Masjid, Delhi - Aurangzeb
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2010 UPPCS (Mains) G.S. 1st 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.254

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The meaning of 'Deh' in Mughal period was
explanation: In Mughal Period, Deh was used for the village/ Mauja. In the period of Shah Jahan, there is a unit, named ‘Chakla’ between Sarkar and Pargana.
source: UP PSC ACF/RFO (Mains) 2020 Paper I · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.255

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the court poet of Raja Jai Singh Raja of Amer?
explanation: Biharilal was the court poet of Raja Jai Singh of Amer. He was born in Gwalior in 1595 AD. He was a famous Hindi poet of his times. Though Bihari Satsai is the only known work of Bihari.
source: ACF/RFO (Mains) I 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.255

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which the following is NOT correctly matched?
explanation: For a long time in Mughal empire, before Akbar, Gaj-e-Siknadari was used for the measurement of land. In 1575AD, for the expansion of 'Khalisa' land a new land measurement system was implemented, this was 'Jarib'. Raja Todar Mal, one of Akbar's Nauratnas, used the Jarib, which was of 31 digits or 32 inches Finally in 1586 AD, use of Ilahi-Gaz (41 digits or 33 inches) was started.
source: UPPCS (Pre), 2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.255

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Earliest capital of Baghela Dynasty was located at
explanation: Baghela dynasty was related to the Rewa Royal family of Madhya Pradesh. Earliest capital of this dynasty was Bandhavgarh. Maharaja Vikramaditya of Baghela dynasty transferred his capital from Bandhavgarh to Rewa in 1617 AD. Medieval History
source: ACF/RFO (Mains) Ist 2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.255

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer from the codes given below the lists : List-I List-II A. Treaty of Allahabad 1. 1782 B. Treaty of Mangalore 2. 1784 C. Treaty of Salbai 3. 1769 D. Treaty of Madras 4. 1765 Codes : A B C D A B C D
explanation: The correct match is as follows :- List-I List - II Treaty of Allahabad 1765 Treaty of Mangalore 1784 Treaty of Salbai 1782 Treaty of Madras
source: UPPCS (Pre), 2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.255

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Arrange the following battles in chronological order and select the correct answer from the codes given below : I. Battle of Sarnal II. Battle of Bilgram III. Battle of Dharmat IV. Battle of Jajau Codes :
explanation: The correct chronological order of battles are as follows - Battle Year Battle of Bilgram 1540 Battle of Sarnal 1572 Battle of Dharmat 1658 Battle of Jajau 1707 Hence the correct chronology is II, I, III, IV.
source: UPPCS (Pre), 2019 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.255

subject: AP & Indian History
question: With reference to Mughal India, what is/are the difference/differences between Jagirdar and Zamindar? 1. Jagirdars were holders of land assignments in lieu of judicial and police duties, whereas Zamindars were holders of revenue rights without obligation to perform any duty other than revenue collection. 2. Land assignments to Jagirdars were hereditary and revenue rights of Zamindars were not hereditary. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation: In Mughal period, Jagirdars were the mansabdars to whom land was granted in lieu of cash payment. Jagirs were transferable and the right over them was limited up to their service period. While Zamindars were those landlords who enjoyed hereditary right of the collection of revenue and got some part of revenue for their services. All the administrative rights were vested in the hands of Fauzdars. Thus statements 1 & 2 both are false.
source: IAS (Pre)-2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.255

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The class of traders who specialized in carrying bulk goods over long distances during Mughal period were called ____.
explanation: The Banjaras were the most important trader- nomads. Their caravan was called tanda. Sultan Alauddin Khalji used the Banjaras to transport grain to the city markets. Emperor Jahangir wrote in his memoirs that the Banjaras carried grain on their bullocks from different areas and sold it in towns. They transported food grain for the Mughal army during military campaigns. With a large army there could be 100,000 bullocks carrying grain.

Agriculture of Mughal was large enough to give its peasants a decent earnings.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements: Ahadis were those troopers who- 1. Offered their services singly 2. Did not attach themselves to any chief 3. Had the emperor as their immediate colonel 4. Attached themselves to Mirzas Of these statements :
explanation: Ahadi troopers were basically the royal troopers. Salary and remuneration of these troopers were paid from state treasury and were directly under separate Amir or Bakhshi. Sometimes they were kept under Mansabdars. Ahadis were considered very efficient loyal troops and were paid high salaries. Ahadis- were individual troopers, they were also called gentlemen-troopers and received much higher salaries then other troopers. They were recruited directly by the emperors. They performed miscellaneous tasks also.
source: (IAS (Pre) G.S. 1998) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.257

question: Arrange the followings in chronological order and choose the correct answer from the codes given below: 1. Ahilya Bai 2. Durgawati 3. Padmini 4. Tara Bai Codes :
explanation: Queen Padmini was the wife of Rana Ratan Singh of Mewar who committed 'Jauhar' at the time of Allauddin’s attack in January 1303. •••• Queen Durgawati was the mother and care taker of the minor ruler of Gondwana Vir Narayan. She died while fighting Mughal Governor of Malwa in 1564. •••• Tara Bai Bhonsle was the mother of Shivaji II of Maratha. She faced Mughals to save the Maratha kingdom from 1700 to 1708. •••• Ahilya Bai was the ruler of Holkar dynasty of Maratha. She built hundreds of temples, more than 30 Dharmshalas numerous ghats and wells all for the welfare of people..
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 2003 UP Lower (Pre) 2002 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.257

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements about Mansabdari system of Mughals: 1. Jat and Sawar posts were provided 2. Mansabdars were heriditary officials 3. Here was three class of mansabdars 4. Salary was provided to them from office of Diwan Choose the correct answer from the codes given below:
explanation: Mansabdari system was introduced in Mughal Empire during Akbar reign. The post of Mansabdar was provided on the basis of ‘Jat’ and ‘Sawar’. The term 'Jat' stands for the salary and the designation of a person while the term 'Sawar' referred to the number of cavalrymen that a Mansabdar had. The post of Mansabdar was not hereditary. Mansabdars were paid salary in cash or as land grants. They were under Mir Bakhshi's office. Three classes of mansabdar were Mansabdar, Amir and Amir-i-umda.
source: UP UDA/LDA (Pre) 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.258

question: Match the following events and years— A. Control on Delhi by Nadirshah 1. 1556 B. First Battle between Babur and 2. 1526 Ibrahim Lodi C. Battle between Hemu and 3. 1761 Akbar D. Battle between Ahmad Shah 4. 1739 Abdali and Marathas Codes: A B C D A B C D
explanation: On 21st April, 1526 the First Battle of Panipat was fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi. Babur used Tuluguma warfare technique as a result of which Ibrahim Lodi was defeated. The Second Battle of Panipat was fought between Afghan force underth Hemu and Mughal force under Bairam Khan on 5 November 1556. Hemu wasth defeated. In March 1739 invader Nadir Shah, invaded Delhi during the reign of Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah. He plundered and murdered people mercilessly. While returning he took away Kohinoor Diamond and Peacock throne (Takht-e-Taus).

question: Districts during Mughal period were known as–

question: Copper coin during Mughal period was called-

source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1995 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.262

subject: AP & Indian History
question: 'Maullim' during Mughal period was-
explanation: Maullim during Mughal period was an instrument installed on the Ship to find the location of the ship and to know the position of the Sun and stars so that sailors could decide the directon of their movement.
source: UPPCS (Main) Ist Paper GS, 2014 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.262

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following was the founder of independent state of Hyderabad?
explanation: Independent state of Hyderabad was founded by Nizam al-Mulk (Āṣaf Jāh) or Chin Qilich Khan, who was intermittently a viceroy of the Deccan (peninsular India) under the Mughal emperors from 1713 to 1721. He retained the post again with the title Āṣaf Jāh in 1724. The title of Ashaf Jah was provided by Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah. This time he became virtually independent and founded the Nizam dynasty of Hyderabad.
source: UPPCS (Main) G.S. Ist Paper 2011 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.263

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What is khidmati?
options: 1/5th part of wealth obtained in loot
Tax levied on sale and purchase of goods
Tax payable by defeated Indian Nobles
A house tax charged on Hindus
explanation: Khidmati was a kind of offering given by the defeated Hindu kings to the Muslim rulers.
source: (UP UDA/LDA Spl. 2006) · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.263

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Mughal rulers of medieval India were basically-
explanation: Mughal rulers of Medieval India belonged to ‘Chagatai Turk’ dynasty. They were the fifthth generation of Timur from paternal side and 7 generation of Genghis Khan from maternal side.
source: UP UDA/LDA (Pre) 2010 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.263

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Where was the capital of the king of Punjab Maharaja Ranjit Singh?
explanation: Founder of the Sikh Empire of Punjab Maharaja Ranjit singh was born in 1780 AD at Gujranwala town, now in Pakistan. He belonged to Sukerchakia Misl (confederacy). The name of his father was Maha Singh. He seized Lahore in 1799 AD. Afghan king Jaman Shah appointed him as the governor of Lahore. In 1801 Ranjit Singh declared himself the Maharaja of Punjab. He captured the city of Amritsar in 1802. He established his capital in Lahore. Medieval History
source: Uttarakhand PCS (Pre) 2006-07 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.263

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following city in India is called ‘Pink city’?
explanation: City of Jaipur was established by Sawai Raja Mirza Jai Singh. The city was established in a planned way with all the buildings in ‘Pink’ colour. This is why the city is known as Pink city.
source: Uttarakhand UDA/LDA (Pre) 2006 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.263

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Muhatsib in Mughal administration was:
explanation: Muhatsib in Mughal administration was custodian of public affairs and moral character of people in the kingdom. He was responsible to ensure whether Shariyat law was being followed by the people or not. He was also responsible to have a check on the use of intoxicating drinks.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2004-05 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.263

subject: AP & Indian History
question: ‘Madad-e-Mash’ in Mughal administration indicate -
options: Revenue free land granted to Scholars
explanation: Sources of revenue in the Mughal period were mainly land revenue, octroi, gifts, salt tax, pal or person tax. 'Land revenue' was the most important of these. In the Mughal period, 'Madad-e-Mash' was given as land grant to a person of religious instinct. Most of such land was unproductive. This land was also called 'milq'. Among the Mughal rulers, it was Akbar who first tried to organize the land and the land revenue system. Akbar started a new system called 'Dahsala' in 1580.
source: BPSC (Pre) 2003-04 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.263

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Identify the region from where Europeans used to get most of Saltpetre and opium?
explanation: Bihar and Bengal were the most Opium and Saltpetre producing regions during the period. Europeans were getting these products from Bihar in bulk. Salt-petre was required in the manufacture of gunpowder.
source: BPSC (Pre) 1995 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.263

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which Rajput ruler continuously struggled for freedom against Mughals and did not surrender?
explanation: Some Rajput rulers did not accept the supremacy of Akbar and continued their struggle for the freedom till last. Chandrasen Rathore of Marwar and King Udai Singh of Mewar were such Rulers.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre.) G.S. 2012 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.263

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The greatness of Guru Gobind Singh lies in, that-
options: He formed the military system of the Sikhs.
He was the founder of Sikh Kingdom
explanation: Guru Gobind Singh is credited for various reforms in Sikhism. He established the Khalsa Panth to make Sikh a warrior community. He introduced 5ks (Kangha, Kesh, Kripan, Kada and achha) in Sikhism.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre) G.S. 1993 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.264

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which dynasty made Orchha the capital of Bundelkhand?
explanation: Located on the bank of river Betwa, Orchha is the city known for various historical monuments, established by Bundela rulers. The town Orchha was established by Rudrapratap Singh.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 1996 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.264

subject: AP & Indian History
question: What is Golkunda called at present?
explanation: Golconda is currently located in Hyderabad (Telengana). The Golconda kingdom was founded by Quli Qutb Shah after the partition of the empire. Aurangzeb merged it into the Mughal state in 1687 AD. The famous Kohinoor diamond was extracted from the Golconda mine.
source: MPPSC (Pre) GS, 1990 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.264

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who were Karori during Mughal period?
explanation: Karori was a revenue officer at Sarkar (District level) responsible for the collection of 1 Crore Dam (2,50,000 Rs., As 1 Rs. was equal to 40 Dam). Akbar had made this appointment in 1573 AD after Conquest of Gujarat.
source: UPPSC Food Safety Inspector Exam. 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.264

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Duties of Mir Bakhshi in Mughal administration was-
explanation: Mir Bakhshi during Mughal period was an official in charge of military affairs. He was the head of the Mansabdars and authorized for the recommendation in appointment of Mansabdars. He was also responsible for their payments.
source: UPPCS (Pre) Spl. G.S. 2004 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.264

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who among the following was the head of military in Mughal period?
source: UPPCS (Pre) G.S. 1992 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.264

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The term for the practice of awarding contracts for realization of land revenue was-
explanation: Izara system/revenue farming was introduced during the reign of Mughal Emperor Jahandar Shan (1712-1713). The collection of revenue was difficult for the small Jagirdars as they were living away from the land. Therefore they decided to give contract for the collection of land revenue. This system was known as ‘Izara’ System. Later big Jagirdars also followed the same system of revenue collection. It resulted in exploitation of peasants because Ijaredars used to collect more and more revenue to earn profit. It further resulted in decrease of state income and maximum exploitation of peasants as they were least interested in cultivation. It increased the poverty among the farmers and deteriorated the economic condition of Mughal empire.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 2009 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.264

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following is also known as Settlement system?
explanation: Jabti orth Dahsala system introduced by Todarmal during 24 year of Akbar’s reign in 1580 AD was also known as Bandobast(Settlement) system or Todarmal system. Under this system land revenue was determined on the basis of average real production of various cropsrd of the last ten years. The rate of land revenue was 1/3 of real production and crop.
source: Jharkhand PSC (Pre) G.S. Ist 2013 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.264

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following pairs of words and meaning is not correctly matched?
options: Khalisa : The villages in which revenue was deposited directly in state treasury
Inam : Land granted to scholars and religious persons
Jagir : State land granted to Mansabdars in lieu of their salary
explanation: Jagir during Mughal period stands for the land granted to Mansabdars in lieu of cash for the services rendered by them. Inam was the land granted to religious persons, scholars, and the persons of repute. Khalisa during Mughal period was the state land in which revenue was directly deposited in Royal Treasury. Mawda, Mauja or Deeh were such small villages in which land was under Paragana.
source: UPSC CAPF Exam. Ist 2017 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.264

subject: AP & Indian History
question: The main seat (Peeth) of Varkari sect is situated at____.
explanation: The Vaishnava poet-saints of Maharashtra Such as Jnaneshwar, Namdev, Eknath and Tukaram were devotees of lord Vitthala. Devotion oround Lord Vitthala (a form of Vishnu) gave rise to the Varkari sect which lay emphasis on an annual pilgrimage to pandharpur. Thus pandharpur was the principle seat.
source: RAS/RTS (Pre)-2018 · Ancient & Medieval History GS p.264
